title: Head of Quality
description:
Our Company

Whisper Aero is pioneering a more compelling and connected future by delivering cleaner, quieter, and more efficient propulsion solutions. Today's open rotor propulsion systems are challenged by safety, noise, and performance limitations at all scales. Whisper's breakthrough technologies allow aircraft to fly anywhere at any time without disturbing communities, at greater speeds, and with incredible improvements in efficiency and cost. Their innovations also enable a new generation of air moving products that can blend into the soundscapes of daily life. Whisper was founded by industry veterans, Mark Moore and Ian Villa, and continues to innovate a future that’s as considerate as it is compelling with its world-class team in Tennessee.

About the Role

We are seeking a hands-on Head of Quality to build and lead Whisper Aero’s enterprise quality organization as we scale from rapid product development and prototype builds into certified, repeatable production. This executive leader will own the company-wide quality strategy, Quality Management System (QMS), product and manufacturing quality, supplier quality, customer quality, and regulatory compliance. The role will partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Operations, Programs, and Finance to embed quality from concept through sustainment, develop a high-performing team, and ensure that safety, reliability, speed, and cost are managed as an integrated operating system.

What You’ll Do

  • Set and execute the enterprise quality vision, operating model, multi-year roadmap, and resource plan in alignment with company and product objectives.
  • Serve as the senior quality authority and management representative for customers, regulators, certification bodies, and executive leadership.
  • Lead, coach, and scale a multidisciplinary organization spanning product, manufacturing, supplier, systems, inspection, and customer quality.
  • Establish clear decision rights, escalation mechanisms, and quality gates across development, NPI, production, delivery, and field support.
  • Own the company quality management review, enterprise risk portfolio, and executive reporting cadence.

Enterprise Quality Leadership & Quality Management System

  • Mature and scale the existing AS9100-certified QMS from prototype-focused processes to rate production, aligned with customer requirements and 14 CFR Part 21 quality system requirements.
  • Own quality policy, objectives, management review, internal and external audits, document and records control, corrective action, configuration assurance, and organizational learning.
  • Translate quality data into business decisions through leading and lagging indicators, including first-pass yield, defect and escape rates, cost of poor quality, supplier performance, CAPA effectiveness, and process capability.

Product, Manufacturing & Operational Quality

  • Embed quality planning in product architecture and design reviews through requirements flow-down, DFMEA, verification and validation, configuration control, and design-for-manufacturability.
  • Lead quality execution from prototype and NPI through production readiness, rate ramp, customer delivery, and sustainment.
  • Establish APQP-based mechanisms including process flows, PFMEAs, control plans, Measurement Systems Analysis (MSA), SPC, process qualification and validation, inspection and test strategies, FAI/PPAP, and acceptance criteria.
  • Own MRB governance, containment, root-cause and corrective action, deviation and nonconformance control, and recurrence prevention without compromising safety or compliance.
  • Partner with Operations to improve yield, reliability, traceability, automation, and process capability while scaling production responsibly.

Supplier & Customer Quality

  • Establish supplier quality strategy, requirements, selection criteria, qualification, surveillance, development, and performance management across the supply base.
  • Lead supplier audits, source and receiving inspection strategy, FAI/PPAP, process capability reviews, SCARs, and recovery plans for critical suppliers.
  • Represent Quality in customer reviews, contract and requirement flow-down, acceptance, investigations, corrective actions, and delivery readiness.
  • Create closed-loop mechanisms that translate supplier, factory, test, and field signals into preventive action and product improvement.

Regulatory, Certification & Risk Governance

  • Own readiness for AS9100D certification and compliance with applicable FAA, customer, contractual, and export-controlled aerospace and defense requirements.
  • Lead quality engagement with the FAA, customers, registrars, and third-party auditors, including findings, corrective actions, and sustained effectiveness.
  • Establish enterprise product and process risk governance, independent escalation, stop-work authority, and transparent executive communication for significant quality or safety issues.
  • Ensure effective supplier control, configuration and document control, records management, calibration, traceability, nonconformance handling, and production acceptance.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline.
  • 12+ years of progressive quality, manufacturing, product, or supplier quality experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, automotive, medical device, or another complex regulated hardware environment.
  • 5+ years leading managers and multidisciplinary quality teams, including organizational design, hiring, coaching, budgeting, and resource planning.
  • Demonstrated ownership of an AS9100D- or ISO 9001-based QMS and successful leadership of certification, customer, or regulatory audits.
  • Proven experience scaling hardware from development and NPI through stable production, using APQP, FMEA, control plans, MSA, SPC, PPAP/FAI, RCCA/CAPA, and MRB.
  • Executive-level communication, sound risk judgment, and a record of influencing Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Programs, and senior leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with FAA production approval and 14 CFR Part 21 quality system requirements.
  • Experience building a quality organization and digital QMS in a fast-growing, vertically integrated technology or aerospace startup.
  • Experience with high-rate or automated production of complex electromechanical, propulsion, aerospace, or safety-critical products.
  • ASQ CQE, CMQ/OE, CSQP, AS9100 Lead Auditor, or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification.
  • Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, or Business Administration.
  • Strong command of ERP, PLM, MES, eQMS, business intelligence, and statistical analysis tools.

Benefits:

  • Top-tier Benefits: Employee-first focused comprehensive benefits package, minimum of 90% employer-paid plans for employees and dependents with optional HSA/FSA account offerings
  • PTO & Federal Holidays: Starting at four weeks of paid time off for vacation, sick, and personal days
  • Competitive Salary: Value-based compensation, plus enjoy Tennessee’s no-income-tax life
  • End of Year Bonuses: For eligible employees

title: Real Estate Photographer - Yakima, WA
description:
Role Mission

Are you a visual storyteller with an eye for detail and a knack for seamless execution?

Ziprent (a subsidiary of TurboTenant) is looking for a independent contractor (1099) Real Estate Photographer & Field Operations Specialist to be our eyes and ears on the ground. This isn’t just about snapping a few photos; it’s about crafting the digital first impression for our rental properties and ensuring every home is "rent-ready" through meticulous property walkthroughs and technical setups.

In this role, you’ll serve as a vital link in our growth engine, transforming empty spaces into high-performing listings. You’ll work independently to manage everything from 3D tours and high-fidelity photography to smart lockbox installations and condition reporting. If you love the freedom of the road and have a "tech-forward" approach, we want to talk to you.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Visual Storytelling: Deliver 15–25+ professionally edited, high-quality interior and exterior photos that make our listings pop.

  • Property Stewardship: Perform initial property walkthroughs and submit comprehensive condition reports to ensure our high standards are met.
  • Operational Logistics: Take the lead on key management, including the pick-up, installation, and battery maintenance of smart lockboxes.
  • High-Velocity Response: Maintain a "Be Better" mindset by responding promptly to new assignments and ensuring a 24-hour turnaround on all reports and deliverables.
  • Territory Mastery: Serving our local community and surrounding region, with a willingness to travel a 35–50+ mile radius to support our expanding market.

Qualifications:

  • Proven Experience: A strong real estate photography portfolio showcasing your ability to capture spaces effectively.
  • Tech-Savvy Toolkit: Professional gear including a high-quality wide-angle lens and a 360° camera compatible with Zillow.
  • Editing Expertise: Advanced photo editing skills to ensure every shot is polished and professional.
  • Mobile Proficiency: An updated mobile device capable of capturing clear, detailed images for on-site walkthrough reports.
  • Collaborative Spirit: Excellent written communication skills and a professional demeanor when representing the Ziprent/TurboTenant brand.
  • Reliability: A valid driver’s license, a reliable vehicle, and a flexible schedule to handle multiple shoots per month.
  • Location: You must live within 35 miles of the market area to be considered for this role.

Bonus SuperPowers:

  • Compliance Knowledge: Familiarity with FHA and housing compliance (smoke alarms, CO detectors, etc.).
  • Efficient Workflow: You stay ahead of the curve by leveraging modern tools and smart processes to streamline documentation, reporting, and day-to-day tasks—maximizing productivity without sacrificing quality.

  • AI-Native Workflow: You use modern tools to streamline your editing or reporting process for maximum efficiency.

Our "Be Better" Culture:

At TurboTenant, we live by the Be Better mantra. Our high-performance culture makes us relentless in our efforts to Be Better at serving our landlords and renters, and in unlocking the potential in one another.

What does our Be Better culture mean to you?

  1. You’ll be in an environment that pushes you to reach your potential.

  3. You’ll be on the highest performing team of your career.

About Us:

At TurboTenant, we simplify the complex and intimidating process of managing your own rental property. And we do it through an elegant software platform for small, “do-it-yourself” landlords and their tenants. But don’t take our word for it. Read reviews from some of our 1 million landlords.

Number of job requests varies by market region. This is a contracted 1099 position, and requests are sent out on an as-needed basis. Most markets average 3 –10+ jobs per month.

Candidates should be flexible and comfortable with limited assignments initially while the market and workload grow.

The role requires completion of a background check and signing of an independent contractor agreement.

Compensation

    • $225–$325+ per listing appointment (varies based on property size and scope)
      • Includes: professionally edited photos, Zillow 3D tour, floor plan, initial walkthrough report, and lockbox installation with key management
    • $50/hour for additional as-needed tasks

    • Travel Compensation:

$1—$100,000 USD

TurboTenant is proud to serve a diverse group of landlords and renters. We strive to reflect that diversity within our team. Role and Scope of Position:

Lead Engineer is responsible for the development, expansion, planning, design, maintenance and operation of the system and its equipment to meet the mission and objectives of the organization. This position shares accountability with peers in the strategy, development, and design of the organization’s Life Cycle Plan, a comprehensive long-term plan for the transmission/distribution system. Responsible for supervising, assigning, prioritizing and directing the work performed by other Engineers and staff.

Lead Engineer is responsible for the development, maintenance, planning, and design of the overhead and underground transmission systems to meet the set mission and objectives of the organization. In addition, this position coordinates inspection of assets under urgent conditions. Responsible for ensuring that the Eversource transmission and distribution systems are inspected and reported on to high quality standards that provide customers with safe, and reliable electric service. This position shares accountability with peers in the strategy, development, and design of the organization’s Life Cycle Plan, a comprehensive long-term plan for the organization. This is a leadership role, so the Lead Engineer is also responsible for supervising, assigning, prioritizing, educating, and directing the work performed by other Engineers and staff. The Lead Engineer provides technical expertise in Civil Engineering and helps to incorporate innovation across the group.

Experiences: Minimum of eight (8) years is required, with at least five (5) of those being in the technical, operational, or engineering aspects of the electrical utility industry. Work includes calculating, comparing, technical writing, editing, planning, evaluating, interpreting, organizing, consulting, analyzing, designing, documenting, specifying, coordinating, implementing and presenting. Job Summary and Responsibilities

Under immediate supervision of Construction and Maintenance Foreman, performs equipment operation and physical labor tasks required in general gas distribution construction/maintenance work. Performs miscellaneous duties including painting meters and regulators, cutting and cleaning brush/weeds from around work areas, assist Foreman and other crews with related duties as assigned. Ability to understand and carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form. Perform other duties as assigned by Supervisor.

• This position may provide services to affiliates of the Company subject to the UNS Energy Code of Conduct and the related Policies and Procedures.

Job Requirements

• Uses pick, shovel and digging bar in the process of gas main and service line installation and maintenance.

• Operates excavation equipment relating to construction and maintenance of gas distribution system.

• Locates and repairs leaks on gas distribution system.

• Must regularly load and unload materials and equipment to and from crew truck.

• Maintains truck inventory so that materials are on hand for construction and maintenance activities.

• Paints meter sets, regulator stations, city gates, etc. as needed.

• Operates jackhammer and compactor on a regular basis.

• Maintains equipment and machinery (greasing, oil and filter changes, light bulbs, general cleaning, etc.)

• Assists in leak investigations/pinpointing leaks using probe bar and Combustible Gas Indicator.

• Locates mains and services using a Metro-Tech pipe locator or similar equipment.

• Performs various C & M tasks such as priming and wrapping of steel pipe, installation of tracer wire on non-steel systems (P.E., PVC, etc.)

• Operate company vehicle as required.

• All work will be done according to company safety standards.

• At times must work in a blowing gas environment using SCBA equipment.

Movement to a C& M Crewman II position would only occur after proven tested knowledge of company procedures including but not limited to gas pipeline construction issues, and having all required qualifications of a C&M Crewman I. Employee must be proficient at operating all related company construction department equipment.

Movement to the C & M Crewman III position would only occur after proven tested ability to pass Title 49 CFR Part 192 Appendix-C Stick Arc- < 2” Butt/ All Fillet weld qualification, and having all required qualifications of a C & M Crewman II (i.e. PE Fitters Card, Class A CDL, O & M Training, task training, etc.) Employee must be a proficient operator of all related company construction department equipment.

Movement to the C & M Crewman IV position would only occur after proven tested ability to pass API 1104 Stick Arc- 12” Multiple weld qualification, and having all required qualifications of a C & M Crewman III (i.e. App.-C, Stick Arc- < 2” Butt/ All Fillet weld qualification, PE Fitters Card, Class A CDL, O & M Training, task training, etc.) Employee must be a proficient operator of all related company construction department equipment.

Additional Requirements

High school diploma or equivalent. Must possess a valid AZ Drivers license. Must obtain a CDL within 6 months of employment. Ability to lift a minimum of 95 pounds. Must be able to endure strenuous work in all types of weather conditions. This job requires some after hours and weekend call-out duties. The incumbent may be required to perform an operational, maintenance and/or emergency function. Such function may be in a safety sensitive role during the course of the calendar year and might include receiving and acting upon product release calls.

title: Vice President of Development
description:
DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT
BASE WAGE $82,891.75-$95,325.51

JOB TYPE Full-Time

DESCRIPTION

The Director of Development is responsible for developing and implementing SAL Community Services’ fundraising initiatives, identifying and writing grants, and communicating with and soliciting current and prospective donors. A member of the Administrative Team, the Director of Development works closely with the Chief Executive Officer and the Board of Directors to strengthen and expand giving programs.

We are passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable working and learning environment for all children, families, staff, and our communities. We believe every member on our team enriches our diversity by exposing us to a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the world, identify challenges, and to discover, design and deliver solutions

As SAL Community Services' Director of Development, you will have the opportunity for work including:

Fund Development
  • Prepare and execute annual fundraising plan, with specific short- and long-range funding objectives and giving strategies to achieve organizational goals.
  • Cultivate donors through consistent communication, regular meetings, and engagement opportunities.
  • Identify, write and submit grant proposals for funds from private foundations, corporations, and government agencies; maintains comprehensive schedule of grant opportunities, deadlines, follow-up activities, and reporting requirements for grants received.
  • Aggressively seek, research, and develop new and effective fundraising campaigns/sources both public and private, including major giving, annual giving, endowment and other donor-funded opportunities.
  • Coordinate and plan capital campaigns, the Little Bogey’s Golf Classic, Birdies for Charity, United Way Campaign, and other fundraising events.
  • Provide stewardship for donors by supplying thank you notes and tax receipts for all gifts.
  • Strategize and implement fundraising campaigns for special projects, as needed.
Communications
  • Develop and execute communication plans in alignment with organizational needs including:
    • Social media brand, presence, and responsiveness.
    • Marketing of SAL Community Services on both an organizational and programmatic level.
    • Crisis communication with both internal and external stakeholders.
  • Provide accurate and timely reports and/or presentations to internal and external stakeholders regarding the use, source, percent to goal, and management of donated dollars.
Community Partnerships
  • Maintain high level of knowledge of the community in order to develop favorable, compelling relationships with current, past, and/or potential donors
  • Represent SAL Community Services to highest degree of reverence at all times to various stakeholders in the community, internally, and at external public events.
Supervisory Responsibilities
  • Responsible for overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of Development team staff.
  • Ensure the responsibilities, authorities, and accountabilities of all subordinates in accordance with organization and grantor policies and applicable federal and state laws.
  • Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, onboarding, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.
We are looking for an administrative team member who:
  • Provides compassionate leadership and accountability across teams for high quality programming.
  • Is passionate about building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive environment for all.
  • Is innovative, strategic, and dedicated to contributing their skills and energy to a dynamic and growing mission-focused agency.

Salary, benefits and perks
Our entire compensation package includes paid time off and paid holidays; health, dental, and vision benefits; 401(k) with employer contribution; and pet insurance. A full list of benefits is available on our website.

Qualifications
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. A full list of job responsibilities will be provided prior to an interview. This position must obtain required background clearances. Requests for reasonable accommodation as required under applicable law will be considered.

Education and Experience
Required: Bachelor’s Degree from a four-year accredited college or university in Public Relations, Communication, Marketing, or applicable related field and a minimum of two years’ experience in a fundraising environment with proven ability to obtain major gifts and/or grants. Preferred: Current CFRE Certification or Bachelor’s Degree with at least five years of experience in a leadership fundraising environment. In lieu of five years of experience, those with at least two years of experience working in a similar leadership role in a non-profit organization with federal and state grants will be deemed higher qualified.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION

Mission
SAL Community Services (SAL) strengthens children, families, and individuals to build and enhance thriving communities.

About Us
At SAL Community Services, we provide Support, Advocacy, and Learning in our communities—from childhood to adulthood. Our mission is to strengthen children, families, and individuals to build and enhance thriving communities. Founded in 1970, we have a history of listening to the needs of our community and responding. We have grown from an organization focused on providing quality child care to low-income working families to one that meets a wide variety of needs, from early care and education to crisis assistance and stabilization services. Today, SAL has a bi-state 17 county regional footprint from the Quad Cities to Central Illinois area. We advocate with and for the people we support, the communities we serve, and the solutions we champion, and we offer an inclusive, welcoming community for the people we serve—and our employees. Learn more on our website at

title: Semiconductor Packaging Process Engineering Lead
description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

Intel Corporation is a global leader in the semiconductor industry, engineering the foundational technologies that power modern computing. Within Intel, the Epoxy Mold Module division plays a pivotal role in developing and scaling world-class semiconductor packaging solutions. By advancing next-generation assembly processes and driving operational excellence, our group directly enables Intel’s product roadmap and delivers innovative, high-quality products to customers worldwide.

We are seeking a visionary and action-oriented Packaging Module Development Manager to lead our engineering team in Arizona. In this critical leadership role, you will guide a specialized team responsible for advancing semiconductor packaging processes and introducing new equipment within a 24x7 manufacturing environment. Your strategic oversight and mentorship will directly resolve complex technical challenges, elevate manufacturing yield and throughput, and shape the future of Intel's packaging capabilities.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Team Leadership & Mentorship: Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers across a 24x7 operation, cultivating technical expertise, clear goal alignment, and differentiated execution.
  • Process & Equipment Introduction: Guide the deployment, implementation, and optimization of new packaging equipment and process technologies into the manufacturing environment.
  • Specification Oversight: Direct equipment and process specifications to guarantee strict alignment with operational goals and manufacturing expectations.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Manage shift engineering coverage and build strong partnerships across manufacturing, automation, and partner engineering groups.

Established in 1980, GLFHC is a mission-driven, multi-site nonprofit healthcare organization employing more than 700 staff and serving communities throughout the Merrimack Valley. We provide comprehensive, patient-centered care and proudly sponsor the Lawrence Family Medicine Residency Program.

Job Description:

The Associate Director, Integrated Content leads the firm's content strategy and function, overseeing a team responsible for developing high-impact, differentiated content that builds awareness of the firm's thought leadership and expertise, strengthens its market position, and creates demand by opening doors to meaningful client conversations. Reporting into the Director of Marketing and partnering across Marketing, Brand, Communications, Business Development, and firm leadership, this role defines the firm's content vision, editorial strategy, and flagship thought leadership initiatives, ensuring content aligns with buyer needs, business objectives, and brand standards across channels.

This role combines strategic leadership with hands-on content development and execution, leading by example to shape compelling narratives, develop impactful thought leadership, and deliver editorial excellence. The Associate Director builds and coaches a high-performing content team, manages external agency and contractor resources, and leverages AI and emerging technologies to scale content development, improve efficiency, and maximize impact. Working closely with attorneys and internal stakeholders, this leader advances a modern, integrated, data-informed content function that drives awareness, engagement, and measurable business impact.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Develop and evolve the firm's integrated content and thought leadership strategy, aligning priorities with business objectives, market opportunities, buyer needs, and demand generation goals.
  • Identify and prioritize high-impact content opportunities that build awareness of the firm's expertise, strengthen market positioning, generate demand, and open doors to meaningful client conversations.
  • Serve as a senior advisor on editorial strategy and integrated content planning, partnering closely with Marketing to align content development with campaign strategies, audience needs, content format types and distribution plans, while collaborating with Brand, Communications, Business Development, and firm leadership to advance strategic priorities.
  • Lead and execute high-profile thought leadership initiatives, including flagship reports, articles, client case studies, and other strategic content (videos, podcasts, etc.), demonstrating exceptional editorial judgment, storytelling, and content development capabilities.
  • Translate complex legal, business, and market trends into compelling, differentiated content and narratives that resonate with clients and target audiences.
  • Identify and pursue strategic third-party content partnerships, sponsorships, and co-created thought leadership opportunities that amplify the firm's expertise, expand market reach, and engage priority audiences.
  • Establish editorial standards, best practices, and content development processes that ensure quality, consistency, efficiency, and alignment with the firm's brand and strategic priorities.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing content team, building capabilities, providing hands-on guidance, and fostering a culture of creativity, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Manage external agency and contractor resources, ensuring quality, effective resource allocation, and alignment with content priorities and business objectives.
  • Drive an insight-led approach to content strategy, leveraging performance analytics, audience behavior, and market intelligence to optimize content effectiveness, audience engagement, and business impact.
  • Champion innovation in content development, leveraging AI, emerging formats, and new storytelling approaches to scale production, increase efficiency, and extend the reach and impact of the firm's expertise.

Job Specifications:

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • 15+ years of experience in content strategy, thought leadership, editorial, communications, or marketing, preferably within a professional service or B2B environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute enterprise content strategies aligned with business objectives, audience needs, and demand generation goals.
  • Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills, with a proven ability to personally develop sophisticated, high-impact content across multiple formats and audiences.
  • Strong executive presence and consultative skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders, challenge thinking, and shape compelling narratives.
  • Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives and collaborating effectively across Marketing, Communications, Business Development, and other functions.
  • Strong understanding of content marketing, audience strategy, and performance measurement, with the ability to translate insights into actionable content decisions.
  • Proven experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams, building capabilities, and managing external writers, agencies, and editorial resources.
  • Ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on execution, managing competing priorities while maintaining exceptional quality.
  • Demonstrated experience leveraging AI-enabled tools, emerging technologies, and evolving content practices to improve efficiency, scale production, and enhance content effectiveness.

Job Title:

Senior Fiscal Associate

Department:

Academic Affairs Administration | Budget and Resource Management

The Senior Fiscal Associate primarily supports procurement, travel, and procurement card (PCard) activities within the Office of Academic Affairs (OAA). This position reports to the Manager of Procurement, Receivables, and Customer Service and requires exceptional attention to detail, accuracy, and customer service.


As a member of the OAA Business Services team, the Senior Fiscal Associate provides guidance, training, and transactional support related to procurement and travel activities for OAA and its reporting units. The team is also responsible for processing deposits, managing the OAA Faculty Club account, and overseeing the reconciliation of procurement transactions associated with group travel.


The Senior Fiscal Associate ensures compliance with university policies, procedures, and financial guidelines while supporting quality assurance efforts and maintaining accurate records. This role implements established business processes and communicates procurement-related information to finance staff to support reconciliation, reporting, and operational efficiency.


This position also plays a key role in customer service and stakeholder engagement by building and maintaining positive relationships with faculty, staff, suppliers, and university partners. Responsibilities include providing timely and accurate guidance regarding procurement and travel processes, responding to inquiries, routing requests to appropriate resources, and developing targeted communications and training materials for stakeholders.


Job Duties

60% Procurement and Travel Transactions

  • Review and approve procurement-related workflow transactions in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Consult with faculty and staff to resolve errors, omissions, and compliance concerns related to procurement requests.
  • Assist units with the submission and processing of group travel transactions in Workday.
  • Ensure procurement and travel activities comply with university policies, procedures, and financial guidelines.
  • Provide quality assurance support for procurement and travel documentation and approvals.

25% Customer Service and Stakeholder Support

  • Deliver exceptional customer service related to procurement, travel, and PCard inquiries.
  • Respond to, triage, and route requests to the appropriate university partners and resources.
  • Escalate complex issues to the Procurement Lead or Manager as appropriate.
  • Provide guidance and support related to requisitions, purchase orders, spend authorizations, expense reports, miscellaneous payments, supplier invoice requests, procurement cards, and related financial transactions.
  • Develop and facilitate procurement and travel-related training sessions for stakeholders on a regular and as-needed basis.
  • Create and distribute communications, reminders, and updates related to procurement and travel processes.

10% Process Improvement and Team Support

  • Collaborate with the Manager of Procurement, Receivables, and Customer Service to identify and implement process improvements.
  • Support the development and documentation of best practices for procurement and travel operations.
  • Communicate process updates and procedural changes to OAA units and stakeholders.

5% Other Duties

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Required Education

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Additional certification, vocational training, or an associate degree in a related field may be considered favorably.

title: SHIPWRIGHT I_II  Full-time Project Position (Edna Lockwood Restoration) (71130)
description:
Would you like the opportunity to help preserve a unique piece of Chesapeake Bay maritime history?

The Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum (CBMM) is seeking a skilled Shipwright I or Shipwright II to join the restoration of Edna E. Lockwood, a National Historic Landmark and the last of the historic sailing log-bottom bugeyes. Built in 1889 by John B. Harrison of Tilghman Island, Edna is a treasured part of CBMM’s historic floating fleet and an extraordinary example of traditional Chesapeake Bay boatbuilding.

This is a rare opportunity to put your traditional wooden boatbuilding skills to work preserving an important piece of Chesapeake Bay maritime heritage for future generations.

This is a full-time, temporary project position expected to last approximately 12 to 14 months.

About the Position

CBMM’s Shipyard is a working exhibit of Chesapeake Bay wooden boatbuilding and restoration, open to the public seven days a week. Our shipwrights restore, build, and maintain traditional wooden vessels while sharing that work with museum guests, volunteers, and apprentices.

The successful candidate will work as part of CBMM’s Shipyard team on the restoration of Edna Lockwood. Depending on experience and qualifications, the selected candidate may be hired at the Shipwright I or Shipwright II level.

What You’ll Do

  • Perform traditional shipwright work, including producing templates and patterns, fitting internal and external components, preparing slipways, and constructing cradles.
  • Select and work with quality lumber appropriate for traditional wooden boat construction and restoration.
  • Fabricate vessel components, including keels, futtocks, planking, support structures, blocking, and staging.
  • Safely manipulate large timbers using machinery, block and tackle, and traditional methods.
  • Build and restore vessels according to plans and specifications.
  • Apply traditional preservatives and finishes.
  • Safely operate and maintain woodworking tools, machinery, and shop equipment.
  • Maintain a safe, clean, and organized work environment.
  • Work collaboratively with CBMM staff, volunteers, and apprentices.
  • Interact with museum guests and share the restoration process in CBMM’s public working Shipyard.

Learn More About Edna E. Lockwood

Discover the history of this remarkable vessel and the work ahead:

  • Edna E. Lockwood, Bugeye, 1889
  • Watch an overview of the upcoming work

Join us and put your craftsmanship to work preserving a one-of-a-kind piece of Chesapeake Bay maritime history.

Trase is the operating system for high-stakes environments, providing end-to-end solutions for deploying, managing, and optimizing AI within industries where security, governance, and data sovereignty are non-negotiable.

Trase’s suite of products includes Origin, its agentic operating system; Leagues, its marketplace for specialized, configurable, ready-to-deploy agents; and Arena, where developers build, evaluate, and package the agents that run on Origin. We’re in production at Duke Health, where our agents save over 5,490 hours of clinical labor annually in a single department. We’ve raised $10.5M from Red Cell Partners and top the Hugging Face GAIA Leaderboard for Generalized AI Assistants, ahead of Google, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI. Now we’re scaling.

Senior Product Manager, Origin: Enterprise AI Platform

Your job is to make it easy for customers to put agents into production, understand how they're operating, understand and accept risk, and maintain the controls and trust their business requires.

You’ll be the product manager for Trase Origin, our platform for deploying and governing AI agents. You’ll work with customers, sales and presales, GRC, and our federal team to gather requirements, then write the PRDs engineering builds from. You'll own strategy, discovery, priorities, delivery, and results.

  • Understand the customer: Work directly with administrators, platform teams, and governance stakeholders. Learn how they operate, where adoption gets stuck, and which problems matter enough to solve.

  • Make enterprise AI manageable: Own experiences that help customers administer agents, manage access and policies, and understand activity, usage, and cost across their organization.
  • Build trust into the product: Help customers evaluate risk, approve agents for production, and maintain visibility and accountability. Partner with GRC and our federal team to translate customer requirements into engineering deliverables to ship usable product capabilities.
  • Support production operations: Give operators the visibility and controls they need to monitor agents, understand problems, and keep them running reliably.
  • Drive product-led growth: Make installation, setup, and adoption straightforward across managed and customer-operated environments. Reduce the friction between evaluating the platform and putting it to work.
  • Own the results: Connect product decisions to adoption, customer value, and licensing revenue. Work with sales and product marketing to understand buying barriers and help customers succeed.

  • You've owned and shipped enterprise software used by administrators, platform teams, or security and governance stakeholders.
  • You can work through complex technical and organizational requirements and turn them into a clear, usable product.
  • You think like an entrepreneur. You find valuable problems, test your assumptions, and decide where to invest.
  • You assume you can change the outcome and act on it. You go find the customers, evidence, and collaborators you need without waiting for someone to hand you a plan.
  • You learn quickly, ask precise questions, and exercise sound judgment when the information is incomplete.
  • You ship. You make decisions, resolve obstacles, and stay accountable for whether the work improves the customer's experience.
  • You understand that enterprise controls and ease of adoption both matter, and you have experience making them work together.

  • Experience with identity, access management, governance, or compliance capabilities.
  • Experience serving regulated enterprises or government customers.
  • Experience with self-service enterprise software, cloud marketplaces, or multiple deployment models.

title: Warranty Coordinator
description:
The Warranty Coordinator oversees the post-construction closeout phase for commercial construction projects, managing the transition of commercial, industrial, or institutional assets from the operations team to the client. This role is responsible for administering the defects liability period (DLP), coordinating latent defect remediation, and managing contractual warranty claims with subcontractors and manufacturers. The objective is to minimize corporate risk, enforce trade partner accountability, and maintain client relationships for commercial construction projects

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Contract & Claims Administration

  • Warranty Tracking: Review prime contracts to define project-specific warranty obligations, durations and performance bonds.
  • Claim Assessment: Field complex post-occupancy requests from commercial facility managers; evaluate technical merit against construction documents, project specs, and industry standards.
  • Claim Intake & Assessment: Evaluate incoming client maintenance requests to determine if the defect falls under the contractor’s one-year general warranty, a specific trade partner agreement, or vendor equipment coverage.
  • Subcontractor Enforcement: Issue formal Notices to Cure and track warranty obligations, ensuring trade partners repair defects at their own expense rather than the General Contractor’s.
  • Subcontractor Coordination: Schedule, dispatch, and manage trade partners and field technicians to complete corrective repairs safely and efficiently.
  • Inspections & Walkthroughs: Lead systematic facility walkthroughs with clients (11-month post-occupancy inspections)

Technical Coordination & Closeout

  • Work Order Dispatching: Issue and track commercial work orders using enterprise construction platforms like Procore, Autodesk Build, or Service Channel.
  • Documentation Tracking: Update and maintain comprehensive warranty trackers, log substantial completion dates, track parts availability, and file vendor equipment claims.

description:
HB - VP of Construction


We are Lennar

Lennar is one of the nation's leading homebuilders, dedicated to making an impact and creating an extraordinary experience for their Homeowners, Communities, and Associates by building quality homes and providing exceptional customer service, giving back to the communities in which we work and live in, and fostering a culture of opportunity and growth for our Associates throughout their career. Lennar has been recognized as a Fortune 500® company and consistently ranked among the top homebuilders in the United States.


A Career that Empowers You to Build Your Future

As a Vice President of Construction within Lennar's Homebuilding division, you will serve as a senior professional and subject matter expert responsible for driving construction excellence across a defined market or multi-community portfolio. In this role, you will apply deep operational expertise and executive-level judgment to shape construction strategy, ensure quality outcomes, and uphold Lennar's commitment to delivering an exceptional homebuying experience. Your work directly influences the pace, cost efficiency, and quality of homes delivered to Lennar customers, making this a critical role in connecting divisional strategy to on-the-ground results.


Your Responsibilities on the Team

  • Lead the development and execution of construction strategies across a designated market or portfolio of communities, applying senior-level judgment to align field operations with division-wide production goals, schedule targets, and quality benchmarks established by Lennar's Homebuilding leadership.
  • Serve as the primary construction authority and escalation point for complex field challenges, including scope deviations, trade partner performance issues, permitting obstacles, and site conditions that require executive-level resolution to maintain project momentum and protect schedule integrity.
  • Conduct systematic field reviews and quality audits across active communities, evaluating construction stage completion, workmanship standards, and adherence to Lennar's build specifications and warranty requirements to ensure homes are delivered to the highest standard at every phase of the construction cycle.
  • Own the construction budget at the market or portfolio level by monitoring cost performance against approved proformas, identifying variances, analyzing root causes, and recommending corrective actions that preserve margin integrity without compromising quality or regulatory compliance.
  • Drive the pre-closing and closing orientation readiness process across communities by establishing clear quality thresholds and field accountability protocols that ensure each home is thoroughly punch-listed, inspected, and transitioned from production to homeowner service in a condition that reflects Lennar's quality promise.
  • Build and maintain strategic relationships with municipal agencies, inspection authorities, and permitting offices across the division's operating markets, proactively navigating regulatory requirements to secure approvals, resolve compliance issues, and mitigate schedule risk associated with government interfaces.
  • Analyze construction cycle time data, trade partner scheduling, and material delivery pipelines to identify systemic inefficiencies and implement process improvements that reduce build time, eliminate rework, and increase overall throughput across the community portfolio without sacrificing construction standards.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Land, Sales, Finance, and Customer Experience teams to provide expert construction input during pre-development planning, community launch preparation, and post-closing warranty resolution, ensuring that field realities are accurately represented in business decisions that affect project scope, timelines, and customer commitments.

Your Toolbox

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Architecture, or a related field required; advanced degree in Business, Engineering, or Construction-related discipline strongly preferred.
  • Minimum of 12 to 15 years of progressive experience in residential homebuilding construction, with demonstrated expertise operating at a senior or executive scope across multiple communities or markets simultaneously.
  • Advanced working knowledge of residential construction processes, phased build cycles, trade sequencing, and quality control standards applicable to high-volume production homebuilding environments.
  • Proven ability to read, interpret, and evaluate construction blueprints, architectural plans, engineering documents, and municipal permit packages with the precision required to make consequential field and design decisions independently.
  • Deep familiarity with local and regional building codes, zoning regulations, inspection protocols, and permitting processes across multiple jurisdictions, with the ability to navigate complex regulatory environments as a credible representative of the organization.
  • Strong analytical and financial acumen, including the ability to manage and evaluate construction budgets, interpret cost reports, assess variance drivers, and develop data-supported recommendations that influence executive-level resource and scheduling decisions.
  • Exceptional professional judgment and decision-making capability, with a track record of resolving high-stakes construction challenges independently, balancing urgency with thoroughness, and escalating appropriately when divisional risk is involved.
  • Proficiency with construction management platforms, project scheduling tools, and productivity software commonly used in large-scale residential homebuilding operations, with the ability to leverage technology to monitor performance and communicate progress across a geographically distributed portfolio.

Physical & Office/Site Presence Requirements

This is primarily a sedentary office position which requires the incumbent to have the ability to operate computer equipment, speak, hear, bend, stoop, reach, lift, and move and carry up to 25 lbs. Finger dexterity is necessary.

title: Manager, Government Affairs
location: United States - District of Columbia - Washington
description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

At Gilead our pursuit of a healthier world for all people has yielded a cure for hepatitis C, revolutionary improvements in HIV treatment and prevention as well as advancements in therapies for viral and inflammatory diseases and certain cancers.


We set and achieve bold ambitions in our fight against the world’s most devastating diseases, united in our commitment to confronting the largest public health challenges of our day and improving the lives of patients for generations to come.


As Manager, Government Affairs, you will be an integral part of a fast-paced, highly collaborative Federal Government Affairs (FGA) team, partnering with Government Affairs & Policy and cross-functional colleagues to devise, execute, and track strategic plans and substantive projects across the enterprise.


Reporting to the Vice President, Federal Government Affairs, you will play a central role in developing and implementing coordinated strategies, initiatives, and engagements around issues that impact Gilead/Kite and our patients. The ideal candidate is a motivated and detail-oriented self-starter who writes clearly and tracks work rigorously to completion.


Key Responsibilities:

· Partner with the Federal Government Affairs team and Government Affairs leadership to devise, execute and track operating plans, ensuring those plans are aligned to broader company priorities.

· Serve as project manager for substantive GA and enterprise projects of increasing complexity: define scope, develop and maintain comprehensive project plans, including timelines, milestones, owners, deliverables, and resource requirements, and drive projects to on-time, high-quality completion.

· Coordinate project activities across functions, ensuring alignment with overall project goals and objectives; run timely, efficient, and action-oriented project meetings and track decisions, action items, and deliverables.

· Build and maintain structured systems, documents, trackers, dashboards, and repeatable processes for GA priorities, legislative and regulatory developments, stakeholder engagements, and enterprise initiatives.

· Draft, edit, and quality-check high-quality written products, including strategic plans, briefing memos, presentations, position summaries, and leadership updates.

· Monitor federal legislation, regulations, programs, and executive branch actions impacting Gilead/Kite; over time, you will become adept at flagging implications for GA priorities.

· Develop and maintain a high-impact GA communications platforms to deliver timely updates informing internal stakeholders regarding key government actions impacting Gilead.

· Support preparation of materials for leadership and governance reviews, Congressional engagements, and trade association workgroups; staff workgroups as needed, reflect Gilead’s perspective in those discussions, and share outputs with the GA team and partners as appropriate.

· Coordinate with cross-functional internal partners, including Legal, Commercial, Research, Development and Public Affairs, to identify opportunities to advance Gilead’s legislative and regulatory priorities and to ensure an aligned policy perspective.

· Support GA operations, including the annual planning cycle, budget tracking, coordination of external consultants.

· Identify opportunities for process improvement and optimization, including via leveraging AI, and drive adoption of best practices across the team.

· Manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, exercising sound judgment and discretion with confidential information.

  • 6+ Years with BS/BA
    OR

Preferred Qualifications:

· Strong project management capabilities with a proven ability to prioritize and execute across multiple workstreams, and a track record of managing complex projects and meeting challenging deadlines.

· Excellent written communication skills, with demonstrated ability to synthesize complex policy and business material into clear and accurate products for senior audiences.

· A resourceful self-starter with problem-solving and critical thinking skills; self-motivated with a strong sense of ownership.

· Attention to detail, organized and thorough, with strong organizational and time management skills.

· Excellent collaboration, interpersonal, and communication skills, with demonstrated success working in fast-paced, dynamic environments and influencing stakeholders without direct authority.

Position Summary:
The Operating Room (OR) Manager is responsible for the daily operations of the surgical services department in the Ambulatory Surgery Center (ASC). This role ensures safe, efficient, and high-quality perioperative care by overseeing clinical staff, managing operating room workflow, coordinating with physicians and anesthesia providers, and maintaining compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards. The OR Manager acts as a clinical leader, resource, and mentor to the perioperative nursing team.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
• Supervise, support, and evaluate OR staff, including RNs, surgical technologists, and support personnel.
• Manage day-to-day operations of the operating rooms, ensuring efficiency, patient safety, and adherence to surgical schedules.
• Collaborate with surgeons, anesthesia providers, and nursing leadership to ensure seamless patient flow.
• Develop and maintain OR staffing schedules to meet clinical and operational needs.
• Oversee surgical case preparation, instrument/equipment readiness, and supply management.
• Ensure compliance with all infection control, safety, and sterile processing standards.
• Participate in hiring, orientation, training, and professional development of surgical services staff.
• Lead and monitor Quality Improvement (QI) and Performance Improvement (PI) activities for surgical services.
• Assist in budget management, including supply cost containment and resource utilization.
• Maintain compliance with AAAHC, Joint Commission, CMS, OSHA, and state specific requirements.
• Serve as a resource and clinical expert to staff, patients, and families regarding perioperative care.
• Ensure readiness for all regulatory inspections and accreditation surveys.
Qualifications:
Education:
• Graduate of an accredited school of nursing; BSN and or Master’s degree preferred.
Licensure:
• Current, unrestricted Registered Nurse (RN) license in the state of practice required.
Experience:
• Minimum of 3–5 years of perioperative nursing experience, including circulating and/or scrub experience.
• At least 2 years of leadership or charge nurse experience in an OR setting required.
Certification:
• Current BLS required.
• Current ACLS required. If not held at hire, must be obtained within three (3) months of start date.
• PALS may be required based on the patient population.
• CNOR certification preferred.
Skills:
• Strong knowledge of surgical procedures, aseptic technique, and regulatory requirements in ambulatory surgery.
• Demonstrated leadership, organizational, and decision-making skills.
• Excellent communication, team-building, and problem-solving abilities.
Physical/Mental Requirements:
• Ability to work in a fast-paced surgical environment.
• Ability to stand for prolonged periods and assist with patient transfers.
• Strong critical thinking, prioritization, and stress management skills.
• Ability to lift up to 25 pounds and assist in patient positioning or transfers when necessary.

title: Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations
description:
Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations

Own the supply chain and CMC project engine behind Nurix’s clinical programs and commercial readiness. In this multifaceted role, you will select and manage CMOs, keep clinical supply flowing to trial sites around the world, and drive cross-functional CMC plans from early development toward commercialization, in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities.

Position Description

The position is a multifaceted role supporting several areas within the Technical Operations group, including supply chain management, CMC project management, and clinical labeling and distribution. The ideal candidate will be highly motivated and self-directed, with experience and interest in working in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities and opportunities.

The Opportunity

  • Lead the effort to identify, select, and manage Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) for the development and cGMP manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and DS in support of ongoing clinical programs and commercial products (with finance and commercial teams)
  • Manage global supply chains and logistics in support of demand for clinical studies and commercial products
  • Working in conjunction with technical teams, provide vendor management support in all logistics and operations to ensure on-time delivery of materials
  • Coordinate the design and execution of cross-functional CMC project plans and budgeting for early clinical development through commercial readiness
  • Maintain frequent communication with cross-functional CMC project team members and key internal stakeholders so that all parties are aware of current project status, issues, contingencies, milestones, and budgets
  • Proactively identify the CMC critical path, risks, and impediments to successful development, and drive the identification and development of solutions to mitigate these risks
  • Serve as primary clinical supply chain contact, working collaboratively with internal and external partners
  • Manage clinical supply planning and forecasting for study protocols and develop packaging/labeling and global distribution strategies
  • Monitor IXRS portal processes, including high and low enrolling site settings, drug acknowledgement, depot and site supply levels, and IMP status of released lots or expired drug
  • Coordinate the preparation and/or review of CMC sections of INDs, CTAs, NDAs, MAAs, and other regulatory submissions to ensure timely distribution of clinical trial materials
  • Coordinate the process validation programs to support commercialization
  • Initiate and manage high-value intercontinental, cross-border, and domestic shipments
  • Coordinate the preparation, review, editing, and approval of cGMP batch records and CMC regulatory and Quality documents
  • Coordinate the preparation of technical reports, publications, and oral presentations

What You’ll Bring

  • BS with 15+ years’ experience; degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
  • At least 10 years of relevant experience in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology CMC/cGMP environment
  • Excellent project management skills and the ability to work cross-functionally to develop and execute project plans
  • Experience managing US and international CRO/CMOs for the manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and cGMP DS and DP for programs in development
  • Experience with clinical supply chain, including forecasting supply needs
  • Experience with cGMP manufacturing and IND, CTA, and NDA filings; thorough knowledge of relevant FDA and EMEA regulations
  • Experience in supply chain management, and experience establishing pharmaceutical supply chain systems and networks
  • Able to identify and resolve critical issues
  • Sufficient technical background and experience to work closely with other technical functional areas
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and exceptional interpersonal and management skills to collaborate with others on assigned projects (including both internal teams and external collaborators)
  • Bonus: Advanced degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
  • Bonus: Experience managing US and international CMOs for commercial programs

Salary Range: $270,300 - $295,700

The posted range applies to roles based in the San Francisco Bay Area and reflects local market conditions. Where an offer lands within that range depends on the candidate’s relevant experience, technical expertise, and how their background aligns with the role’s requirements.

Location: Onsite – Brisbane, CA

Fit with Nurix Culture and Values

  • Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
  • Solutions and results-oriented focus
  • Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

About Nurix Therapeutics

Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix’s dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. Nurix aims to establish degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care, writing medicine’s next chapter with a new script to outmatch disease.

Our Team:


We have an exciting leadership opportunity to join our amazing Energy Efficiency Commercial & Industrial (C&I) Team in Manchester NH.


The Supervisor is responsible for supervising a team of Energy Efficiency Consultants responsible for engagement with customers, contractors and engineers pursuing energy efficiency projects throughout New Hampshire.


The Supervisor is responsible for effective execution of C&I strategy and managing the energy efficiency portfolio for associated team to achieve goals. Responsible for engagement with internal stakeholders including sales, engineering, evaluation teams as well as initiatives and technical solutions. Regularly interacts with customers, regulators, other supervisors in Massachusetts and Connecticut and/or other stakeholders.


Our overall mission is to provide assistance and support to internal and external subject matter experts. The technical assistance & support efforts are designed to reduce the overall natural gas & electricity consumption by replacing or substituting end use devices or systems with technically more advanced equipment without affecting service to the customer.


Recommendations include adoption of high-efficiency equipment including lighting, heating, ventilating and air conditioning (HVAC) systems or control modifications, efficient building design, advanced electric motor drives, heat recovery systems, and manufacturing processes.


Essential Functions:

· Directs supervision of department staff, including personnel professional development, performance assessments, recruitment and preparation of reporting procedures for program implementation activities (e.g. production summary, target attainment, etc.)

· Oversee the budgeting, invoicing and tracking of expenses and energy savings, as well as the development of RFP's for contracted services.

· Oversee the integration of strategic activities between the customer, program administrators, advisory consultants and vendor/contractors to yield customer-centric programs and services. Leads initiatives that research, identify, develop and implement new value-added products and services for all customer classes.

· Develop relationships with key customers, stakeholders, and contractors that participate in assigned energy efficiency programs.

· Leads process improvement initiatives within area of responsibility and engage stakeholders to ensure all resultant improvements are delivered on time, on budget and within scope approved by management.

· Executes on department plans to ensure compliance with regulatory filings and oversight of rate-payer funds for Energy Efficiency programs.

· Leads the development of draft testimony and testifies in front of regulatory and legislative bodies as assigned.

· Represents Eversource in national energy efficiency conferences and/or stake holder events (e.g. ACEEE, ASHRAE, ACI, and CEE).

(Technical Knowledge/Skill/Education/Licenses/Certifications)

Technical Knowledge/Skill:

Job Details:

Purpose

Experienced Senior Linux Administrator to support and evolve a Linux infrastructure in a compliance-driven environment for the Advanced Technology Laboratory (ATL).


Responsibilities


  • Under general direction, perform Linux computer systems installation, configuration, administration, maintenance, troubleshooting, and end-user support for software’s, servers, workstations, laptops, and virtual machines. This is a hands-on role with a clear near-term mission: modernize and standardize the existing infrastructure — rebuilding systems onto a lean, consistent, well-governed baseline. This role operates with a high degree of autonomy — and will be expected to own infrastructure initiatives end-to-end, from planning through execution, with minimal daily supervision.
  • Ensure Linux systems integrate properly with SAN/NAS storage and backup infrastructure; partner with the storage administration team on backup services, recovery operations, troubleshooting, and escalation.
  • Support infrastructure modernization efforts, including assessing, rebuilding, and redesigning existing Linux systems; standardization; and creation of golden images with automated provisioning pipelines (e.g., PXE/Kickstart).
  • Administer configuration management tooling (Salt/Ansible) to enforce consistent, auditable configurations across the environment.
  • Establish and maintain repository infrastructure for software distribution and patching — leveraging the central IT mirror and standing up a local mirror to meet lab-specific business needs — including point-release control to standardize patch levels across the environment; manage content synchronization, availability, and access controls.
  • Perform and maintain Linux, backup and storage systems audits for compliance with established information assurance policies and configuration guidelines.
  • Document and maintain processes, procedures and configurations for Linux, storage and backup solution configuration and change management.
  • Maintain computer hardware/software inventories and documentation.
  • Other related functions as assigned.



Required Qualifications


  • Bachelor's degree in computer science or other related field.
  • Five years of experience administering Linux systems in an enterprise storage and backup environment, including integration with SAN/NAS infrastructure (multipathing, LVM, filesystems, NFS server/client configuration) and backup/restore operations from the Linux side
  • Experience with commonly used concepts, practices, and procedures used in maintaining backup and storage infrastructure
  • Experience with FC, iSCSI, or other network storage protocols
  • Experience with commonly used concepts, practices, procedures, and tools used in maintaining a Linux enterprise infrastructure, with strong hands-on expertise in Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 8/9
  • Demonstrated track record of designing and executing Linux infrastructure improvements, from assessment through implementation — not limited to daily operations.
  • Experience with shell scripting: Perl, Python, Bash, or similar
  • Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.


Preferred Qualifications


  • At least seven years of experience in Linux system administration.
  • Current DoD 8570.1/8140 IAT II or greater certification (CySA+, Security+, GICSP, GSEC, or similar approved IA certifications)
  • Experience administering Ubuntu systems in addition to RHEL
  • Experience creating and maintaining golden images / standardized server templates (RHEL golden images, VMware templates) and automated provisioning (Kickstart, PXE, cloud-init)
  • Experience with infrastructure architecture — building, rebuilding, or redesigning existing Linux infrastructure
  • Experience administering VMware vSphere environments hosting Linux VMs
  • Experience with system configuration management tools such as Salt, Ansible, Kickstart, Cobbler, RHN Satellite, or Puppet
  • Experience establishing and maintaining repository/mirror infrastructure (e.g., RHEL/Alma local mirrors, Satellite, Artifactory), including point-release/patch-level control
  • Experience with orchestration software such as Kubernetes, Docker, or Podman
  • Experience with source code management tools such as Subversion or Git
  • Experience with web and database hosting environments such as Apache, nginx, MySQL/MariaDB, or PostgreSQL
  • Experience supporting compute-heavy workloads on physical (bare-metal) servers
  • Experience with infrastructure migrations (e.g., NAS-to-array data migrations, storage consolidation)
  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST 800-171, CMMC, STIGs) in controlled environments
  • Relevant certifications (RHCE or equivalent) a plus

General Notes

An agency designated by the federal government handles the investigation as to the requirement for eligibility for access to classified information. Factors considered during this investigation include but are not limited to allegiance to the United States, foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations, drug involvement, the likelihood of continuation of such conduct, etc.

title: Manager Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs
description:
POSITION SUMMARY: The Manager, Regulatory Affairs and Quality Assurance (Biologics) drives complex FDA regulatory submissions for biologic programs, from Phase 1 through marketing applications (BLA/NDA). At Natera, we move fast because there is a patient waiting for every test and treatment. In this role, you will build and own quality systems, translate executive strategy into compliant submissions, and provide regulatory guidance to ensure rapid product approvals. You will coordinate risk assessments balancing technical impact, patient safety, and regulatory compliance.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Turn executive strategy, development priorities, and target product profiles into actionable regulatory plans and submissions.

  • Apply in-depth knowledge of FDCA, PHS Act Section 351, 21 CFR, and FDA/ICH guidance to build submissions that meet current agency expectations.

  • Guide cross-functional teams in preparation for pre-IND/INTERACT and FDA meeting requests (Type A/B/C/D, pre-BLA/NDA).

  • Author and review CMC (Module 3), nonclinical (Modules 2.4/2.6, 4), or clinical (Modules 2.5/2.7, 5) components of regulatory submissions.

  • Support RA leadership in maintaining INDs, including protocol amendments, safety reports, and change notifications.

  • Prepare briefing materials, question strategies, and tracking minutes for FDA meetings.

  • Draft technical responses to FDA information requests and clinical holds.

  • Represent Regulatory Affairs on program teams to ensure deliverables meet regulatory requirements with the least-burdensome approaches.

  • Own core quality system processes, including CAPA, nonconformance reports (NCRs), change control, and SOP management.

  • Build and maintain agile quality systems that ensure compliance without slowing down our ability to deliver critical products.

  • Support FDA and CDMO inspection readiness (PAI/PLI, BIMO) through mock inspections and document preparation.

  • Manage and develop a team of quality and regulatory professionals as business needs require.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • B.S., M.S., or equivalent in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Chemistry, Biochemistry, or Engineering (experience may substitute for education).

  • 5-8 years of biotech or pharma industry experience in regulatory affairs, including Phase 1 IND through marketing application. Biologics experience preferred.

  • Hands-on experience with eCTD and FDA ESG submissions.

  • Working knowledge of FDA biologics regulations (21 CFR Parts 11, 50, 56, 58, 210/211, 312, 600-610) and ICH guidelines.

  • Direct experience managing CAPA, NCR, and change control in an electronic QMS.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

  • Capable of operating independently and building structure where it is missing.

  • Strong scientific writing and risk assessment skills, relying on evidence and data to make decisions.

  • Clear, proactive communicator who adapts quickly to shifting priorities.

  • Experience with CBER- or CDER-regulated biologics (monoclonal antibodies, recombinant proteins, cell/gene therapy).

  • RAC certification or ASQ CQA/CQE is a plus.

  • CDMO oversight and phase-appropriate GMP experience.

The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.
