All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. Further, Babel Street will not discriminate against applicants for inquiring about, discussing or disclosing their pay or, in certain circumstances, the pay of their co‐worker, Pay Transparency Nondiscrimination. In addition, Babel Street's policy is to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances where a particular employee works. For over 50 years, DN Solutions has built machine tools that shape the world around us, including the cars we drive, the planes we fly, and the medical devices that save lives. We develop smart machines and customized solutions that advance these essential industries.

Join our applications engineering team and help coach, teach, manage the current and future members of DN Solutions!

The Chicago Showroom Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, operation, and performance of the company's flagship technology center and showroom. This position oversees daily showroom activities, machine readiness, customer demonstrations, special events, training programs, and facility operations while ensuring an exceptional customer experience.

The Showroom Manager reports directly to Engineering Director and works closely with Sales, Applications Engineering, Automation, Product Management, Service, and Marketing teams to showcase manufacturing solutions, support sales growth, and position the company as a technology leader in the CNC machine tool industry.

Job Responsibilities

  • Lead all day-to-day operations of the Chicago Technology Center and showroom, ensuring a safe, professional, and customer-focused environment.
  • Oversee the readiness, operation, maintenance, installation, and relocation of showroom equipment, including CNC machine tools, automation systems, and robotics cells.

  • Develop and manage annual operating plans and budgets, oversee facility and event-related expenses, and identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and reduce costs.
  • Coordinate customer demonstrations, proof-of-concept projects, test cuts, and turnkey project runoffs, ensuring successful execution and effective use of showroom resources.

  • Collaborate with Marketing, Sales, Service, and Product Management to support customer engagement, new machine introductions, market launches, and strategic business initiatives.

Required

Preferred

  • Experience managing a machine tool showroom, technology center, or customer demonstration facility.
  • Experience in aerospace, medical, automotive, or other precision manufacturing industries.

title: Legal Recruiting Coordinator
description:
Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP, one of the world’s leading global law firms with offices in strategic hubs of commerce, law, and government across North America, Asia, Europe, and the Middle East, is seeking to hire a Legal Recruiting Coordinator. This position will reside in the Pittsburgh office and will be responsible for coordinating a wide range of activities supporting the overall planning, management and administration of student recruiting and integration, including planning of the summer associate program, orientation and special projects for the Pittsburgh office.


A hybrid in-office/remote working schedule is available for this position.

General Responsibilities


Law Student Recruiting:

  • Coordinate all aspects of 1L, 2L, and entry-level associate recruiting, delivering seamless and high-touch candidate experience.
  • Provide administrative support on firmwide law student recruiting initiatives.
  • Cultivate strong relationships with career services professionals and student organization leaders.
  • Design and execute impactful recruiting events, receptions, and follow-up strategies that strengthen the firm’s brand on campus.
  • Review candidate materials and prepare interview packages for review, serve as a primary point of contact throughout the recruiting lifecycle.
  • Coordinate callback interviews and create a polished, welcoming interview experience.
  • Contribute to offer strategy and follow-up office visits and lunches/dinners.
  • Compile information for National Association for Law Placement (NALP).
  • Maintain ViRecruit and other student recruiting databases; prepare status reports and update internal team with offers and declines.

Summer Associate Program:

  • Plan and participate in a best-in-class summer program, including orientation, training, and signature events.
  • Oversee the assignment process, maintaining a robust pipeline of meaningful work and tracking performance feedback.
  • Act as a trusted resource and primary point of contact for summer associates and attorneys, ensuring proper integration and a rewarding summer experience.
  • Drive consistent communication to ensure an inclusive, rewarding, and memorable summer experience.

Fall Associate Orientation:

  • Coordinate all aspects of onboarding for the fall associate class.
  • Oversee bar exam registration, preparation programs, and related logistics.
  • Administer relocation stipends and loan programs.
  • Plan and execute a comprehensive and welcoming fall orientation program.

Experience/Qualifications:


This job requires:

  • A bachelor’s degree (B. A.) from four-year college or university, and
  • A minimum of three years of related law firm recruiting experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Law student recruiting experience is preferred.
  • To perform the job successfully, an individual must demonstrate the following knowledge skills and abilities:
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • The ability to provide quality customer service to both internal and external clients.
  • Planning/organizational skills.
  • The ability to work individually as well as with a team.
  • Ability to adapt to change and balance competing demands.
  • Basic knowledge of the Microsoft Suite applications (MS Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Teams). Knowledge of ViRecruit and FloRecruit is a plus.

Qualified candidates must apply online by visiting our website at www.morganlewis.com and selecting “Careers.”

Job Title:

Brand Associate

Department:

External Affairs | Marketing | Brand Experience

Position Overview

The Office of Marketing (OM) builds, protects, and advances the Ohio State brand, strengthening the university’s reputation and ensuring a consistent, compelling brand presence across audiences and experiences. Within OM, the Brand Strategy & Stewardship function provides the enterprise capability that defines how the brand is understood, applied, and experienced across the institution.

The Brand Associate is a brand steward and trusted partner who supports the (interim) Senior Director, Brand Strategy & Stewardship in bringing Ohio State’s brand to life across the university. This role focuses on brand strategy application, governance support, guided consultation, and enablement—not marketing strategy or campaign execution. The Brand Associate helps ensure the brand is consistently and thoughtfully expressed across colleges, units, and initiatives, reinforcing Ohio State as a cohesive branded house. The Brand Associate provides brand consultation to assigned university partners, assisting and guiding them in applying the enterprise brand platform to their initiatives, environments, and experiences. This role supports brand architecture, naming, and co-branding efforts; contributes to brand governance processes; and helps implement brand tools, standards, and frameworks that enable others to deliver on brand intent.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Brand Strategy & Stewardship, the Brand Associate serves as a connector between brand strategy and institutional practice—helping teams interpret brand guidance, navigate brand decisions, and support the quality and consistency of brand expression across the enterprise. Working collaboratively across OM and the broader university, the Brand Associate brings together people, insights, and best practices to support brand-aligned outcomes. This role requires strong relationship-building skills, developing professional judgment, and the ability to work effectively in evolving situations while managing multiple priorities with guidance and support.Top of Form

All members of Advancement are part of creating an inclusive culture that inspires an exceptionally multifaceted and talented team and are expected to exhibit The Ohio State University’s Shared Values. The Office of Advancement is committed to acting with kindness, respect, and integrity at all times and welcoming our colleagues’ ideas, voices, and perspectives, acknowledging that we are better together.

About the Office of Marketing

The Office of Marketing (OM) advances The Ohio State University’s enterprise priorities by translating the university’s strategic plan into clear marketing imperatives, initiatives, and narratives that guide engagement with key audiences. OM leads enterprise marketing strategy and coordination to strengthen Ohio State’s reputation, visibility, and distinctiveness—enabling colleges, administrative units, Wexner Medical Center (WMC), and Athletics to align their priorities with institutional goals while addressing their unique audiences and needs. Through integrated marketing and brand stewardship, OM ensures the university presents a cohesive, compelling presence that drives impact at scale.


Duties and Responsibilities

60% Brand Stewardship & Consultation

  • Serve as a brand steward and advisor to guide campus-wide colleges, units and collaborators in applying Ohio State’s brand platform, experience principles and narrative
  • Serve as point of contact for Brand Center inquiries and requests, ensuring timely follow-up and resolution
  • Conduct reviews of brand applications and materials to ensure alignment with brand standards and guidelines; and provide recommendations for improvement
  • Route and evaluate brand-related inquiries to ensure alignment with policies and processes
  • Elevate complex or precedent-setting brand decisions to leadership for guidance and resolution as appropriate
  • Collaborate with OMC peers to ensure brand intent is understood and applied correctly across channels and disciplines
  • Assist leaders and teams in making informed brand decisions that protect and strengthen brand equity

25% Brand Governance & Enablement

  • Maintain and organize brand resources, templates, toolkits and reference materials to ensure access and usability for stakeholders
  • Contribute to the creation and refinement of brand guidelines, templates, and resources
  • Assist in developing brand education, onboarding materials, workshops and presentations to increase brand literacy and understanding across the institution
  • Support cultivating brand champions through organizational adoption of brand standards, tools and practices through communications, stakeholder engagement and change management
  • Support the development, maintenance and adoption of brand governance framework, standards and tools
  • Support brand architecture, naming and co-branding initiatives in alignment with enterprise strategy

10% Brand Insights & Continuous Improvement

  • Contribute to brand health reporting and insights in partnership with analytics teams
  • Collect and organize data related to brand adoption, compliance and stakeholder engagement, prepare summaries and reports to support brand usage and continuous improvement discussions
  • Identify and share trends, risk and opportunities related to brand consistency, perception and on-going brand evolution

5%

  • Performs other duties as assigned

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, psychology, or related field, or equivalent experience
  • Minimum two (2) years of professional experience in brand management, brand strategy, marketing or related roles
  • Experience applying an enterprise or master brand across multiple units or lines of business
  • Demonstrated ability to apply brand platforms to real-world scenarios with appropriate guidance
  • Effective consultative, relationship-building, and communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a complex, matrixed environment while receiving coaching and direction on higher impact decisions


Desired Qualifications (We’re committed to building a team that reflects a variety of skills and experiences and encourage you to apply even if your experience does not align perfectly)

  • Four (4) years of relevant brand strategy or brand stewardship experience
  • Experience in client, account, or relationship management roles
  • Experience working within large, decentralized organizations
  • Familiarity with brand governance, naming, or brand architecture processes

The Office of Advancement is committed to providing tools and resources for you to learn our business, proprietary databases, University-specific processes, and advancement practices.

You Need to Know

Aside from the unparalleled benefits of working for The Ohio State University and working in the vibrant, smart, enjoyable, and growing city of Columbus, Ohio, this opportunity will provide exceptional rewards that arise from working for an institution doing worldwide life-changing teaching and research. Learn more here: .

title: Real Estate Photographer - Phoenix, AZ
description:
Role Mission

Are you a visual storyteller with an eye for detail and a knack for seamless execution?

Ziprent (a subsidiary of TurboTenant) is looking for a independent contractor (1099) Real Estate Photographer & Field Operations Specialist to be our eyes and ears on the ground. This isn’t just about snapping a few photos; it’s about crafting the digital first impression for our rental properties and ensuring every home is "rent-ready" through meticulous property walkthroughs and technical setups.

In this role, you’ll serve as a vital link in our growth engine, transforming empty spaces into high-performing listings. You’ll work independently to manage everything from 3D tours and high-fidelity photography to smart lockbox installations and condition reporting. If you love the freedom of the road and have a "tech-forward" approach, we want to talk to you.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Visual Storytelling: Deliver 15–25+ professionally edited, high-quality interior and exterior photos that make our listings pop.
  • Immersive Tech: Capture Zillow 3D tours and digital floor plans using a 360° camera to provide prospective tenants with a "true-to-life" experience.
  • Property Stewardship: Perform initial property walkthroughs and submit comprehensive condition reports to ensure our high standards are met.
  • Operational Logistics: Take the lead on key management, including the pick-up, installation, and battery maintenance of smart lockboxes.
  • High-Velocity Response: Maintain a "Be Better" mindset by responding promptly to new assignments and ensuring a 24-hour turnaround on all reports and deliverables.
  • Territory Mastery: Serving our local community and surrounding region, with a willingness to travel a 35–50+ mile radius to support our expanding market.

Qualifications:

  • Proven Experience: A strong real estate photography portfolio showcasing your ability to capture spaces effectively.
  • Tech-Savvy Toolkit: Professional gear including a high-quality wide-angle lens and a 360° camera compatible with Zillow.
  • Editing Expertise: Advanced photo editing skills to ensure every shot is polished and professional.
  • Mobile Proficiency: An updated mobile device capable of capturing clear, detailed images for on-site walkthrough reports.
  • Collaborative Spirit: Excellent written communication skills and a professional demeanor when representing the Ziprent/TurboTenant brand.
  • Reliability: A valid driver’s license, a reliable vehicle, and a flexible schedule to handle multiple shoots per month.
  • Location: You must live within 35 miles of the market area to be considered for this role.

Bonus SuperPowers:

  • Compliance Knowledge: Familiarity with FHA and housing compliance (smoke alarms, CO detectors, etc.).
  • Efficient Workflow: You stay ahead of the curve by leveraging modern tools and smart processes to streamline documentation, reporting, and day-to-day tasks—maximizing productivity without sacrificing quality.
  • Tech Comfort: You have a "can-do" attitude when it comes to learning new property management software.
  • AI-Native Workflow: You use modern tools to streamline your editing or reporting process for maximum efficiency.
  • Hyper-Detail Oriented: You notice the small things—from a loose door handle to a flickering light—that others might miss.

Our "Be Better" Culture:

At TurboTenant, we live by the Be Better mantra. Our high-performance culture makes us relentless in our efforts to Be Better at serving our landlords and renters, and in unlocking the potential in one another.

What does our Be Better culture mean to you?

  1. You’ll be in an environment that pushes you to reach your potential.
  2. You’ll make a massive impact on our landlords, renters, company, and the proptech industry.
  3. You’ll be on the highest performing team of your career.

About Us:

At TurboTenant, we simplify the complex and intimidating process of managing your own rental property. And we do it through an elegant software platform for small, “do-it-yourself” landlords and their tenants. But don’t take our word for it. Read reviews from some of our 1 million landlords.

Quantity of Jobs:

Number of job requests varies by market region. This is a contracted 1099 position, and requests are sent out on an as-needed basis. Most markets average 3 –10+ jobs per month.

Candidates should be flexible and comfortable with limited assignments initially while the market and workload grow.

The role requires completion of a background check and signing of an independent contractor agreement.

Compensation

    • $225–$325+ per listing appointment (varies based on property size and scope)
      • Includes: professionally edited photos, Zillow 3D tour, floor plan, initial walkthrough report, and lockbox installation with key management
    • $50/hour for additional as-needed tasks
    • Lockbox Pick-Up:
      • $30–$60 per lockbox (depending on distance)
    • Travel Compensation:
      • Paid for travel exceeding 35 miles each way (70 miles round trip)
      • Reimbursed at $1.20 per mile beyond this threshold

Salary Range
$1—$100,000 USD

Additional Information

TurboTenant is proud to serve a diverse group of landlords and renters. We strive to reflect that diversity within our team. Employment at TurboTenant is based on merit, competence, performance, and business need. TurboTenant celebrates being an equal opportunity employer and never discriminates based on race, color, genetic information, religion, national origin, sex, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), age, or any other basis protected by law.

At this time, employer-based visa sponsorship is not available. All candidates must be eligible to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Next Steps

Ready to work on the highest performing team of your career at TurboTenant? Submit your resume and we’ll be in touch soon.

title: Salesperson
description:
Job Description

What is a Salesperson?

Entry level sales position capable of supporting the DIY business and achieve our sales and service objectives. The role has good knowledge of store systems, basic automotive system knowledge and basic part knowledge. The role has the basic ability to source from stores, hubs, pdq, and external suppliers. The role has in-depth knowledge of the store inventory and maintenance processes. Position can be part time or full time. Fleet safety certification preferred.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide excellent selling experience for DIY customer visits and phone calls
  • Achieve personal sales goal and help store achieve its sales goals
  • Provide DIY services including battery installation, testing, wiper installs, etc.
  • Maintain store product and operational standards
  • Responsible for inventory processes including truck put away, shoot outs, cycle counts, Back stock, etc.

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Store Cleanliness including floors, bathrooms, facing, dusting, parking lot
  • General stocking including truck stocking and back stock
  • Safely deliver parts to customers as needed

Success Factors

  • Basic driving and navigation ability
  • Ability to use delivery board system
  • Friendly communication
  • Ability to locate and stock parts
  • Safety knowledge and skills
  • Operating inventory systems and store equipment
  • Parts and automotive system knowledge skills
  • Operating POS and Parts lookup systems
  • Expert at testing and diagnostic equipment for DIY service

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a Salesperson

  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, peers and management
  • Read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, parts catalogs, and procedure manuals
  • Use basic math accurately: add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals
  • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings, and weekends as needed

Prior Experience that Sets a Salesperson up for Success

  • 2-3 years of successful sales experience in a diverse retail environment, providing superior customer experiences

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

description:
CINÉPOLIS CAREERS

Cinépolis USA is a luxury cinema exhibitor offering enhanced movie-going experiences through our “Cinépolis Luxury Cinemas” and “Movie House & Eatery” theater concepts. Based in Dallas, we operate 26 luxury and premium theaters across California, Florida, New Jersey, Connecticut, Texas, Maryland, and Ohio, with plans to expand further. As part of Cinépolis International, the most popular movie theater exhibitor globally, we are dedicated to innovation, film, and hospitality worldwide.

AS A CINÉPOLIS TEAM MEMBER, YOU ARE WHAT IS MOST IMPORTANT TO US!
Our team members enjoy a generous employee discount on tickets, food, and nonalcoholic beverages, and they also receive gifts for reaching milestone work anniversaries!

JOB DESCRIPTION

DEPARMENT: Operations

LOCATION: Theater

REPORTS TO: General Manager

JOB DUTIES

  • Deliver concessions items, kitchen items, and bar items to guests including utensils, sauces, and napkins while embodying Nice and Amazing Service by following all In Seat Dining procedures.
  • Work closely with expediter to ensure all food is delivered simultaneously, in high quality and in a timely fashion.
  • Demonstrate Commitment, and Integrity at all times – double check that orders are correct and complete and communicate with kitchen/expediter/supervisors if they are not.
  • Guide guests through the menu and suggest promotions, add-ons, or upselling, demonstrating knowledge of menu and Cinepolis offerings if guests would like to order more items.
  • Clean auditoriums removing all dishes, trash, and providing managers with any found items.
  • Be of service to your team members and assist them when needed including scanning tickets for guests, cleaning and restroom checks, and ringing up guests at concessions or box office.
  • Navigate guest complaints and assist with requests or direct them to proper resource if unable to assist.
  • Be cognizant of issues with movie projections-communicating with management when issues arise.
  • Complete all opening, mid and closing procedures- including but not limited to other duties.
  • Acknowledging guest by Cinépolis standards.
  • Attend and participate in trainings and meetings.


EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS


• Must be 18 years or older. Refer to your state guidelines.
• 1+ years of food running or bussing preferred.
• ServSafe, Food Handling, and Alcohol training certifications required.
• Strong interpersonal skills for interacting with employees, guests, and management.
• Effective communication skills with the ability to handle difficult and stressful situations and issues in a positive manner.
• Must be able to maintain strong attention to detail while able to prioritize in a fast-paced and constantly changing environment.
• Have integrity and can be counted on to do the right thing.
• Available nights, holidays, and weekends.

WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The employee may be asked to light lift 25lbs to 50lbs occasionally with assistance.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee regularly works in a theater environment where typical levels of noise, dust, and activity can be expected. The noise level in the work environment is typical for cinemas and can vary from moderate to high depending on areas of premise.

Job Details:

General Notes


Off-Campus Living plays a vital role in interfacing with the community beyond UT Austin. The coordinator serves as a student and family facing staff person to assist and educate around topics such as housing, transportation, connecting to Austin and various independent living skills. Through strategic outreach and program coordination, the coordinator ensures students have the information they need to make informed choices about their life outside of UT Austin. Must be eligible to work in the United States on a full-time basis for any employer.


Responsibilities

  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with campus and off-campus stakeholders by attending campus and community meetings. This could include property manager site visits, committee meetings, working groups and introductory meetings with organizations we wish to establish connections with.

  • Support students living off campus by connecting them with off-campus resources through a variety of digital medium and in-person opportunities (e.g., online apartment finder, email correspondence, social media, website, programming and tabling events, phone calls, and in person consultations).

  • Support students living off campus by creating and coordinating events collaboratively with campus partners and community organizations. Be responsible for idea generation, logistical details, execution of the event, and assessment of the success of the event.

  • Assist in the hiring, training, and development of student staff hired to support our off-campus work. The coordinator will help supervise student staff, provide feedback on work, co-lead student staff meetings, and meet individually with student staff on a weekly basis.

  • Support the student transition to off campus by creating and facilitating presentations for students, families, and staff regarding off-campus living, community resources and information about the Austin community. Customize presentations for various audiences such as graduate and international students on a variety of topics (e.g., affordable housing, emergency preparedness, exploring Austin, finding and being a good roommate, etc.).

  • Assist with other basic need and support areas including UT Outpost with functions including programming, outreach and logistical needs such as restocking pantry locations.

Required Qualifications


Bachelor’s degree and three years of experience developing, administering, facilitating and implementing programs for college students. Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with students, faculty, administration, and external stakeholders. Professional demeanor. Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills including presentations, written correspondence, and reports. Equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.


Preferred Qualifications


Preference will be given to candidates with a graduate degree in student affairs administration, public administration, public policy, educational leadership or related fields. Experience with university housing, property management, real estate, local governmental affairs and emergency preparedness. Possess effective facilitation skills and experience delivering content in dynamic environments. Knowledge of event planning and communications. Experience supervising professional and para-professional staff. Demonstrated, end-to-end project/program management experience.

$58,750

  • Repetitive use of a keyboard at a workstation

title: CRM Manager (Hubspot)
description:
Know HubSpot inside and out? Put that expertise to work making the world a little more connected, safe, and understanding.

For over 50 years, InterExchange, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, has connected young people from around the world with life-changing cultural exchange experiences. Our participants are au pairs, summer camp counselors, university students in seasonal jobs, and young professionals in training and internships, each welcomed by an American host family, camp, or employer. HubSpot is how we make those connections work: finding hosts who will truly welcome participants, guiding applicants through each step, and making sure that anyone who needs support, even thousands of miles from home, gets it quickly.

The Role

As our CRM Manager, you'll own, run, and continuously improve our HubSpot ecosystem across Sales, Marketing, and Service Hubs. This is a hands-on, cross-functional role: you'll be the platform's primary administrator and a trusted partner to participant and host recruitment, marketing, support, and our data team. You’ll partner with programs, marketing, support, customer experience, and leadership to understand evolving needs and translate them into scalable HubSpot solutions.

What You'll Do

  • Run the platform. Manage configuration, pipelines, custom objects, workflows, and permissions; set governance standards; and keep data clean, deduplicated, and well-documented.
  • Protect our email reputation. Oversee deliverability, sending domains, subscriptions, and consent so our emails reach people and honor their choices.
  • Enable our teams. Facilitate our HubSpot Community of Practice, a cross-functional governance forum where platform decisions are made collaboratively across teams; manage the request intake process, build workflows, reports, and campaigns, and train users to become self-sufficient.
  • Power participant support. Own Service Hub, including knowledge bases, live chat, AI-assisted replies and chatbots, ticket pipelines, and SLAs.
  • Strengthen host recruitment. Adapt Sales Hub to a mission-driven setting, set up outreach tools and data enrichment, and report on what brings in the strongest hosts.
  • Partner with Data. Serve as the HubSpot expert on reverse ETL pipelines and data extracts, aligning object models and field definitions with our broader data architecture.
  • Turn data into insight. Build trusted dashboards and KPI reporting for recruitment, marketing, support, and leadership.

What You'll Bring

Required

  • 5+ years of hands-on HubSpot admin-level experience across Sales, Marketing, and Service Hubs, including multiple brands or business units
  • Deep configuration skills: properties, pipelines, lifecycle stages, custom objects, workflows, automation, and dashboards
  • Experience implementing CRM governance, data quality standards, and deduplication
  • Strong knowledge of AI capabilities, including HubSpot's
  • A solid grasp of how sales, marketing, and support operations intersect in a CRM
  • Clear, plain-language communication and a habit of listening first, understanding why a process works before changing it
  • Comfort working independently and juggling priorities across teams

Nice to Have

  • HubSpot certifications (Sales, Marketing, Service, RevOps, or CRM Implementation)
  • Experience with reverse ETL tools such as Census or Hightouch, and with data warehousing concepts
  • Working knowledge of SQL, YAML, dbt models, webhooks, or REST APIs
  • Experience training non-technical users and writing documentation for them
  • A background in operations or revenue operations at a mid-sized organization

Please note that this is an outline of the essential functions and requirements of this position and is not intended to be exhaustive.

Start Date

TBD, applications will be accepted on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Compensation

This is a full-time, exempt position, with a starting base salary of $145,000 annualized

Hours & Location

Monday to Friday; 9:30 am - 5:30 pm, with flexible start/end times available, and additional hours if needed.

Hybrid schedule with 3 days per week in our NYC headquarters.

How to Apply

Complete our online application form and upload your resume

Benefits & Perks of Employment at InterExchange

  • Affordable, quality medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401k retirement plan with safe harbor employer contribution
  • Generous paid time off and health time off package
  • Employer-sponsored life insurance
  • Flex-time options
  • Professional Development & Educational Assistance Program
  • Pre-tax FSA for medical and/or dependent care expenses
  • Pre-tax commuter benefits
  • Supplemental insurance plans
  • Pet Insurance Discount

About Us

InterExchange is a private, nonprofit organization with over 50 years of experience in international cultural exchange. We are dedicated to promoting international understanding through development and implementation of affordable intercultural and life experiential work/training opportunities. By participating in InterExchange programs both in the U.S. and abroad, tens of thousands of young people and their hosts have gained insight into other cultures. InterExchange is designated by the U.S. Department of State to sponsor several J-1 Visa exchange programs including Au Pair USA, Work & Travel USA, Camp USA, and Career Training USA. Program participants are placed in the U.S. and abroad by InterExchange in collaboration with international cooperating agencies and government agencies. Additionally, we offer Work Abroad opportunities for Americans seeking similar experience overseas.

Opportunities for All

InterExchange is fully committed to providing opportunities for people across all dimensions of race, ethnicity, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, socio-economic status, age, sensory, mental, or physical abilities, religious beliefs, marital status, veteran status, political beliefs, and more. We strive to maintain an environment for our staff, leadership, and board that is vibrant, welcoming, innovative, collaborative, and free of barriers and discriminatory practices—strengthening our programs while reinforcing our commitment to fairness and representation in the field of cultural exchange.

Any essential function or requirement of this job will be evaluated as necessary should an applicant be unable to perform the function or requirement due to a disability as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Reasonable accommodation(s) for the specific disability will be made for the employee or applicant when possible.

Mutual Understanding & Respect

InterExchange actively promotes an environment of respectful communication and collaboration both internally and externally. We encourage thoughtful exchange of ideas and create space for all voices to be heard and respected.

We are excited to welcome a new team member who actively embraces our mission and values.

title: Landscape Project Manager
description:
Landscape Project Manager – Irrigation & Landscape Construction

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Landscape Project Manager to oversee a large-scale commercial landscape and irrigation conservation project.

This position will be responsible for managing all aspects of project execution, including scheduling, budgeting, procurement, subcontractor coordination, quality control, and project closeout.

The ideal candidate has a strong background in commercial landscape construction, irrigation systems, and construction project management, with proven experience working alongside general contractors on complex projects.

Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee daily project operations to ensure work is completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and according to specifications.
  • Develop and manage project schedules, budgets, procurement plans, and resource allocation.
  • Coordinate with general contractors, subcontractors, field crews, vendors, and other project stakeholders.
  • Monitor project costs, labor productivity, material usage, and financial performance.
  • Review construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and project requirements.
  • Manage project documentation, including RFIs, submittals, change orders, progress billing, and cost forecasts.
  • Coordinate irrigation system upgrades, including pressure-regulated components, high-efficiency nozzles, drip irrigation, and controller programming.
  • Oversee landscape renovation activities, including turf removal, grading, soil preparation, planting, and mulching.
  • Ensure all installations meet project specifications, quality standards, and safety requirements.
  • Identify and resolve project challenges, scheduling conflicts, and potential cost overruns.
  • Conduct site inspections and coordinate testing, commissioning, and quality assurance.
  • Maintain accurate project records, progress reports, and documentation.
  • Manage final inspections, punch lists, project closeout, and warranty handoff.

Required Qualifications

  • Proven experience managing large-scale commercial landscape construction and irrigation projects.
  • Strong understanding of landscape installation, irrigation systems, and water conservation practices.
  • Experience coordinating projects with general contractors, subcontractors, and field operations teams.
  • Knowledge of construction budgeting, scheduling, cost forecasting, change orders, and project documentation.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and contracts.
  • Experience managing multiple crews, vendors, and project timelines.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and construction project management software.
  • Strong organizational, leadership, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with large commercial properties, corporate campuses, or complex landscape renovation projects.
  • Familiarity with irrigation retrofits, water conservation systems, and drought-tolerant landscaping.
  • Knowledge of Rain Bird irrigation products or comparable irrigation systems.
  • Irrigation Association certification or related industry credentials.
  • Degree in Construction Management, Landscape Architecture, Horticulture, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

What We're Looking For

We are seeking a hands-on Project Manager who can effectively balance field operations, financial performance, and client expectations. The successful candidate will be proactive, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing complex construction projects in a fast-paced environment.

This is an opportunity to contribute to a significant landscape and irrigation conservation project while working with an experienced team of landscape professionals.

title: Director, Pre-Award Program Management
description:
About Us:

eSimplicity is modern digital services company that work across government, partnering with our clients to improve the lives and ensure the security of all Americans-from soldiers and veteran to kids and the elderly, and defend national interests on the battlefield. Our engineers, designers and strategist cut through complexity to create intuitive products and services that equip Federal agencies with solutions to courageously transform today for a better tomorrow for all Americans.


The Director, Pre-Award Program Management is eSimplicity’s dedicated Bid Readiness Lead on large and strategic pursuits. The role is the link between capture, technical proposal, basis of estimate (BOE) and program delivery and risk. It ensures that our price proposal is competitive, compliant, defensible and executable, as well as aligned with our technical response. The Director is accountable for the BOE and for optimizing the balance between competitive pricing and execution risk, including proposal assumptions. The Director may also be responsible for management, staffing and/or key personnel for some proposals, as well as pre-award program planning. After award, the Director supports program startup activities, as needed.


The Director takes part in capture only as far as needed to understand the solution and ground the estimate. Capture strategy, customer relationships and teaming remain with the Capture Manager.


Building on this work, the Director also maintains eSimplicity’s program-management standards and supports readiness for CMMI appraisals and ISO audits. This enables process compliance and excellent performance, and ensures that what we propose matches how we actually work. The COO may also assign the Director to manage a small program, with a matching reduction in other responsibilities.


Responsibilities:


Proposal: Estimation and BOE

  • Own the level of effort (LOE) and the Basis of Estimate: the BOE spreadsheet, BOE narrative and technical assumptions.
  • Serve as eSimplicity’s go-to authority for compliant, defensible BOEs. This covers solicitation requirements, contract type (FFP, T&M, cost-plus, IDIQ task orders), price realism and price reasonableness.
  • Work with Pricing through pricing iterations and trade-offs. Assess the impact of pricing changes on meeting SOO/SOW/PWS objectives, program execution, proposal risk and program risk.
  • Maintain and manage eSimplicity’s BOE standards, templates and estimating assumptions.
  • Look for AI and other tools that make estimating, proposal development and program management faster and more accurate.


Proposal: Risk

  • Identify execution risks and mitigations, and estimate what they would cost. Recommend how that cost should be reflected in the price.
  • Develop and document the pricing assumptions that come from the BOE, and help build both bid case and business case scenarios.
  • Contribute to and review the Execution Model (the cost and price model we believe we will actually deliver at) alongside the Bid Model, so the executability review is complete before Price & Proposal Submission approval.
  • Give leadership a clear, concise read on risk, compliance and financial exposure at bid/no-bid gate reviews and price approval.


Proposal: Management and Staffing

  • Write or lead the management, staffing and key personnel sections. Contribute to the technical solution.
  • Recommend team structures and labor mix that are competitive and staffable.
  • Lead or support identification of key personnel, résumés and letters of commitment.
  • Take part in color team reviews. Make sure proposal commitments line up with the BOE and with eSimplicity practices.


Capture Involvement

  • Involvement in capture serves the estimate. The aim is continuity, clarity and early answers for the BOE, risk and staffing work above, not ownership of capture.
  • Join capture early enough to understand the customer’s requirements, the emerging solution and the win strategy, so the LOE, BOE and staffing plan reflect the real solution.
  • Give the Capture Manager and solution architects a delivery and cost view: what is executable, what is staffable, and what price-to-win trade-offs mean for risk.
  • Contribute to the management and staffing approach as the solution takes shape.

Pre-award Planning and Program startup

  • Build the program plan, staffing and hiring plan, incumbent capture plan and financial plan before award, so we are ready on day one.
  • After award, lead or provide hands-on support for startup and transition, as needed, until the program is stable.


Process Standards and Audit Readiness

  • This work grows out of the bid and startup work above. The person who defines how we estimate, staff and start programs is well placed to keep those practices documented, consistent and audit-ready.
  • Keep proposal-ready descriptions of our certifications, quality processes and management approach, so proposals describe what we really do.
  • Maintain a lightweight set of program management standards, templates and tools, starting with estimating, startup, reporting and risk practices.
  • Support readiness for CMMI appraisals and ISO audits with process assets, artifacts and metrics, in coordination with Integrated Operations and Security, which own those programs and related standards such as CMMC.
  • Run internal process compliance checks. Track findings and corrective actions to closure.


Program Management

  • When assigned by the COO, serve as PM for a small, stable program, with a matching reduction in other responsibilities. Own customer relationships, delivery, staffing and financial performance.

As an Aquatic Technician, you will play a crucial role in ensuring the health, safety, and functionality of aquatic facilities, including ponds, lakes, pools, aquariums, and water features.

title: Senior Product Manager: Developer Experience
description:
About Us

Trase is the operating system for high-stakes environments, providing end-to-end solutions for deploying, managing, and optimizing AI within industries where security, governance, and data sovereignty are non-negotiable.

Our HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant platform bridges the “last mile” of AI adoption, empowering sectors like healthcare and national security to run trustworthy, predictable AI agents across any model or environment—whether in the cloud, on-prem, or at the edge—with unified policy enforcement, continuous monitoring, and fully immutable audit trails.

Trase’s suite of products includes Origin, its agentic operating system; Leagues, its marketplace for specialized, configurable, ready-to-deploy agents; and Arena, where developers build, evaluate, and package the agents that run on Origin. The company has repeatedly topped Hugging Face’s GAIA Leaderboard for Generalized AI Assistants, placing it firmly at the forefront of AI-agent innovation.

The role: Senior Product Manager, Developer Experience

You'll own the experience of developers who build, test, and deploy AI agents with Trase. Your job is to help a new developer get to a working agent quickly and give experienced teams tools they can trust in production. As teams move from experimental agent demos to mission-critical production systems, you will define the standard for how serious developers build, evaluate, and ship AI agents.

You’ll be the product manager for Trase Arena, our SDK and tools for building AI agents. Your scope covers a developer’s work from the first build through deployment, observability and improvement on Origin. You'll work directly with developers, engineering, design, and product marketing to build an experience that earns adoption through the product itself.

What You Will Do

  • Know the developer: Work directly with developers to understand what they're trying to build. Observe where they get stuck, test assumptions, and use what you learn to set priorities.
  • Set a high bar for the tools: Own the developer experience across the SDK, APIs, and CLI. Make them consistent, predictable, well documented, and useful for real development work.
  • Make the whole journey work: Connect building, testing, evaluation, packaging, and deployment into a coherent experience. Partner with the enterprise platform PM to make the path through production approval clear for builders and operators.
  • Own documentation and onboarding: Treat these as core parts of the product. Help developers understand the concepts, complete their first deployment, and solve problems independently.
  • Build ecosystem foundations: Prioritize examples, templates, and reference integrations that help developers build useful agents. Shape how developers discover, reuse, and share what others have built.
  • Earn developer trust: Establish clear expectations for compatibility, API versioning, and deprecation. Work with engineering to make changes understandable and manageable for developers.
  • Drive product-led growth: Reduce friction from first use through repeat adoption. Partner with product marketing on getting-started content and developer adoption, grounding that work in the actual product experience.
  • Measure and deliver: Own priorities and follow through from discovery to release. Track monthly active developers, time to first deployment, onboarding time, developer satisfaction, and the number of agents built with Arena and running on Origin.

About You

  • You've owned and shipped developer products such as SDKs, APIs, CLIs, or development platforms.
  • You have strong product taste in developer tooling: You have an opinionated point of view on what makes an API intuitive, an error message actionable, and a CLI joyful to use—and you can defend those opinions with engineers and designers.
  • You care about the details developers notice: clear abstractions, useful errors, accurate examples, dependable behavior, and documentation that answers the question.
  • You think like an entrepreneur. You identify useful opportunities, test them with developers, and turn what you learn into product decisions.
  • You take ownership without waiting for direction. You understand how to keep individual developers moving fast without creating dead-ends, allowing us to scale into production.
  • You learn quickly and exercise sound judgment. You can explain a complex problem clearly and choose a practical path through it.
  • You ship and measure what happens next. Your standard is whether developers can successfully build and deploy something useful.

Nice to have (not required)

  • Experience building AI agents or working with evaluation and testing tools.
  • Experience growing a developer ecosystem, marketplace, or integration platform.
  • Experience improving self-service activation and developer retention.
  • Experience connecting developer workflows with enterprise production requirements.

Our Trase Benefits:

For full-time roles only

  • Career track opportunity with potential for rapid advancement with strong performance as the firm grows
  • 100% employer paid, comprehensive health care including medical, dental, and vision for you and your family.
  • Paid maternity and paternity for 14 weeks at employees' normal pay.
  • Unlimited PTO, with management approval.
  • Opportunities for professional development and continued learning.

description:
CINÉPOLIS CAREERS

Cinépolis USA is a luxury cinema exhibitor offering enhanced movie-going experiences through our “Cinépolis Luxury Cinemas” and “Movie House & Eatery” theater concepts. Based in Dallas, we operate 26 luxury and premium theaters across California, Florida, New Jersey, Connecticut, Texas, Maryland, and Ohio, with plans to expand further. As part of Cinépolis International, the most popular movie theater exhibitor globally, we are dedicated to innovation, film, and hospitality worldwide.

AS A CINÉPOLIS TEAM MEMBER, YOU ARE WHAT IS MOST IMPORTANT TO US!
Our team members enjoy a generous employee discount on tickets, food, and nonalcoholic beverages, and they also receive gifts for reaching milestone work anniversaries!

JOB DESCRIPTION

FLSA STATUS: Non-Exempt

TITLE: Kitchen Staff
DEPARMENT: Operations

LOCATION: Theater
SUPERVISORY RESPONSABILITY NO

REPORTS TO: Kitchen Manager

JOB SUMMARY
The Kitchen staff will ensure consistency in food quality, prepare orders in a short period of time, and prepare menu items in accordance with established recipes and guidelines. All of this must be done while maintaining a clean, safe, and sanity working area.

JOB DUTIES

• Show Passion and Commitment by preparing menu items accurately and promptly when ordered through point of sale system.
• Show integrity by only making items ordered through the point of sale system and always doing the right thing.
• Be of service and accommodate special requests whenever possible, with management approval, to create a positive and tailored experience for each guest.
• Prepares dishes according to recipes to maintain quality and consistency throughout Cinepolis.
• Cook menu items in cooperation with the rest of the kitchen staff to ensure that food comes out simultaneously, in high quality and in a timely fashion.
• Remake items when instructed by a Supervisor or Manager.
• Always Adhere to Food Handlers Safety guidelines including by not limited to the following: Keep all food items within safe temperatures, label all food correctly with dates, always avoiding cross contamination by washing hands and using correct tools and surfaces.
• Maintain order and cleanliness by washing dishes and cleaning work area during the shift and at the end of shift.
• Keeps all kitchen areas stocked with dry products and prep materials and restock dry goods consistently throughout shift and at end of shift.
• Uses FIFO system to keep food fresh and eliminate waste.
• Accurately maintain waste logs for all discarded items whether due to being expired or dishes made incorrectly/sent back.
• Keep supervisor and kitchen manager up to date on inventory levels.
• Maintain a positive and professional approach with coworkers and customers.
• Work safely and at all times including using cutting gloves, asking for assistance if needed with moving heavy items, or staying hydrated from heat.
• Lock and secure food and equipment.
• Follow all opening, mid and closing procedures.
• Attend and participate in trainings and meetings.
• Other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

• Must have at least 1 year of professional kitchen experience, culinary training preferred. Experience should include dishwashing, prep/cook, and expediting experience.
• If does not meet experience requirements, position can start as a dishwasher and/or prep cook as an entry level with career growth potential.
• ServSafe training certification preferred or must complete training and certification provided by Cinépolis prior to going on the line
• Proficiency in kitchen operations and execution
• Must have working knowledge of U.S. measurements, weight and volume
• Ability to follow instructions on safe use of all chemical/cleaning materials
• Must work effectively with supervisors and co-workers and with minimal supervision
• Ability to meet deadlines- time management.
• Ability to stand on feet for an extended period of time
• Ability to walk, lift, twist, bend, reach, and handle food products on a frequent basis.
• Good communication skills with support personnel and management and ability to work effectively with supervisors and co-workers in a high-volume setting.
• Ability to handle difficult and stressful situations and issues in a positive manner
• Bilingual in Spanish and English a plus, but not a requirement
• Flexible working hours including holidays and weekends

WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL DEMANDS


The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, you will walk, bend, and stand for periods of time. The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds. The employee may be asked to light lift 25lbs to 50lbs occasionally with assistance.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee regularly works in a theater environment where typical levels of noise, dust and activity can be expected. The noise level in the work environment is typical for cinemas and can vary from moderate to high depending on areas of premise.

title: Clinical Field Specialist
description:
Clinical Field Specialist (CFS) – Women’s Health

Territory: West Texas (Covering Lubbock, Midland, Odessa, Amarillo, Abilene, San Angelo, and El Paso)

Position Summary The Clinical Field Specialist (CFS) will drive revenue growth and market expansion across the West Texas territory through direct engagement with individual Maternal-Fetal Medicine specialists (MFMs), OB/GYNs, and Genetic Counselors. This role focuses on building and maintaining strong clinical relationships while developing and executing strategic business plans that accelerate adoption. The CFS will support both established and newly launched diagnostic products, providing clinical expertise, educational support, and hands-on training in technical product applications.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Revenue & Market Growth: Increase revenue and drive market development through direct consultative sales to individual MFMs, OB/GYNs, and Genetic Counselors across the West Texas region.
  • Relationship Management: Execute effective prospecting strategies while cultivating and maintaining long-term relationships with key clinical stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Strategic Territory Execution: Create and implement a comprehensive business plan to rapidly grow market share and revenue across a geographically expansive territory.
  • Product Launch & Support: Champion both currently marketed diagnostic assays and new product launches, serving as a clinical and technical resource for accounts.
  • Organizational Impact: Play a critical role in regional and national commercial success by sharing market insights and collaborating cross-functionally.
  • Compliance & Data Security: Work regularly with Protected Health Information (PHI) in both paper and electronic formats, utilizing secure technologies to perform daily job functions.
  • Training Requirements: Complete mandatory training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance, and security within the first 30 days of hire, and maintain current status on all ongoing Natera training requirements.

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required; preferred fields include Science, Nursing (RN/NP), or a related healthcare discipline.
  • Experience & Clinical Background: Three (3) years of physician sales experience in the diagnostic laboratory or women's health industry is preferred, though not strictly required for candidates with strong clinical credentials. We are actively open to Nurse Practitioners (NPs) currently working within an MFM or OB/GYN practice looking to transition into a commercial clinical specialist role.
  • Local Ties: Must reside within the West Texas territory; candidates with established roots, local familiarity, and existing clinical relationships in the region are strongly preferred.
  • Market Knowledge: Deep understanding of the OB/GYN and MFM workflow and clinical landscape, with a proven ability to build trust with providers.
  • Launch & Growth Mindset: Demonstrated ability to drive adoption, educate clinical teams, and grow volume in developing or expansive markets.
  • Technical Proficiency: Proficient with Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Gmail, and Salesforce.com.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Communication: Strong organizational and presentation skills with the proven ability to communicate complex clinical data effectively to diverse audiences.
  • Territory & Time Management: Exceptional time management and travel-planning skills with the ability to assess, route, and prioritize opportunities effectively across a wide geographic footprint.
  • Strategic Mindset: Adaptable, self-motivated, and results-driven, combining strong interpersonal and analytical skills with the ability to think strategically while executing tactically.
  • Closing Focus: Demonstrates a sense of urgency and a strong focus on closing business and driving consistent test volume.
  • Consultative Problem-Solving: Assesses the operational and clinical needs of medical professionals through consultative sales, logistical coordination, and proactive problem-solving.
  • Collaboration: Works effectively both independently in the field and collaboratively with internal commercial, medical affairs, and customer support teams.

Compensation & Benefits The total on-target earnings (OTE) package includes a competitive base salary along with uncapped quarterly commissions. Beyond OTE, the comprehensive compensation package also features a monthly car allowance, Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and full corporate benefits.



The compensation package listed is for 1st year OTE, which are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. On-target earnings (OTE) represent the total potential income an employee can earn by achieving 100% of their performance goals. It combines a base salary with commissions and serves as an estimated figure rather than a guaranteed amount, providing a guideline based on average performance outcomes.

On-target earnings (OTE)
$165,000—$195,000 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. title: Senior Payment Integrity Program Development Manager – Operational Excellence
description:
Job Description

A bit about this role:


At Devoted, our mission is to build trust with our providers and members by ensuring claims are paid accurately and on time with transparent policies. Our Payment Integrity Concept Development team develops and sustains programs that improve payment accuracy, affordability, and provider experience.

As our Senior Payment Integrity Program Development Manager – Operational Excellence, you will help ensure our internal and vendor-supported payment integrity edits and audits are implemented accurately, perform as intended, and continue delivering value over time.

You will combine payment integrity expertise, analytical judgment, and operational leadership to manage complex portfolio activities, investigate performance issues, and develop more effective and scalable ways of working. Partnering across technical and operational teams, you will drive improvements that strengthen program accuracy, financial performance, efficiency, and provider experience.

Success means not only resolving today's problems, but im

proving the systems that prevent them from recurring.


Your responsibilities and impact will include:

  • Portfolio Performance & Optimization: Evaluate the effectiveness of payment integrity edits and audits, independently investigate complex performance or operational issues, identify root causes, and drive improvements in accuracy, financial outcomes, and provider experience.

  • Implementation & Validation Assurance: Ensure new and modified payment integrity programs are appropriately validated and implemented as intended. Partner with technical and operational teams to strengthen testing, quality controls, and implementation reliability.

  • Portfolio Maintenance & Operational Execution: Lead assigned internal and vendor-supported portfolio activities, ensuring effective prioritization, issue resolution, maintenance, and ongoing program performance.

  • Operational Transformation & Scalability: Identify and implement improvements to processes, workflows, and supporting capabilities across validation, monitoring, maintenance, and knowledge sharing. Leverage technology, automation, and operational best practices to improve efficiency, transparency, and scalability.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence: Independently advance complex initiatives, develop evidence-based recommendations, and build alignment across Payment Integrity, Engineering, Data Science, Claims, Compliance, and other stakeholders to achieve measurable results.


Required skills and experience:

  • Bachelor's degree and 6+ years of relevant professional experience, including substantial hands-on payment integrity experience within a health plan or payment integrity vendor.

  • Strong understanding of healthcare claims, payment integrity edits and audits, claims adjudication, Medicare/CMS reimbursement policies, NCCI/CCI edits, and supporting operational processes.

  • Demonstrated ability to investigate complex payment integrity issues, analyze root causes, and drive effective resolution.

  • Strong analytical and technical literacy, including the ability to read and interpret SQL queries, claims data, configuration specifications, validation results, and performance metrics.

  • Proven experience designing and implementing operational improvements, scalable workflows, or technology-enabled solutions that deliver measurable results.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently explore and apply analytical tools, technology, and automation to improve workflows, identify opportunities, and develop scalable operational solutions.

  • Experience collaborating with technical and operational partners to implement, troubleshoot, or improve payment integrity programs.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex, multiphase initiatives, exercise sound judgment, and influence cross-functional stakeholders.


Desired skills and experience:

  • Experience with Medicare Advantage and Commercial payment integrity programs.

  • Experience with vendor-supported claims editing platforms or proprietary payment integrity solutions.

  • Professional coding certification (e.g., CPC, CCS) or comparable reimbursement expertise.

  • Experience implementing AI-enabled analytics, automated testing, performance monitoring, or workflow automation to improve payment integrity operations.

title: Department Chair, Applied Clinical Psychology
description:
Job Description:

Department Chair, Applied Clinical Psychology

About The Chicago School

The Chicago School is a nonprofit university with seven in-person locations across the United States, a growing online campus, and education partnerships worldwide. The Chicago School is a minority-majority university with 6,000+ students across 35+ degree programs in psychology, behavioral health, and nursing. The Chicago School is committed to creating a diverse pipeline of future professionals who will fundamentally improve the health and well-being of future generations of diverse communities. Founded in 1979 by a group of psychologists and educators, The Chicago School has grown into a dominant and globally respected leader in the fields of psychology and behavioral health sciences. Today, The Chicago School has an annual operating budget of nearly $150M and employs nearly 600 full-time faculty and staff. As an institution, The Chicago School is deeply committed to student success, innovation, and community impact. Our students are meaningfully connected in their communities, donating more than 1.2 million service hours per year through fieldwork and practicum opportunities. The Chicago School is part of the TCS Education System, a nonprofit system of colleges advancing student success and community impact.


The Program:

The Applied Clinical Psychology program is a post-master’s Psy.D. program. Students complete two years of coursework covering advanced topics in psychology. Additionally, they complete a practicum in the second year, and the third year is dedicated to a full-time internship. Students complete a dissertation as part of the program. Student enroll in the program in one of three modalities/locations: Anaheim, Los Angeles, and Online Distance Learning. All modalities/locations of the program involve asynchronous and synchronous learning opportunities for the students.


Position Title:

Department Chair – Applied Clinical Psychology


Principle Duties:

  • Maintain collegial, productive relationships with relevant accrediting, licensure, and professional bodies, and ensure timely completion of all required reports and documentation, such as the internal program review processes.
  • Provide leadership and oversight of the program’s compliance with the Program Learning Outcomes and continuous quality improvement.
  • Facilitate Program Faculty Governance and All Faculty meetings and support effective faculty participation in decision-making.
  • Provide leadership and oversight for the professional development of Department, Affiliate, and Adjunct Faculty, ensuring alignment with quality standards, licensure requirements, and institutional priorities.
  • Provide academic leadership for curriculum design, review, and revision to ensure relevance and scientific integrity.
  • Oversee and support all aspects of student affairs at the program level, including student progression, evaluation, and remediation processes.
  • Oversee and support the development and maintenance of high-quality practicum and internship training opportunities; ensure monitoring of supervisor credentials, site quality, and training alignment with program’s licensure states.
  • Develop strategic academic and budget plans for the Department, including actions based on assessment findings and program review outcomes; achieve departmental academic and financial goals.
  • Promote a culturally responsive learning environment and ensure integration of multicultural and diversity competencies across coursework and clinical training.
  • Participate in and oversee program-related scholarship, research, and scientific inquiry consistent with the program’s training model.
  • Provide leadership for dissertation processes, student research mentorship, and faculty engagement in scholarly work.

Supervise the Program Chair(s), Department Manager, Department Faculty, and Training Faculty, to achieve academic, training, and operational goals, and to ensure the effective functioning of each.

Position Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. or Psy.D. in Clinical Psychology, preferably from an APA-accredited doctoral program.
  • Licensed as a psychologist, preferably in the State of California.
  • Demonstrated identity as a psychologist, reflected in scholarship, professional activities, and engagement in the field.
  • Significant experience in graduate psychology education, including teaching, advising, dissertation supervision, and academic administration.
  • Experience supervising clinical training (practicum and/or internship).
  • Proven ability to lead academic programs or units within a university setting, with strengths in strategic planning, accreditation, program assessment, and curriculum development.
  • Commitment to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) and demonstrated ability to promote multicultural competence among faculty, students, and training sites.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, organization, and people-development skills, with the ability to support faculty excellence and foster interdisciplinary initiatives.
  • Record of scholarly productivity and professional achievement appropriate to a doctoral-level program.
  • Ability to represent the program professionally to internal and external stakeholders, training sites, community partners, and accrediting bodies.

Disclaimer:

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. All personnel may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed.

Application:

To apply, please complete this application and include a letter of interest and curriculum vitae

The Chicago School offers a generous compensation and benefits package, as well as the opportunity to work for a leader in the field of education. Some of our key benefits include: generous paid time-off, medical and dental coverage, company-paid life and disability insurance, retirement plan with employer contribution, multiple flexible spending accounts (FSA), tuition reimbursement, professional development, and regular employee appreciation events.

The Chicago School is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Data Analytics & Engineering Tech Lead - IoT
description:
Digital & Technology Team (D&T) Digital & Technology Team (D&T) is an integral division of HEINEKEN Business Services Poland (HBSP). We are committed to making Heineken the most connected brewery.
