Cargo: Advanced Tree Trimmer

Tipo de salario: No exento

Fecha de creación/Fecha de revisión: 04/24/2026

Resumen del puesto:

El Advanced Tree Trimmer es un Qualified Line Clearance Tree Trimmer (podador calificado para el despeje de líneas) responsable de podar y retirar árboles, ramas y arbustos cerca de las líneas eléctricas para reducir la interferencia de la vegetación. La persona en esta función utiliza diversos equipos, herramientas y técnicas para realizar cuidados avanzados de los árboles, considerando patrones de crecimiento y asegurando la salud y apariencia del árbol.

Funciones esenciales del puesto:

  • Carga vehículos y equipos con ramas y troncos de tamaño fácil de manipular que no sean aptos para astillar.

  • Poda, retira o tala árboles usando equipos de trepa, como camión con elevador aéreo (canasta), arnés de seguridad, cuerda de trepa y escalera. También trabaja en el suelo utilizando sierras manuales, sierras de suelo, podadoras u otras herramientas aplicables.

  • Trabaja en altura para cortar ramas o secciones de tronco y bajarlas al suelo con cuerdas de aparejo.

  • Utiliza herramientas apropiadas en el suelo para talar árboles o troncos caídos y dividirlos en piezas fáciles de manipular.

  • Trabaja cerca de equipos peligrosos y puede desempeñarse en proximidad a líneas energizadas mientras supervisa directamente las actividades de empleados no calificados que trabajan cerca de conductores energizados.

  • Aplica herbicidas con reguladores de crecimiento a la maleza (brush) y los troncos. Mantiene los registros de aplicación correspondientes.

  • Cumple y ayuda a capacitar a empleados con menos experiencia sobre las políticas de la empresa, los procedimientos, las prácticas de seguridad en el trabajo, los métodos de trabajo aprobados y las normativas de OSHA.

  • Repara daños menores a la propiedad que ocurran en el lugar de trabajo. Informa al General Foreperson de las situaciones que requieran atención, de forma oportuna.

  • Introduce maleza (brush) y residuos en la astilladora.

  • Coloca señales de advertencia, barreras, banderas, transmite señales manuales, dirige el tráfico y utiliza otros dispositivos de control de tráfico según corresponda, para proteger a los empleados y al público de los peligros en y alrededor del área de trabajo. Coopera con los propietarios, clientes y personal de emergencia cuando sea necesario bloquear calles o entradas.

  • Realiza inspecciones de vehículos y equipos para garantizar su correcto funcionamiento. Efectúa el mantenimiento rutinario de los vehículos, equipos y herramientas de la empresa. Informa al General Foreperson. sobre las necesidades de mantenimiento especializado de los vehículos o equipos.

  • Durante emergencias o desastres naturales, puede ser necesario permanecer de servicio durante la duración del evento.

  • Apoya, participa activamente y actúa de acuerdo con la cultura de seguridad y de propiedad de empleados de Wright.

  • Cumple con las leyes, normas y reglamentos federales, estatales y locales aplicables; mantiene el conocimiento y cumplimiento de todas las políticas y procedimientos de la empresa.

  • Mantiene una asistencia regular y puntual al trabajo y a las reuniones.

Otras funciones:

  • Conduce y opera los vehículos y equipos asignados.

  • Puede asistir en la obtención de permisos escritos de los propietarios de las propiedades. Ayuda a promover y mantener buenas relaciones con clientes, público y empleados.

Funciones de supervisión:

Conocimientos, habilidades y aptitudes requeridas:

  • Conocimiento de los árboles, incluyendo su identificación, hábitos de crecimiento y técnicas de arboricultura específicas para la poda, el mantenimiento, la reparación y la eliminación de árboles en proximidad a conductores energizados.

  • Excelentes habilidades de atención al cliente y comunicación, centradas en la creación de relaciones, la escucha activa, la formulación de preguntas y la paciencia. Capacidad para comunicarse eficazmente con el público, los clientes y los empleados.

  • Conocimiento y comprensión de American National Standards for Tree Care Operations (las Normas Nacionales Estadounidenses para Operaciones de Cuidado de Árboles - ANSI Z133.1 – versión vigente) y de American National Standards for Proper Pruning (las Normas Nacionales Estadounidenses para la Poda Adecuada - ANSI A300).

  • Capacidad para cumplir y capacitar a los empleados sobre los requisitos de seguridad de la empresa y del sector.

  • Conocimientos sobre circuitos eléctricos y habilidad para leer e interpretar planos de circuitos.

  • Conocimiento de las normas de generación, transmisión y distribución de energía eléctrica de OSHA, incluido el artículo 1910.269 del Título 29 del Código de Reglamentaciones Federales (CFR). Capacidad para determinar el voltaje nominal, usar correctamente herramientas aisladas cerca de partes energizadas y distinguir las partes vivas expuestas de otras partes del equipo eléctrico.

  • Capacidad para aprender rápidamente y seguir instrucciones con precisión.

  • Capacidad para comunicarse con otras personas y representar a Wright Tree Service de manera profesional.

  • Capacidad para comprender o leer y escribir tanto las instrucciones laborales como la información de seguridad, en forma escrita y verbal.

  • Capacidad para reconocer plantas venenosas y adoptar las medidas preventivas adecuadas.

  • Debe ser capaz de llevar el equipo de protección personal (PPE) requerido.

  • Capacidad para trabajar jornadas prolongadas y realizar horas extras durante emergencias (incluidos feriados, fines de semana y trabajos por tormentas), estando sujeto a llamadas de emergencia.

  • Conocimiento y capacitación en rescate en árboles y con elevador aéreo (canasta).

  • Capacidad para operar y mantener todas las herramientas y equipos requeridos.

  • Capacidad para trabajar tanto de forma independiente como en equipo.

Requisitos de formación, certificación y experiencia:

  • Contar con un mínimo de 1 año de experiencia trabajando en equipos de poda o despeje de árboles, o haber completado con éxito las evaluaciones de habilidades correspondientes.

  • Se prefiere diploma de educación secundaria o equivalente, aunque no es obligatorio.

  • Debe contar con credenciales vigentes de resucitación cardiopulmonar (CPR), o poder obtenerlas en un plazo de 90 días tras la contratación.

Otros requisitos preferidos:

  • Capacidad para obtener y mantener una licencia de conducir válida o una licencia comercial (según la división y los requisitos del cliente o contrato) y una tarjeta médica emitida por el Department of Transportation (Departamento de Transporte, DOT) conforme a las regulaciones de FMCSA.

  • Conducir un vehículo con una astilladora u otra unidad remolcada acoplada hacia, desde o dentro del área de trabajo.

  • Mantener la certificación o equivalente en aplicación de herbicidas según lo requieran Wright Tree Service y las leyes locales, estatales y federales.

  • Mantenerse informado sobre nuevos equipos, especificaciones, normas, prácticas y procedimientos operativos.

Características físicas:

Este puesto puede requerir las siguientes exigencias y actividades físicas:

  • Flexionarse, estirarse, permanecer de pie, caminar, trepar, levantar, cargar, sujetar, hablar, oír y realizar movimientos repetitivos de manera efectiva. Ocasionalmente alcanzar hacia arriba o hacia abajo.

  • Ejercer hasta 100 libras (45 kg) de fuerza ocasionalmente o hasta 50 libras (23 kg) de fuerza con frecuencia, o hasta 50 libras (23 kg) de fuerza de manera constante para mover objetos.

  • Poseer la capacidad para levantar, mover y maniobrar hasta 50 libras (23 kg) ocasionalmente y hasta 30 libras (14 kg) con frecuencia.

  • Debe tener agudeza visual suficiente para determinar la precisión, limpieza y exhaustividad del trabajo asignado o para hacer observaciones generales del entorno; agudeza visual cercana, como para leer una pantalla de computadora, materiales impresos, inspeccionar defectos pequeños o utilizar instrumentos de medición.

  • Poder entrar y salir de vehículos y equipos varias veces al día.

Factores ambientales:

Las personas en este puesto pueden estar expuestas a los siguientes factores:

  • Exposición habitual a condiciones de trabajo tanto interiores como exteriores.

  • Exposición habitual a las condiciones meteorológicas, climáticas y de temperatura, como lluvia, calor, sol, frío y nieve.

  • Exposición habitual a la naturaleza, como plantas irritantes, insectos que pican o muerden, polvo, etc.; el puesto se desarrolla al aire libre en terrenos irregulares.

  • Exposición habitual a ruido, vibraciones, peligros laborales como la proximidad a piezas móviles, equipos mecánicos, vehículos en movimiento, equipos con motor de gasolina, corriente eléctrica, alturas, calor, productos químicos, espacios reducidos, pasillos o conductos estrechos, enfermedades transmisibles, patógenos de transmisión sanguínea, productos de limpieza, polvo, olores y diversos tipos de plagas.

Las funciones, responsabilidades y actividades pueden modificarse en cualquier momento, con o sin previo aviso.

Job Description

Scope of Position
The Senior Reimbursement Analyst position is responsible for intervention and follow-up on accounts that require clinical interpretation and analysis along the revenue cycle. Primary focus will be assuring precertification for outpatient procedures, and accounts that are rejected from the payers for a variety of reasons. This position requires a high level of clinical knowledge and the ability to use a work proficiently in the Integrated Health Information Systems (IHIS). In addition, this position provides support through education and communication to other departments such as MIM, PCRMs, Physicians, Nurse Practitioners, PAs, and other clinical personnel. This positions requires that the individual be able to identify trends and offers suggestions for process improvement to support avoidance of and recoupment of lost revenue.

Responsible for follow-up on rejected and denied claims using evidence based support and other documentation as needed. Works with Medical Information Management to ensure proper ICD10 and CPT4 coding are performed on each claim. Responsible for identifying trends in denials and providing education to clinical staff and managed care payers to reduce these denials; Gather all clinical and supporting evidence and submit to payers for pre-determination of off-label services and/or complex procedures and treatment modalities; Communicate status of pre-determination request to stakeholders; Educate clinical and other staff on off-label definitions and policies and requirements for authorization on other complex cancer treatment modalities; Provide clinical support to non-clinical pre-certification staff as needed. Must have a strong understanding of the disease implications, use of various treatment modalities, and expected outcomes.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience. 2 years of relevant experience required. 2-4 years of relevant experience preferred.

title: Clinical Documentation and Coding Denials Auditor
description:
Inova Health is looking for a dedicated Clinical Doc and Coding Denials Auditor to join the team. This role will be Full-time Monday through Friday, fully remote.

This position is eligible for remote work for candidates residing in the following states – VA, MD, DC, DE, FL, GA, NC, OH, PA, SC, TN, TX, WV.

Inova is consistently ranked a national healthcare leader in safety, quality and patient experience. We are also proud to be consistently recognized as a top employer in both the D.C. metro area and the nation.

Featured Benefits:

  • Committed to Team Member Health: offering medical, dental and vision coverage, and a robust team member wellness program.

  • Retirement: Inova matches the first 5% of eligible contributions – starting on your first day.

  • Tuition and Student Loan Assistance: offering up to $5,250 per year in education assistance and up to $10,000 for student loans.

  • Mental Health Support: offering all Inova team members, their spouses/partners, and their children 25 mental health coaching or therapy sessions, per person, per year, at no cost.

  • Work/Life Balance: offering paid time off, paid parental leave, flexible work schedules, and remote and hybrid career opportunities.

Clinical Doc and Coding Denials Auditor Job Responsibilities:

  • Independently reviews, evaluates, and resolves complex payer DRG denials and downgrades related to clinical validity, medical necessity, coding accuracy, and documentation integrity, utilizing advanced clinical, coding, and regulatory expertise to identify root causes and determine denial validity through analysis of clinical documentation, payer policies, published clinical references, and official coding guidelines.
  • Exercises independent judgment and direct decision-making authority regarding denial disposition, including acceptance, appeal, escalation, and performance of second and third-level appeals activities.
  • Conducts pre- and post- bill clinical documentation and coding audits of denied encounters utilizing Epic, Solventum Encompass 360, and other audit technologies.
  • Prepares complex appeal letters and supporting documentation utilizing clinical evidence, coding guidelines, regulatory requirements, and payer policy interpretation.
  • Represents the organization in payer peer-to-peer reviews and denial discussions and supports HIM senior leadership with denial analysis and trends for Joint Operating Committee (JOC) meetings and other reimbursement-related engagements.
  • Collaborates with CDI, Coding, Revenue Integrity, physician leadership, and CDI Physician Advisors to identify denial trends, reimbursement risks, documentation improvement opportunities, and denial prevention strategies.
  • Provides education and consultative guidance to physicians, coding professionals, CDI teams, and operational leadership regarding coding compliance, documentation integrity, clinical validation, and reimbursement optimization.
  • Utilizes reporting tools, work queues, and database applications to analyze denial outcomes, maintain audit documentation, and support operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Performs additional audit, educational, reimbursement integrity, and denial management responsibilities as assigned.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in nursing or a health information-related field
  • Experience: 7 years of recent CDI, DRG validation or coding audit experience in an acute hospital setting with clinician training as RN, BSN, NP, PA or MD, or non-clinical advanced degree in a healthcare-related field
  • Certification: Either CCS or CCDS is required

Behavioral & Mindset Expectations

• Customer-Centric Focus: A genuine passion for helping people, coupled with strong communication skills and emotional composure in a fast-paced environment.

• Self-Motivation & Initiative: A self-starter who identifies what needs to be done, prioritizes tasks independently, and takes pride in a job well done.

  • Build dashboards, reports, and data visualizations that communicate complex analytical findings to technical and nontechnical audiences within assigned areas

title: CRA I
description:
CRA I

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health
• We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
• We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
• We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

  • Performs site qualification, site initiation, interim monitoring, site management activities and close-out visits (performed on-site or remotely) ensuring regulatory, ICH-GCP and/or Good Pharmacoepidemiological Practices (GPP) and protocol compliance. Uses judgment and experience to evaluate overall performance of site and site staff and to provide recommendations regarding site-specific actions; immediately communicates/escalates serious issues to the project team and with guidance develops action plans. Maintains a working knowledge of ICH/GCP Guidelines or other applicable guidance, relevant regulations, and company SOPs/processes.
  • Verifies the process of obtaining informed consent has been adequately performed and documented for each subject/patient, as required/appropriate. Demonstrates diligence in protecting the confidentiality of each subject/patient. Assesses factors that might affect subject/patient’s safety and clinical data integrity at an investigator/physician site such as protocol deviation/violations and pharmacovigilance issues.
  • For the Clinical Monitoring/Site Management Plan (CMP/SMP): Assesses site processes
    Conducts Source Document Review of appropriate site source documents and medical records
    Verifies required clinical data entered in the case report form (CRF) is accurate and complete
    Applies query resolution techniques remotely and on site, and provides guidance to site staff as necessary, driving query resolution to closure within agreed timelines
    Utilizes available hardware and software to support the effective conduct of the clinical project data review and capture
    Verifies site compliance with electronic data capture requirements
  • May perform investigational product (IP) inventory, reconciliation and reviews storage and security. Verifies the IP has been dispensed and administered to subjects/patients according to the protocol. Verifies issues or risks associated with blinded or randomized information related to IP. Applies knowledge of GCP/local regulations and organizational procedures to ensure IP is appropriately (re)labelled, imported and released/returned.
  • Routinely reviews the Investigator Site File (ISF) for accuracy, timeliness and completeness. Reconciles contents of the ISF with the Trial Master File (TMF). Ensures the investigator/physician site is aware of the requirement of archiving essential documents in accordance with local guidelines and regulations
  • Documents activities via confirmation letters, follow-up letters, trip reports, communication logs, and other required project documents as per SOPs and Clinical Monitoring Plan/Site Management Plan. Supports subject/patient recruitment, retention and awareness strategies. Enters data into tracking systems as required to track all observations, ongoing status and assigned action items to resolution.
  • For assigned activities, understands project scope, budgets, and timelines; manages site-level activities / communication to ensure project objectives, deliverables and timelines are met. Must be able to quickly adapt, with the oversight of the Lead CRA, to changing priorities to achieve goals / targets.
  • May act as primary liaison with project site personnel, or in collaboration with another CRA or Central Monitoring Associate (CMA). Ensures all assigned sites and project-specific site team members are trained and compliant with applicable requirements.
  • Prepares for and attends Investigator Meetings and/or sponsor face to face meetings. Participates in global clinical monitoring/project staff meetings (inclusive of Sponsor representation, as applicable) and attends clinical training sessions according to the project specific requirements.
  • Provides guidance at the site and project level towards audit readiness standards and supports preparation for audit and required follow-up actions.
  • For Real World Late Phase, the CRA I will use the business card title of Site Management Associate I. Additional responsibilities include:
    Site support throughout the study lifecycle from site identification through close-out
    Knowledge of local requirements for real world late phase study designs
    Chart Abstraction activities and data collection
    Collaboration with Sponsor affiliates, medical science liaisons and local country staff

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or RN in a related field or equivalent combination of education, training and experience
  • Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice/ICH Guidelines and other applicable regulatory requirements
  • Must demonstrate good computer skills and be able to embrace new technologies
  • Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to manage required travel of up to 75% on a regular basis
  • US ONLY: As part of your employment with Syneos Health, you may be deployed to Sites that require certain medical and other personal information to gain facility access. Are you a visual storyteller with an eye for detail and a knack for seamless execution?

Ziprent (a subsidiary of TurboTenant) is looking for a independent contractor (1099) Real Estate Photographer & Field Operations Specialist to be our eyes and ears on the ground. This isn’t just about snapping a few photos; it’s about crafting the digital first impression for our rental properties and ensuring every home is "rent-ready" through meticulous property walkthroughs and technical setups.

In this role, you’ll serve as a vital link in our growth engine, transforming empty spaces into high-performing listings. You’ll work independently to manage everything from 3D tours and high-fidelity photography to smart lockbox installations and condition reporting. If you love the freedom of the road and have a "tech-forward" approach, we want to talk to you.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Visual Storytelling: Deliver 15–25+ professionally edited, high-quality interior and exterior photos that make our listings pop.
  • Immersive Tech: Capture Zillow 3D tours and digital floor plans using a 360° camera to provide prospective tenants with a "true-to-life" experience.
  • Property Stewardship: Perform initial property walkthroughs and submit comprehensive condition reports to ensure our high standards are met.
  • Operational Logistics: Take the lead on key management, including the pick-up, installation, and battery maintenance of smart lockboxes.
  • High-Velocity Response: Maintain a "Be Better" mindset by responding promptly to new assignments and ensuring a 24-hour turnaround on all reports and deliverables.
  • Territory Mastery: Serving our local community and surrounding region, with a willingness to travel a 35–50+ mile radius to support our expanding market.

Qualifications:

  • Proven Experience: A strong real estate photography portfolio showcasing your ability to capture spaces effectively.
  • Tech-Savvy Toolkit: Professional gear including a high-quality wide-angle lens and a 360° camera compatible with Zillow.
  • Editing Expertise: Advanced photo editing skills to ensure every shot is polished and professional.
  • Mobile Proficiency: An updated mobile device capable of capturing clear, detailed images for on-site walkthrough reports.
  • Collaborative Spirit: Excellent written communication skills and a professional demeanor when representing the Ziprent/TurboTenant brand.
  • Reliability: A valid driver’s license, a reliable vehicle, and a flexible schedule to handle multiple shoots per month.

Bonus SuperPowers:

  • Compliance Knowledge: Familiarity with FHA and housing compliance (smoke alarms, CO detectors, etc.).

  • Tech Comfort: You have a "can-do" attitude when it comes to learning new property management software.
  • AI-Native Workflow: You use modern tools to streamline your editing or reporting process for maximum efficiency.
  • Hyper-Detail Oriented: You notice the small things—from a loose door handle to a flickering light—that others might miss.

Our "Be Better" Culture:

At TurboTenant, we live by the Be Better mantra. Our high-performance culture makes us relentless in our efforts to Be Better at serving our landlords and renters, and in unlocking the potential in one another.

What does our Be Better culture mean to you?

  1. You’ll be in an environment that pushes you to reach your potential.

  3. You’ll be on the highest performing team of your career.

At TurboTenant, we simplify the complex and intimidating process of managing your own rental property. And we do it through an elegant software platform for small, “do-it-yourself” landlords and their tenants. But don’t take our word for it. Read reviews from some of our 1 million landlords.

title: Principal Software Architect
description:
About Analog Devices

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at and on LinkedIn and X.

Principal Software Systems Architect

Data Center Platforms


The Opportunity

The rapid expansion of AI and cloud computing is transforming the data center.


Analog Devices is searching for a Principal Software Systems Architect to help define the next generation of embedded software and system architectures for data center infrastructure.


This is not simply a software implementation role. It is an opportunity to work at the intersection of silicon, embedded computing, software, power, sensing, communications, security, and large-scale infrastructure.


You will partner with analog, digital, firmware, software, systems, applications, and product teams to turn complex customer problems into scalable product architectures. You will influence products from their earliest architectural decisions through implementation and deployment.


We are looking for an engineer who is curious by nature, passionate about engineering across disciplines, and energized by problems that don't fit neatly within one technical domain.


You should expect to be challenged. You should expect to challenge others. And you should have the technical credibility and leadership skills to inspire teams to accomplish things that initially appear difficult.


What You’ll Do

Define System and Software Architecture

  • Define embedded software and system architectures spanning devices, platforms, and applications.
  • Translate customer and system requirements into clear hardware/software architectures and engineering requirements.
  • Establish clear architectural boundaries and interfaces among hardware, firmware, algorithms, communications, security, telemetry, configuration, and higher-level software.
  • Drive architectural decisions early in product development, when those decisions have the greatest impact on capability, schedule, cost, reuse, and differentiation.
  • Design for portability and scalability so that software and architectural investments can extend across products and product generations.

Turn Architecture into Products

Architecture is valuable only when it produces results.

You will:

  • Provide technical leadership across teams, challenge assumptions constructively, mentor engineers, and build alignment around critical architectural decisions.
  • Convert ambiguous customer and system problems into concrete technical architectures.
  • Drive tradeoffs involving performance, reliability, security, memory, compute, interfaces, cost, and development complexity.
  • Establish interfaces and architectural contracts that enable multiple engineering teams to execute in parallel.
  • Identify technical risks and critical dependencies early and use analysis, modeling, experimentation, and prototypes to resolve them.
  • Drive decisions to closure and take ownership for results.
  • Apply sound business judgment to architectural decisions, balancing innovation and differentiation with schedule, cost, risk, and customer value.

What We’re Looking For

Technical Depth

The successful candidate will bring substantial experience in several of the following:

  • Embedded systems and software architecture
  • C/C++ and low-level embedded software
  • Real-time and bare-metal systems
  • Microcontrollers and heterogeneous compute architectures
  • Hardware/software co-design
  • Device drivers and hardware abstraction
  • Communications protocols and system interfaces
  • Distributed embedded systems
  • Configuration, telemetry, diagnostics, and fault management
  • Embedded security
  • Software platforms and APIs
  • System integration, validation, and debug

A successful Software Systems Architect must combine deep software expertise with a broad understanding of the underlying hardware and system architecture to recognize cross-domain dependencies and make sound architectural tradeoffs.


Why This Role Matters

Data-center infrastructure is entering a period of significant architectural change.


As a Principal Software Systems Architect, you will work where multiple technologies converge, help make architectural decisions that shape future products, and work alongside engineers across disciplines to turn those decisions into real systems.


If you are passionate about understanding how complex systems work, willing to venture outside the boundaries of your own expertise, and motivated by turning difficult customer problems into successful products, we want to hear from you.

As such, applicants for this position – except US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) – may have to go through an export licensing review process.

title: Engineer, Manufacturing
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

As a Manufacturing Engineering Specialist at Shred-Tech, you will play a key role in optimizing manufacturing operations, supporting new product introductions, and driving continuous improvement initiatives across the organization. You will be responsible for developing, evaluating and implementing efficient manufacturing processes, workflows, equipment layouts and production methods that enhance quality, productivity, safety, and cost-effectiveness.

Working closely with cross-functional teams including Engineering, Production, Quality, Supply Chain and Operations, you will lead process improvement initiatives, support engineering change implementation and contribute to the successful execution of strategic manufacturing projects. The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise with project management capabilities, a proactive problem-solving mindset and a passion for operational excellence.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support new product introductions by identifying and implementing optimal manufacturing methods, tooling, equipment and assembly processes.
  • Analyze existing manufacturing processes to identify opportunities for improving efficiency, quality, throughput, safety and cost performance.
  • Develop, validate and continuously improve manufacturing processes by applying knowledge of product design, fabrication techniques, assembly methods, tooling, materials and production systems.
  • Design and optimize workflow, facility layouts, space utilization and equipment arrangements in collaboration with cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Lead the planning and implementation of process improvements, machinery upgrades, equipment installations and production system enhancements.
  • Coordinate the execution of Engineering Change Notices (ECNs), ensuring timely and effective implementation of both internal and customer-driven design changes.
  • Develop and maintain process documentation, work instructions, standard operating procedures and best practices to ensure consistent execution and knowledge retention.
  • Collaborate effectively across multiple departments to support production goals, resolve technical challenges and improve operational performance.
  • Lead or participate in special projects focused on manufacturing excellence, productivity improvement, capacity expansion and operational optimization.
  • Proactively identify project risks, manufacturing constraints and improvement opportunities, communicating recommendations and mitigation strategies to management.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives utilizing Lean Manufacturing, root cause analysis and problem-solving methodologies to reduce waste, improve productivity and enhance product quality.
  • Monitor and evaluate manufacturing performance metrics, implementing corrective actions and process enhancements where required.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Management, or related field.

Experience

  • Minimum 3 - 7 years of progressive experience in manufacturing environment in a custom engineered, industrial equipment, modular assemblies.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision making skills.
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, fabrication, assembly methods, tooling and production systems.
  • Experience with process improvement, workflow optimization, facility layout planning and production efficiency initiatives.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and work effectively in a fast paced manufacturing environment.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams.
  • Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement and root cause analysis methodologies is considered an asset.
  • Experience within metal fabrication, heavy equipment, industrial machinery or related manufacturing environments is preferred.
  • Proficiency in interpreting engineering drawings, specifications and technical documentation.

Specific Skills, Ability, and Knowledge

  • Strong knowledge of structural steel fabrication, welding, machining and mechanical assembly processes.
  • Familiarity with relevant industry standards and regulations.
  • Experience in CAD design, SolidWorks 3D preferred.
  • Proficiency with the Autodesk Suite.
  • Experience MS Office software (Word, Excel, Visio)
  • Experience in an integrated ERP system environment, Epicor preferred.
  • Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment with attention to details.
  • Willingness to engage in customer issues and troubleshoot as needed to drive resolution.

This opportunity is an existing role.

title: Director, Member Lifecycle and Personalization
description:
Job Description

A bit about this role:


Devoted grew from 212,000 members in December 2025 to more than half a million in September 2026. In 2027, we’ll serve Medicare beneficiaries across 34 states and 1,341 counties. Our engagement work already gets results: new-member digital engagement is up 30% year over year. Our next opportunity is precision—knowing each member well enough to reach them at the right moment, on the right channel, or to not contact them at all.


You’ll own member retention for members across AEP, members at risk of leaving, and preventing involuntary loss. You’ll also build the shared capabilities that every engagement journey runs on: experimentation, decisioning, and contact governance across SMS, email, push, in-app, mail, and outbound phone. The leaders who own onboarding, clinical engagement, and MyDevoted are your partners, and they should move faster because of what you build.


This is a player-coach role. In your first quarter, you’ll write the first experiment plan, build a journey, and draft the first cross-journey contact policy. You’ll lead our engagement operations team. You’ll add the capabilities it needs next and move our work from hand-built programs to a system that composes, tests, and learns.


Engagement runs on Devoted’s own technology platform, the same one behind our growth, so you’ll have control over data, decisioning, and the member experience that off-the-shelf tools can’t offer. The journeys and channels are built. We need the leader who builds the intelligence that decides what each member needs next.


You’ll report to the Chief Experience Officer.


Responsibilities will include:

  • Testing, learning, and measurement strategy. You’ll assess where our testing, targeting, and decisioning capabilities stand today and set the plan to close the gaps. Then you’ll raise how many tests we run and how fast we act on them. That means holdouts across every channel; a decision rule set before each launch; and a clear recommendation on what scales, what changes, and what stops. You’ll keep a learning agenda that works with slow, noisy health outcomes and a once-a-year enrollment cycle.
  • Plan-year lifecycle (retention and renewal). You’ll own the member journey around the plan year. You’ll partner with our insights team so disenrollment learnings feed directly into our annual benefit design process.
  • Contact governance. You’ll build one view of every message a member receives and turn it into a user-centered, data-informed policy that systems enforce: frequency limits, suppression, quiet hours, and channel preferences across the health plan and medical group. You’ll do this in partnership with Legal, Compliance, and clinical leaders.
  • Decisioning. You’ll weigh each member’s competing needs (clinical, retention, and service) to decide what to send, on which channel, and when to send nothing. You’ll start with rules and add models where they earn their place.
  • Composable content. Work with content team to operationalize hand-built campaigns into a small set of durable pieces that can be combined and tested across more than 700 plan variations.
  • Team leadership and operations. You’ll lead our engagement operations and content team and own the reliability, compliance, and quality of everything it ships. You’ll develop its leaders, hire for what we need next, and set the operating rhythm as the work shifts from hand-built to system-driven.


Required skills and experience:

  • You’ve built experimentation or personalization programs for consumers.
  • You’ve owned a consumer metric end to end and moved it.
  • You’ve built and grown a team, including hiring leaders.
  • You’re a player-coach. You can design an experiment and defend its statistics, challenge an engineering estimate, and rewrite a message yourself.
  • You’ve used emerging technology to materially improve engagement work, and you have good judgment and curiosity/experience about AI evaluation, human oversight, and where deterministic rules work better than models.
  • You have 10+ years of experience, including leading leaders.

Desired skills and experience:

  • Consumer subscription, fintech, consumer health, or marketplace businesses where retention is the business model
  • Healthcare, insurance, financial services, or other regulated, trust-dependent environments
  • Experience on either side of engagement platforms: running lifecycle or CRM programs on them, or building them

The Specialist is a member of the Technology Support team responsible for reliable, client-service-driven audiovisual support for meetings, events, presentations, trainings and other multimedia activities in the office, virtually and, when required, offsite. The Specialist prepares and operates meeting room and event technology, supports rehearsals and live programs, responds to AV support requests, troubleshoots common technical issues and collaborates with the broader team to deliver seamless communication and collaboration experiences.

title: Research Radiology Technician
description:

Job Category:

Job Profile:

Radiology Technician

Job Summary:

The Swallowing and Salivary Bioscience Laboratory (SSBL) offers a unique opportunity for a credentialed Radiologic Technologist to support cutting-edge dysphagia and swallowing research in a collaborative academic environment. This position combines advanced fluoroscopic imaging responsibilities with clinical research activities and is ideal for candidates interested in imaging science, research, and evidence-based patient care.


The primary responsibility of this role (approximately 80%) is to operate a C-arm fluoroscopy system during human subjects research visits, ensuring high-quality videofluoroscopic swallowing studies (VFSS), participant safety, and compliance with radiation safety standards and research protocols. The remaining 20% of duties involve supporting clinical research operations, including participant recruitment and study visits, and videofluoroscopic image analysis. The successful candidate will work closely with investigators, speech-language pathologists, and research staff to advance innovative research aimed at improving the assessment and treatment of swallowing disorders.


  • This position is full or part-time, 60%-100%
  • This position requires work to be completed onsite, at a designated campus work location.
  • Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m.- 4:30 p.m.
  • This position has been identified as a position of trust. The selected candidate will be required to pass an initial caregiver check to be eligible for employment under the Wisconsin Caregiver Law and every four years.

Candidates who demonstrate the following knowledge, skills, and abilities will be given first consideration:


  • Strong organizational, analytical, and documentation skills
  • Familiarity with clinical research regulations (e.g., IRB protocols, human subjects protections)

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Follows prescribed techniques in administering general and specific x-rays, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or other radiologic scanning procedures. Adjusts equipment, determines proper voltage, current and desired exposure time, arranges immobilization and support devices to obtain position of patient/participant, adjusts lead shields to protect unaffected parts of the patient's/participant's body, adjusts cone to direct concentration of rays on specific area, and selects proper film
  • Prepares, assesses, and observes patient/participant for procedures and possible reactions or outcomes
  • Transports patients/participants within department, to and from waiting area, as required
  • Processes images, film, and/or other scanning documentation in accordance to guidelines and photographic technique. Performs quality control activities to ensure optimal quality radiographs
  • Troubleshoots and reports equipment problems to supervisor
  • Cleans and disinfects patient/participant rooms and equipment to maintain highest quality safety and cleanliness standards
  • Recruit and enroll research participants by conducting outreach, screening for eligibility, obtaining informed consent, and coordinating participant scheduling in accordance with study protocols.
  • Lead research study visits by guiding participants through study procedures, collecting and documenting study data, performing protocol-required assessments, and ensuring compliance with research protocols and regulatory requirements.
  • Performs analysis of videofluoroscopic swallow study images to derive metrics as study outcomes
  • Performs radiologic procedures as assigned adhering to prescribed techniques

Department:

School of Medicine and Public Health, Department of Medicine, Division of Geriatrics and Gerontology, Swallowing & Salivary Bioscience Laboratory


Fueled by innovation yet grounded in kindness, the Department of Medicine empowers leaders to transform medicine and improve lives everywhere.   • Credentialed Radiologic Technologist with fluoroscopy training (e.g., ARRT certification or equivalent)
  • Eligible for or currently holding appropriate Wisconsin licensure to operate fluoroscopy equipment
  • Demonstrated experience operating radiologic or fluoroscopic imaging equipment
  • Experience working with human research participants or in a clinical/research setting

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with research, swallowing physiology, or videofluoroscopic swallowing studies
  • Experience analyzing imaging data for research purposes
  • Experience interacting with older adults and persons with cognitive impairment
  • Experience with scheduling in a clinical or research setting

title: Life Science Specialist, Pacific Northwest (WA, OR, ID, MT)
description:
The Opportunity:

Avantor is seeking a Life Science Specialist to support customers across Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Montana. This field-based role combines scientific expertise with commercial acumen to help researchers, laboratories, and life science organizations identify solutions that advance their work. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted technical resource, partnering closely with customers and internal sales teams to drive adoption of Avantor's Life Science portfolio.

This position is responsible for promoting the full Life Science product portfolio, with particular emphasis on bioMarke suppliers and strategic growth initiatives. Working alongside sales representatives, business development teams, and strategic partners, you will leverage your scientific background to identify opportunities, solve customer challenges, and support business growth throughout the territory.

This is a customer-facing role, with an expectation of meeting with customers 5 days per week. Candidates should be located within the Northwest territory, with preference given to individuals residing near the Seattle, WA or Portland, OR metropolitan areas.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Biology, Chemistry, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Microbiology, or another scientific discipline, or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Minimum of 4 years of laboratory, research, industry, or scientific applications experience
  • Demonstrated hands-on laboratory experience and the ability to independently troubleshoot scientific workflows, instrumentation, or experimental challenges
  • Experience supporting one or more life science disciplines, including genomics, proteomics, cell biology, cellular sciences, or microbiology
  • Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to translate complex scientific concepts for a variety of audiences
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel throughout the assigned territory

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous sales, field applications, scientific consulting, business development, or customer-facing experience
  • Experience supporting life science purchasing decisions, vendor management, or product evaluations
  • Master's degree, MBA, or other advanced scientific degree
  • Experience working within a distributor, manufacturer, CRO, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, academic, or healthcare research environment
  • Demonstrated success supporting revenue growth, account expansion, or strategic customer initiatives

Who You Are

  • A scientifically curious professional who enjoys solving problems and helping customers achieve their research goals
  • A proactive self-starter who can effectively manage a large geography with limited day-to-day supervision
  • An effective communicator who builds credibility with scientists, researchers, procurement teams, and business stakeholders
  • A collaborative partner who thrives in a matrixed environment and can influence across multiple teams
  • Organized and disciplined in territory planning, account management, and opportunity prioritization
  • Adaptable and motivated by identifying opportunities, developing solutions, and delivering measurable results

How You Will Thrive and Create an Impact

  • Serve as the technical expert for Avantor's Life Science portfolio across the Northwest territory
  • Partner with sales representatives, business development teams, and strategic partners to identify, develop, and close new business opportunities
  • Deliver product demonstrations, scientific consultations, and application-focused support that help customers evaluate and implement solutions
  • Build relationships with researchers, laboratory leaders, procurement stakeholders, and key decision-makers across academic, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, healthcare, and industrial environments
  • Promote the value and capabilities of Avantor's bioMarke supplier network and broader Life Science offerings
  • Collaborate with regional sales leadership to execute territory growth strategies and support key account initiatives
  • Provide market intelligence, competitive insights, and customer feedback to help inform commercial and portfolio strategy
  • Support onboarding and development of newer Life Science Specialists and contribute to sharing best practices across the organization

Why Avantor?

Dare to go further in your career. Join our global team of 14,000+ associates whose passion for discovery and determination to overcome challenges relentlessly advances life-changing science.

The work we do changes people's lives for the better. It brings new patient treatments and therapies to market, giving a cancer survivor the chance to walk his daughter down the aisle. It enables medical devices that help a little boy hear his mom's voice for the first time. Outcomes such as these create unlimited opportunities for you to contribute your talents, learn new skills and grow your career at Avantor.

title: Freelance Information Security Officer  (ISO)
description:
Who we are

At OpenUp, our mission is to make mental well-being accessible to everyone. Following a ‘high tech & high touch’ approach, we support companies, their employees, and their families with proactive and practical mental health services. Through our digital platform, clients can access 1:1 check-ins, online courses, articles, videos, group sessions, mindfulness practices, and a team of committed mental well-being experts. As we believe that mental and physical well-being are deeply connected, we have also added Lifestyle Experts to our offering, focusing on nutrition, exercise, and sleep. We offer a truly holistic approach that helps people take ownership of their health. We’re proud to work with forward-thinking organizations and are committed to raising the bar on accessible care.

OpenUp was ranked in the Top 3 on LinkedIn’s Top Startups list for 2023, 2024 & 2025 and is continuously growing. We are expanding our international teams and we are searching for like-minded talent. We are already serving 2000+ companies (e.g. Rituals, Deloitte, Decathlon, KPMG, and McDonalds), through which 600K+ employees have access to our product.

The role

  • ISMS ownership: own ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and NEN 7510:2024 end to end, the policy set, Statement of Applicability, risk register and the annual revision cycle.
  • Audit & certification: prepare for and steer internal and external audits, and drive corrective actions to closure.
  • Enterprise security assurance: own security due-diligence questionnaires (DDQs), vendor assessments and the security sections of enterprise RFPs, for new deals and renewals.
  • Cloud security governance: govern our Azure posture (Defender for Cloud, vulnerability management, logging, private networking) and turn gaps into a prioritised action list for engineering and hold remediation SLAs. You govern and review; Platform Engineering builds.
  • AI governance: build and own our AI governance framework, and review AI features (AI coach, AI-assisted session notes) for data protection, consent, human oversight and model risk.
  • AI assurance readiness: lead ISO/IEC 42001 and EU AI Act readiness.
  • Incident & continuity: oversee incident management, the data-breach protocol, and business-continuity / disaster-recovery testing.
  • Risk management: mature our risk process toward ISO 31000 alignment.

What you'll bring (must-have)

  • 6+ years in information security, with hands-on ownership of an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS through external audits, not just participation.
  • A track record of owning enterprise security due-diligence / DDQs.
  • Enough Azure cloud-security knowledge (Defender for Cloud, Entra ID, Key Vault, networking, managed identities) to govern and challenge architecture. You do not need to be a cloud engineer, but you cannot be a paperwork-only compliance officer either.
  • Strong policy-writing, and the ability to translate controls into practical engineering actions.
  • Excellent written and asynchronous communication, and real comfort in a distributed, cross-cultural team.
  • Pragmatic, outcome-oriented and comfortable with ambiguity.
  • ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Auditor or Lead Implementer certification.

A strong plus (differentiators)

  • Familiarity with AI/LLM systems and AI governance frameworks (ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 23894).
  • NEN 7510 or other healthcare / high-sensitivity data experience.
  • CISSP, CISM or CIPP/E; AI-governance training such as AIGP.
  • Secure-development background (OWASP, SAST/SCA, supply-chain hardening).

Next steps

Excited about this role at OpenUp? We love to learn more about you. Send us your application through our website and we will be in touch with you soon.

At OpenUp, everyone is welcome to apply - regardless of color, age, gender, nationality or any other label. Our hiring decisions are based on indiscriminate objective measures. We embrace what makes you unique and we believe that a diverse team is crucial to success. If you are ready to OpenUp, join us!

At OpenUp, everyone is welcome to apply regardless of age, gender, background, nationality, or any other characteristic. What matters to us is high performance, a real drive to make an impact and the ambition to become the European market leader. If you're ready to OpenUp, join us!

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to streamline parts of our recruitment process. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgement. All hiring decisions are made by humans. If you would like more information about how we use AI in the process, please contact us.

description:

title: College Completion Manager
description:
Position Overview:
The College Completion Manager is a shared services role within the College Access & Completion Department. This position builds the strategy, tools, trainings, coaching structures, and KPI systems that help regional teams guide students from senior year of high school through college graduation. Regional teams own direct student support; the College Completion Manager builds the infrastructure that helps them do that work well — across senior advising, college matriculation, persistence, community college transfer, and degree completion.

Responsibilities include:

  • Own and continuously improve IYT's national college completion framework, defining student milestones and implementation standards from senior year through college graduation and career activation.
  • Connect senior advising, matriculation, persistence, transfer, graduation, and career activation into one coordinated pathway; define national requirements, regional responsibilities, handoffs, and allowable local adaptations. Lead the national onboarding and stand-up process for regions launching or expanding college completion programs, including readiness assessments, implementation timelines, staffing and role guidance, operating procedures, service standards, data setup, and launch checklists.
  • Build and maintain the standards, trackers, and regional implementation guidance for senior advising, including college applications, FAFSA/CADAA completion, admissions decisions, intent to enroll, orientation, placement, and registration; monitor adoption and data quality.
  • Establish summer melt prevention timelines, outreach protocols, escalation pathways, and enrollment verification systems; train regional teams and monitor implementation and results without assuming direct student outreach.
  • Set national persistence milestones, tiered support standards, referral and escalation procedures, and monitoring guidance for first-semester and year-to-year support; analyze trends and regional implementation gaps.
  • Lead the national community college transfer strategy and implementation infrastructure, including educational planning, counselor connections, pathway selection, transfer applications, outcome verification, and regional performance monitoring.
  • Establish graduation readiness standards and tracking tools for degree audits, credit completion, advisor connection, graduation applications, and verified degrees; build a graduation-to-alumni transition process and a sustainable pipeline of IYT college graduates for alumni leadership opportunities.
  • Build the infrastructure for a volunteer-supported Career Mentor Program serving college students in years 3–6 and aligned to Year 3 Career Activation. Define the service model, mentor recruitment and screening, onboarding, training, matching, student self-service access, participation standards, safeguards, escalation procedures, and outcomes tracking so volunteers can provide career-related support with minimal routine staff involvement.
  • Develop and operationalize IYT's national Alumni Board model and scalable playbook, including charter and governance standards, member eligibility and selection, onboarding, roles, meeting processes, regional representation, leadership succession, and a graduate-to-Board recruitment pipeline.
  • Serve as IYT's staff liaison and representative at Board meetings; provide organizational context and monitor effectiveness while the alumni Chair and Vice-Chair own meeting agendas, facilitation, member engagement, and Board-led decisions.
  • Design and deliver practical training, implementation resources, onboarding, coaching, and technical assistance for regional staff and designated volunteer or alumni leaders. Guide regional leaders through college completion program launch milestones, confirm staff readiness and use of required systems, and provide structured post-launch support until the region can independently operate to national standards.
  • Lead the design, rollout, monitoring, and evaluation of college completion program pilots, including persistence, transfer, career activation, and degree completion initiatives. Define pilot goals, success measures, roles, timelines, reporting, and decision points; use evidence to recommend refinement, scaling, or discontinuation.
  • Partner with Research & Evaluation and Salesforce/Data teams to establish reliable dashboards and reporting for enrollment, summer melt, persistence, transfer, degree completion, alumni leadership pipeline, Alumni Board participation, and Career Mentor engagement; interpret trends and track corrective actions.
  • Independently manage national deliverables from planning through implementation and evaluation; maintain realistic milestones, clear owners, timely communication, high-quality work products, and risk escalation. Establish launch-readiness criteria and monitoring routines for new regional college completion programs; track implementation fidelity, data quality, service adoption, early outcomes, and corrective actions. Coordinate with regional leaders to remove barriers and document measurable improvement without substituting for regional direct-service responsibilities.
  • Additional duties as assigned

Schedule:

  • Monday-Friday, 8:30am-5pm, some weekends, evenings and organization-wide events are required.

Pay Rate:

  • $75,000 - $90,000/Year

Benefits:

  • Benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, Life AD&D, Voluntary Life AD&D, EAP and a 403(b) retirement with 3% employer match after one year of employment. We also offer 2 weeks of accrued paid vacation and additional paid time off for school breaks.

Location:

  • National HQ (Sacramento, CA) with regular travel to regional offices and school sites across California.

title: Software Engineer I (TypeScript, React, AWS, AI-Assisted Development)
description:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers is seeking a Software Engineer I to join our organization as we grow and transform our Technology landscape. Individual will complete intermediate end to end engineering tasks for specific system assignments including developing, analyzing, configuring, testing, debugging, troubleshooting, documenting, health monitoring/alerting, and implementing based on user or system design specifications, as well as participating in troubleshooting, conducting impact analysis and escalating appropriately. Applicants must be authorized to work for ANY employer in the U.S. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT, for this role.

  • Work within guidelines set by team to independently tackle well-scoped problems.
  • Seek opportunities to expand technical knowledge and capabilities.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Four or more years of programming/development experience, preferably in a Full-Stack software engineering role including AI-Assisted Development.
  • Experience developing modern web applications using JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, and React.
  • Experience with cloud-based development and deployment, preferably using AWS.
  • Familiarity with Agile delivery practices, including working in sprints, participating in team ceremonies, and contributing to iterative software delivery.
  • Experience using or interest in leveraging AI-assisted development tools, such as Claude Code or similar AI coding tools, to improve productivity, code quality, and development efficiency.
  • Experience with .NET is a plus.

  • Problem Solving - Proven problem-solving skills including debugging skills, allowing you to determine the source of issues in unfamiliar code or systems; recognize and solve repetitive problems rather than working around them; recognize mistakes and use them as learning opportunities; and break down large problems into smaller, more manageable ones.
  • Communication - Strong communication skills with the ability to clearly and concisely interact with team members, document work in a clear, easy-to-follow manner, collaborate well with team members, take in well-scoped requirements and ask the right questions to ensure clarification, seek out and receive constructive criticism well, and listen when others are speaking.
  • Leadership - Intermediate leadership skills with a proven track record of self-motivation in identifying personal growth opportunities.

What is a Must Have?

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, related STEM field, or its equivalent in education and/or work experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members – including spouses, domestic partners, and children – are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

title: Salesperson
description:
Job Description

What is a Salesperson?

Entry level sales position capable of supporting the DIY business and achieve our sales and service objectives. The role has good knowledge of store systems, basic automotive system knowledge and basic part knowledge. The role has the basic ability to source from stores, hubs, pdq, and external suppliers. The role has in-depth knowledge of the store inventory and maintenance processes. Position can be part time or full time. Fleet safety certification preferred.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide excellent selling experience for DIY customer visits and phone calls
  • Achieve personal sales goal and help store achieve its sales goals
  • Provide DIY services including battery installation, testing, wiper installs, etc.
  • Maintain store product and operational standards
  • Responsible for inventory processes including truck put away, shoot outs, cycle counts, Back stock, etc.

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Store Cleanliness including floors, bathrooms, facing, dusting, parking lot
  • General stocking including truck stocking and back stock
  • Safely deliver parts to customers as needed

Success Factors

  • Basic driving and navigation ability
  • Ability to use delivery board system
  • Friendly communication
  • Ability to locate and stock parts
  • Safety knowledge and skills
  • Operating inventory systems and store equipment
  • Parts and automotive system knowledge skills
  • Operating POS and Parts lookup systems
  • Expert at testing and diagnostic equipment for DIY service

Essential Job Skills Necessary for Success as a Salesperson

  • Speak and write English (Spanish a plus); communicate effectively and build strong relationships with customers, peers and management
  • Read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, parts catalogs, and procedure manuals
  • Use basic math accurately: add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals
  • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings, and weekends as needed

Prior Experience that Sets a Salesperson up for Success

  • 2-3 years of successful sales experience in a diverse retail environment, providing superior customer experiences

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is usually working inside; however, they will occasionally be outside and exposed to various weather conditions while performing such tasks as installing batteries and wiper blades. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

We comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws.

The good faith estimate for this role is between 15.00 USD and 16.13 USD per hour for a new team member.

title: Commercial Pest Technician
description:
Benefits Start Day 1 for Full-Time Colleagues - No Waiting Period!

For more information about our benefits, see below!

We are proud to be a member of the Rentokil family of companies, the global leader in Pest Control and other services across more than 90 countries. We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to many of the world's leading brands and serve consumer and business customers across multiple industries. We are extremely proud of our legacy of excellence and constantly work to fulfill our mission to "protect people, enhance lives, and preserve the planet."

What do our Pest Control Technicians do?


The primary purpose of this role is to perform our industry leading pest management services for commercial customers. You will be responsible for identifying and eliminating pests from residential properties by conducting thorough inspections, determining the type of pest infestation, applying appropriate treatments like pesticides and traps, and providing preventative measures to prevent future infestations, all while adhering to safety regulations and communicating with clients about pest control solutions.


Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:

  • Conduct thorough inspections of client properties to identify signs of pest infestations, damage, and entry points
  • Apply approved pest control products, including chemicals, baits, and traps, to effectively eliminate pests while adhering to safety standards
  • Educate customers on pest prevention methods and the importance of maintaining a pest-free environment. Provide advice on how to reduce the risk of future infestations.
  • Build relationships with customers, schedule and confirm their appointments, help with sales to current customers, and expand our product to new customers
  • Ensure that all pest control equipment is properly maintained, stocked, and in good working condition
  • Adhere to all local, state, and federal regulations regarding pest control products and safety protocols
  • Drive and safely operate a company provided service vehicle (we provide routine maintenance)

Essential Job Functions:

  • Working in tight, confined spaces such as basements, attics, crawl spaces, narrow aisles, or passageways
  • Working around animals, insects and termites
  • You’ll sometimes be working around mechanical parts, vehicles, electrical current, heights and scaffolding, fumes, dust, and chemicals, and we’ll train you how to handle all of these conditions safely
  • Able to work both inside and outside in your local climate in company-provided weather gear
  • Lots of moving around — regularly sitting, climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling, up and down stairs, ladders, scaffolding, ramps, and poles
  • You’ll need to wear personal protective equipment (PPE), like an OSHA-compliant respirator

What do you need?

  • Clean shaven face- for safety reasons (rebreathers have to be able to seal your face)
  • High school diploma or GED; related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Possess a valid driver’s license from state of residence.
  • Licenses/certificates as required by federal, state, and/or local regulations (covered by us)
  • Available to work Monday-Friday and weekends as needed
  • Open to learning and becoming knowledgeable in all areas of pest control
  • Solid reading, writing, and verbal communication skills
  • Basic math skills — You’ll need to be able to follow instructions for mixing on product labels
  • Customer-facing experience preferred

Pay Range

Hourly: $17.00 - $23.00

Why Choose Us?

A career with the Rentokil family of companies can be a professional trajectory filled with opportunity. We pride ourselves on being a world-class team that rewards high performance, and we love to promote from within. We offer competitive pay and many of our roles offer performance incentives.

Below you'll find information about some of what we have to offer. All Full-Time Colleagues qualify for the following and Part-Time Colleagues qualify for most benefits after they meet certain criteria.

This company is a Drug Free workplace.

Rentokil is committed to complying with all Federal, State, and local laws related to the employment of qualified individuals with disabilities.
