title: Clinical Pharmacy Specialist-GI
description:
The Clinical Services Pharmacist II is responsible for providing clinical pharmacy services to patients in GI oncology and will work closely with physicians, mid-level providers, nurses, and pharmacists to provide comprehensive patient care for outpatients. The Clinical Services Pharmacist II will also be responsible for counseling patients starting new intravenous and/or oral antineoplastics; performing clinical assessments; performing adherence and toxicity checks for patients on active therapy; answering drug-information questions; reviewing chemotherapy orders for select providers prior to patients going to infusion; and assisting with drug access.

To learn more about why you should join the Pharmacy Department at Dana-Farber, please copy and paste the link below into your browser:
https://careers.dana-farber.org/division-of-pharmacy.html

Located in Boston and the surrounding communities, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is a leader in life changing breakthroughs in cancer research and patient care. We are united in our mission of conquering cancer, HIV/AIDS, and related diseases. We strive to create an inclusive, diverse, and equitable environment where we provide compassionate and comprehensive care to patients of all backgrounds, and design programs to promote public health particularly among high-risk and underserved populations. We conduct groundbreaking research that advances treatment, we educate tomorrow's physician/researchers, and we work with amazing partners, including other Harvard Medical School-affiliated hospitals.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Practices as a pharmacist in accordance with all federal, state, DFCI and Joint Commission policies, regulations, and standards.
2. Ensures medication orders and/or prescriptions for appropriateness, accuracy and completeness based on patient-specific parameters and clinical data.
3. Provides clinical consultation and evidenced based recommendations for treatment plans, supportive care, dose adjustments and monitoring plans to clinicians regarding pharmacotherapy needs for patients based on literature, clinical practice guidelines and institutional standards.
4. Collaborates as a member of the pharmacy and interdisciplinary team through patient care related meetings including rounds, huddles, and case conferences as applicable.
5. Provides comprehensive education to patients and caregivers receiving oncology related therapy including participation in the oral anticancer education program and review and maintenance of patient education materials.
6. Documents clinical care activities in the EHR and effectively communicate all changes in care plan to the staff involved in patient care.
7. Participates in scholarly and educational activities according to departmental expectations (e.g., in-services, drug use evaluation, resident precepting, clinical research, quality/process improvement, presents continuing education programs, guideline development).
8. Participates in clinical administrative duties such as pathways, beacon validation and active patient management, formulary request process and presentation to P&T committee(s), evaluate off label/exception review, REMS programs and other departmental or strategic initiatives.
9. Participates in the development of policies, procedures, teaching documents, education and/or monitoring tools, workflow design, and other initiatives that will improve and/or expand the program.
10. Other duties and projects as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

• Ability to effectively communicate both orally and in writing with others inside and outside the department (i.e., patients, providers, other institutions).
• Ability to effectively work within a collaborative team-focused environment.
• Ability to use all technology required to perform primary job functions.
• Ability to prioritize and adapt to changes; accepts additional responsibilities based on the changing needs of the work setting.
• Ability to accurately assess drug therapeutic appropriateness based on patient-specific parameters and clinical data.
• Ability to utilize references and/or drug information sources.
• Ability to demonstrate critical thinking skills (ability to analyze information objectively and make a reasoned judgement).
• Ability to resolve common problems within their scope of practice and to escalate appropriately when needed.

Minimum Job Qualifications:

The Clinical Services Pharmacist II must meet the following requirements to be hired and maintain their position in the Pharmacy Department at DFCI.

Minimum Education:
All Pharmacists require a Bachelor of Science in Pharmacy or Doctor of Pharmacy degree from an accredited college of Pharmacy.

Minimum Experience:
PGY2 residency in area of specialty (preferred) or PGY1 plus 2 years of clinical specialist experience (such as oncology, palliative care, anticoagulation) or 5 years of clinical specialist experience (such as oncology, palliative care, anticoagulation) required.

License/Certification/Registration Required:

Must be licensed to practice pharmacy in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Pharmacists must attain board certification in their specialty area within 18 months of employment.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

None

Patient Contact:

Yes

At Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, we work every day to create an innovative, caring, and inclusive environment where every patient, family, and staff member feels they belong. As relentless as we are in our mission to reduce the burden of cancer for all, we are committed to having faculty and staff who offer multifaceted experiences. Cancer knows no boundaries and when it comes to hiring the most dedicated and compassionate professionals, neither do we. title: Internal Wealth Specialist
description:
Discover your potential. Build your legacy.
Go the distance with Capital Group

At Capital Group, we go the distance — for our people, our clients, and each other. As a global, privately held firm with more than 95 years of history, we believe meaningful careers, like meaningful investing, are built over the long term. That’s why we invest in our associates with the same conviction we bring to our clients — through career growth, purpose-driven work, whole-person wellness, and rewards that recognize your contributions. Here, you’ll find the opportunity, global scale and support to unlock your potential and build a career that lasts.


The Role


As an Internal Wealth Specialist, you’ll build and retain consultative relationships with financial professionals in an assigned territory, identify opportunities to bring Capital Group solutions to their clients, and help drive territory sales. You’ll conduct complex advisor conversations and partner closely with external wholesalers to develop and execute territory plans. By combining thoughtful coverage, market insight, and consistent follow-through, you’ll help create long-term value for advisors and the investors they serve.


The Team


You’ll join Capital Group’s Regional Sales Office, a collaborative organization of more than 300 associates that brings together internal sales, operations, and innovation. The team supports financial professionals through long-term, consultative partnerships and works closely with external wholesalers, marketing, and product partners. In this role, you’ll support two external wholesalers, step in for advisor calls and meetings when needed, and help mentor and coach Internal Wealth Generalists.


Your Impact


  • Partner with external wholesalers to build and execute territory sales plans that strengthen advisor relationships and support growth and retention.
  • Conduct outbound and complex sales calls with financial advisors to promote relevant solutions, generate leads, and schedule meetings.
  • Provide timely insights on Capital Group products, capital markets, portfolio construction, practice management, and the retirement landscape.
  • Maintain accurate client interaction, pipeline, and sales activity records in Salesforce to support disciplined territory management.
  • Analyze territory business intelligence and advisor engagement to identify opportunities and inform strategic planning.
  • Collaborate with marketing and product teams to deliver targeted campaigns and messaging for assigned territories.

What You’ll Bring

  • Current Securities Industry Essentials (SIE) at the time of application.
  • Ability to obtain the Series 7 and Series 66 licenses after hire if not already held; a Series 6 or Series 7 at application is strongly preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to build relationships with colleagues and external clients.
  • Working knowledge of investment concepts and products, with interest in capital markets, industry trends, competitor offerings, and regulatory changes.
  • Exceptional organization, time management, and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Collaborative judgment and the ability to work effectively with sales teams and financial advisors while operating independently when needed.


What you’ll get
When you go the distance for our clients, we go the distance for you. You’ll grow through mentoring, leadership programs and tuition reimbursement, and do work that matters at a firm managing $3T+ in AUM for millions of investors worldwide. We invest in your whole life too – with comprehensive wellness and mental health support, family-first benefits, competitive pay with performance and profitability bonuses and a company-funded retirement plan. description:
It's a great feeling to work for a company that does so much good for others around the world!

Make a difference every day with an organization dedicated to doing good and caring for others.

Compass Connections believes every child deserves to have a place where they feel safe and loved. Our organization offers emergency shelter and group home placement for children while we work to reunite them with family.

We know the sooner family reunification is accomplished, the sooner children can safely integrate into the community and thrive.

We are now hiring compassionate and dependable individuals to join our team at our (facility) in (city, state).

ALL Benefits available on the first day of employment.

  • 100% employer-paid medical, dental, vision insurance
  • Retirement plan options
  • Additional employer sponsored benefits available

Ask your recruiter for a complete overview of the benefits available to you.


Hourly Rate: $23.26 an hour.


Language Requirement: Fluency in English and Spanish is required.


Academic Req: Required – High school diploma, or equivalent; Preferred – 2-year associate degree from accredited program/institution, or two or more years of college-level course work in a related human services field


Certifications: First aid, CPR, Emergency behavior intervention


Work experience: Required – 1-year employment experience in the child welfare field working with children and/or adolescents in a social service setting and/or training in a related human services
field; Preferred - 2 plus years’ related experience and/or training in a related human services field


Critical Action Items & Measurable Deliverables:

1. Meet all federal and state regulatory guidelines and standards that are applicable to this position.
2. Document all serious incidents, daily progress, and activities completely, accurately and in a timely manner and in compliance with agency policies and procedures.
3. Assist with orientation of new children and staff.
4. Provide input into development of treatment plans as appropriate or requested.
5. Use positive child management techniques including verbal redirection, de-escalation, and containment.
6. Plan, organize and supervise activities for children in accordance with the daily activity schedule.
7. Teach constructive behavior and social skills, realistic problem-solving behaviors, responsible time and money management, conversational English, personal hygiene, and life skills.
8. Assist children with homework assignments.
9. Maintain an orderly and clean children’s living area including assisting in the household and children’s laundry, overseeing daily chores, identifying routine maintenance work/repair, and reporting it to the Unit Manager.
10. Maintain and update records regarding children’s clothing and personal items.
11. Maintain a secure campus environment by making rounds as required, and by using proper application of radio communication protocols including responding to all radio calls.
12. Take actions to promote positive interaction between children and encourage children to take responsibility in the daily routine of the facility.
13. Model culturally and socially desired behaviors while explaining the behaviors to children to facilitate learning and replication of the behaviors.
14. Work evenings, weekends and holidays as needed or requested by position supervisor.
15. Implement Compass Connections safety protocols including evacuating with children and other staff in case of an emergency.
16. Maintain confidentiality in all areas of child and program operations.
17. Maintain Compass Connections professional and ethical standards of conduct outlined in Compass Connections employee handbook including demonstrating respect for agency staff, children, and community members and complying with required dress code at all times.


Other Responsibilities:

1. Provide sustained and uninterrupted direct supervision of the children assigned to the worker from the start of the assigned shift until relieved.
2. Follow the instructions of medical/clinical staff regarding each child and inform Unit Manager of information impacting the basic health and well-being of children assigned to the worker.
3. Communicate in a positive and respectful manner with children, families and all agency staff including supervisors, co-workers, therapists, student interns, and volunteers.
4. Frequently traverse from one area of the facility to another both indoors and outdoors as needed to provide direct supervision of children.
5. Effectively communicate behavioral expectations and program regulations to children and enforce compliance with regulations and expectations by all children assigned to the worker.
6. Complete all required documentation prior to completion of shift.
7. Meet all pre-determined deadlines required by program supervisor and federal partners.


Requirements:

1. Pass a pre-employment drug screen and random drug screens throughout employment.
2. Provide proof of work eligibility status upon request.
3. Pass a pre-employment and biennial criminal background checks.
4. Demonstrate the ability to:
a. Respond sensitively and competently to the service population’s cultural and socio-economic
characteristics.
b. Work collaboratively with other staff members, service providers and professionals.
c. Provide crisis intervention according to training provided by Compass Connections when needed to maintain a safe environment.
d. Work in a fast-paced environment and maintain emotional control and professional composure at all times.
e. Maintain computer literacy required to meet the responsibilities of the position.
f. Work effectively and without intensive supervision both independently and as a member of a multidisciplinary team.
5. Demonstrate a working knowledge of all Compass Connections policies and procedures.


Compass Connections is committed to following immunization recommendations produced by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control (CDC). As such, our company policy requires that all employees must receive an annual Influenza vaccination or obtain an approved exemption as a medical or religious accommodation. This is a condition of employment, and all new hires will be responsible for providing proof.

title: The North Face: Supervisor - Camarillo
description:
At The North Face we dare to lead the world forward through Exploration. We were born to Explore, Disrupt and to Lead. We were born to Love Wild Places and to Spark Curiosity. We believe that exploration is a mindset - both on the mountain and off the mountain - and it infuses everything we do. As a community of explorers, we stay curious about new ideas, places, and people.

So, before we get to the job details, take a minute to learn a little more about us – our values and our culture. If you can see yourself working side-by-side with a team of adventure-loving people, The North Face just may be the place for you.

To learn more about our values and our culture, visit The North Face Careers or .

Supervisor

What will you do?

A day in the life of a Supervisor at The North Face looks a little like this.

As a Supervisor, you play a key role in supporting the store’s leadership team and driving abets-in-class customer experience. You will lead by example, coach and develop associates, and ensure operational excellence across customer engagement, merchandising, and store standards. In partnership with the Store Manager and Assistant Store Manager, you will help maximize store profitability, foster an inclusive team culture, and contribute to the store’s success. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced retail environment, enjoys mentoring others, and is passionate about delivering exceptional service. Let’s break down that day-in-the-life a bit more.

  • Deliver a high level of personalized customer engagement through genuine interactions.​
  • Support the store team in achieving and exceeding sales goals by monitoring progress against key performance indicators, while also achieving individual goals.​
  • Model selling behaviors and foster a consumer-centric mindset through authentic customer interactions.​
  • Coach and develop associates to deliver high levels of customer engagement and meet productivity goals.​
  • Supervise daily store operations, including opening and closing procedures, floor coverage, and task delegation.​
  • Support stockroom operations by organizing inventory, processing shipments, and ensuring timely product flow to the sales floor.​
  • Assist in training and onboarding new team members; provide ongoing feedback and support.​
  • Maintain visual merchandising standards and ensure product replenishment aligns with brand directives.​
  • Support inventory integrity through proper shipping, receiving, and loss prevention practices.​
  • Promote community engagement by participating in local initiatives and events.​
  • Uphold company policies, safety standards, and operational procedures.​
  • Foster a positive and inclusive store environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and learning.

What do you need to succeed?

We all bring unique skills to work each day. For this role, there are foundational skills needed to succeed, along with 1+ years of retail or store leadership experience in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment​. A High School Diploma or equivalent is preferred; but we value hands-on experience and demonstrated achievements most.

The foundation skills you will need in this position are:

  • Proven ability to drive results through store teams and exceed sales and profit goals.​
  • Skilled in coaching, motivating, and building high-performing, diverse teams.​
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to influence across all levels.​
  • Solution-oriented and flexible in a fast-paced, dynamic retail environment.​
  • Capable of working independently, managing shifting priorities, and meeting business expectations.​
  • Comfortable using word processing, spreadsheets, and retail software tools.​
  • Ability to stand and move throughout the store for extended periods and perform physical tasks such as bending, reaching, squatting, climbing ladders, and lifting light to moderate weight, with or without reasonable accommodation.

title: Project Manager - EPMO
description:
Ultradent, a global name in oral health, is looking for an onsite EPMO Project Manager.

We're growing quickly, and with that growth comes real opportunity — and a lot of motion. We manage a wide range of projects — software implementations, process improvements, governance initiatives, and facilities projects among them — and no two look quite the same. Things move fast, and at the edges they can get messy. We're looking for someone who can step into that and create order: bring structure to the ambiguous, and turn "figure it out" into a clear plan. As a medical device company, we work within real requirements and quality expectations, so getting the details right matters as much as moving quickly.

We already have the framework, the processes, and the systems established. What we need is someone with the judgment to apply them proportionally — running lean where the risk is low, going deeper where it isn't — rather than running the full playbook on everything by default.

This is a full-time, in-office position, on a 9/80 work schedule (9 hours per day with every other Friday off). We value our team culture and believe collaboration and problem-solving thrive best in a shared, in-person environment.

What you'll do

  • Own projects end to end — scope, timeline, budget, and quality — from kickoff to close.
  • Build the plans, timelines, and milestones that fit the work in front of you.
  • Manage stakeholders across the department and the company — keeping people informed, aligned, and bought in.
  • Lead cross-functional teams, manage dependencies, and drive to outcomes.
  • Anticipate risks and clear roadblocks early, with minimal supervision.
  • Drive change management alongside delivery, and keep the work visible through clear, consistent reporting.

What you bring

  • Adequate experience to demonstrate proficiency with independently managing projects end to end is ideal. You bring the craft fully formed — we'll teach you our business.
  • Deep command of project management fundamentals, independent of any single method or tool. You scale the rigor to the risk.
  • Fluency with technology — including AI — to work faster and sharper, and an instinct to find a better way.
  • Excellent communication; you make complex work legible to any audience, from the shop floor to the C-suite.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred and 1-3 years of experience, or equivalent experience of 5+ years preferred.
  • CAPM, PMP, or similar a plus.
  • Experience in medical device manufacturing, supply chain, or QMS is a plus.

Who you are

  • You create order out of ambiguity. You're drawn to messy, undefined problems and energized by turning them into something structured and clear.
  • You own the framework — you don't just follow it. You have the confidence to make the call without waiting to be told.
  • People want to work with you. Much of what you deliver depends on colleagues across the company who are already stretched thin, and you earn their time through credibility and genuine rapport.
  • You care more about getting it right than being right. You test ideas early, learn fast from what doesn't work, and pull good thinking from whoever has it — you're not trying to be the smartest person in the room, you're trying to make the room smarter

Ultradent is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are a global culture where differences and perspectives are sought after, welcomed, and embraced. We consider all qualified applicants fairly, based on their experience, skills, and potential to contribute to our team. Our core values – Integrity, care, quality, innovation, and hard work- guide us daily. These values, when balanced, shape our workplace culture and ensure that we remain focused on our vision while maintaining a professional and inclusive environment.

title: Real Estate Photographer - Salt Lake City, UT
description:
Role Mission

Are you a visual storyteller with an eye for detail and a knack for seamless execution?

Ziprent (a subsidiary of TurboTenant) is looking for a independent contractor (1099) Real Estate Photographer & Field Operations Specialist to be our eyes and ears on the ground. This isn’t just about snapping a few photos; it’s about crafting the digital first impression for our rental properties and ensuring every home is "rent-ready" through meticulous property walkthroughs and technical setups.

In this role, you’ll serve as a vital link in our growth engine, transforming empty spaces into high-performing listings. You’ll work independently to manage everything from 3D tours and high-fidelity photography to smart lockbox installations and condition reporting. If you love the freedom of the road and have a "tech-forward" approach, we want to talk to you.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Visual Storytelling: Deliver 15–25+ professionally edited, high-quality interior and exterior photos that make our listings pop.
  • Immersive Tech: Capture Zillow 3D tours and digital floor plans using a 360° camera to provide prospective tenants with a "true-to-life" experience.
  • Property Stewardship: Perform initial property walkthroughs and submit comprehensive condition reports to ensure our high standards are met.
  • Operational Logistics: Take the lead on key management, including the pick-up, installation, and battery maintenance of smart lockboxes.
  • High-Velocity Response: Maintain a "Be Better" mindset by responding promptly to new assignments and ensuring a 24-hour turnaround on all reports and deliverables.
  • Territory Mastery: Serving our local community and surrounding region, with a willingness to travel a 35–50+ mile radius to support our expanding market.

Qualifications:

  • Proven Experience: A strong real estate photography portfolio showcasing your ability to capture spaces effectively.
  • Tech-Savvy Toolkit: Professional gear including a high-quality wide-angle lens and a 360° camera compatible with Zillow.
  • Editing Expertise: Advanced photo editing skills to ensure every shot is polished and professional.
  • Mobile Proficiency: An updated mobile device capable of capturing clear, detailed images for on-site walkthrough reports.
  • Collaborative Spirit: Excellent written communication skills and a professional demeanor when representing the Ziprent/TurboTenant brand.
  • Reliability: A valid driver’s license, a reliable vehicle, and a flexible schedule to handle multiple shoots per month.
  • Location: You must live within 35 miles of the market area to be considered for this role.

The role requires completion of a background check and signing of an independent contractor agreement.

Bonus SuperPowers:

  • Compliance Knowledge: Familiarity with FHA and housing compliance (smoke alarms, CO detectors, etc.).
  • Efficient Workflow: You stay ahead of the curve by leveraging modern tools and smart processes to streamline documentation, reporting, and day-to-day tasks—maximizing productivity without sacrificing quality.
  • Tech Comfort: You have a "can-do" attitude when it comes to learning new property management software.
  • AI-Native Workflow: You use modern tools to streamline your editing or reporting process for maximum efficiency.
  • Hyper-Detail Oriented: You notice the small things—from a loose door handle to a flickering light—that others might miss.

Our "Be Better" Culture:

At TurboTenant, we live by the Be Better mantra. Our high-performance culture makes us relentless in our efforts to Be Better at serving our landlords and renters, and in unlocking the potential in one another.

What does our Be Better culture mean to you?

  1. You’ll be in an environment that pushes you to reach your potential.
  2. You’ll make a massive impact on our landlords, renters, company, and the proptech industry.
  3. You’ll be on the highest performing team of your career.

About Us:

At TurboTenant, we simplify the complex and intimidating process of managing your own rental property. And we do it through an elegant software platform for small, “do-it-yourself” landlords and their tenants. But don’t take our word for it. Read reviews from some of our 1 million landlords.

Quantity of Jobs:

Number of job requests varies by market region. This is a contracted 1099 position, and requests are sent out on an as-needed basis. Most markets average 3 –10+ jobs per month.

Candidates should be flexible and comfortable with limited assignments initially while the market and workload grow.

Compensation

    • $225–$325+ per listing appointment (varies based on property size and scope)
      • Includes: professionally edited photos, Zillow 3D tour, floor plan, initial walkthrough report, and lockbox installation with key management
    • $50/hour for additional as-needed tasks
    • Lockbox Pick-Up:
      • $30–$60 per lockbox (depending on distance)
    • Travel Compensation:
      • Paid for travel exceeding 35 miles each way (70 miles round trip)
      • Reimbursed at $1.20 per mile beyond this threshold

Salary Range
$1—$100,000 USD

Additional Information

TurboTenant is proud to serve a diverse group of landlords and renters. We strive to reflect that diversity within our team. Employment at TurboTenant is based on merit, competence, performance, and business need. TurboTenant celebrates being an equal opportunity employer and never discriminates based on race, color, genetic information, religion, national origin, sex, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), age, or any other basis protected by law.

At this time, employer-based visa sponsorship is not available. All candidates must be eligible to work in the United States without sponsorship.

This is a classified position and reports to the Children and Family Services Division Director. The incumbent performs duties under general supervision, and provides supervision directly over a staff of professional, para-professional, and support employees.


Minimum Qualifications:

A Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in behavioral or social sciences, three years of professional experience in a problem-solving court program, court, child welfare, substance abuse treatment or mental health treatment fields, and at least one year of progressively responsible lead or supervisory duties OR any equivalent amount of experience, training and/or education approved by Human Resources.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience/knowledge of dependency court processes, substance use disorders, treatment approaches, and available community resources.

Essential Duties & Functions:

  • Oversees comprehensive grant management, ensuring compliance, and implementing data-driven decision-making. Grant management encompasses grant administration, grant submission and reporting/evaluation requirements, performance monitoring, compliance oversight, contract management, subrecipient monitoring, and budget oversight.
  • Manages operational and grant budget planning, implementation, and oversight.

  • Coordinates referrals to any contracted service, acts as a liaison between FTC and the service providers; tracks outcomes of service participants.
  • Leads the FTC Leadership Advisory team comprised of contract attorneys, DCS representatives, service providers, and staff to address Family Treatment Court issues and processes.
  • Interacts with the Family Treatment Court and/or provides training to judges, staff, court management, clients, DCS, community partners/providers, attorneys, and the public to explain Treatment Court programs and services, resolve program, service or client issues, develop program improvements, and maintain a focus on program results.

Additional Responsibilities/Duties:

  • Maintains awareness of current issues in the treatment court, family treatment court, substance abuse, dependency, and child welfare field and attends professional conferences/trainings as assigned.
  • Develops and prepares informational materials, news releases, and other media materials to inform and market the family treatment court programs and services.
  • Performs special assignments as assigned by the Division Director.
  • Performs other related work duties and projects as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • The principles, practices, methods and techniques of effective program administration and management;
  • The principles, practices, methods and techniques of effective grant administration and management;
  • Applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations governing the judiciary, treatment court programs, and grants.
  • Court and treatment court structures and organizations, functions, performance measures, best practices, and services;
  • Strategic planning principles and practices;
  • undefined

  • Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing;
  • Computer and technological skills to utilize and lead implementation of court technology and databases to administer and evaluate FTC;
  • Communicate effectively with staff employees, court administration and management, judges, government and community agency representatives, community leaders, Administrative Office of the Court officials, and the general public.

Must have a valid Arizona Driver License at time of appointment.

Typically performs duties in an office environment and may lift materials and/or equipment 20 pounds or less. This position will require some driving.

title: Maintenance Admin
description:
The Maintenance Admin supports the Maintenance Department by coordinating and maintaining administrative processes, documentation, records, purchasing activities, maintenance data, and departmental performance indicators.

This position ensures that maintenance information is accurate, organized, and available to support preventive and corrective maintenance activities, regulatory compliance, equipment reliability, cost control, and continuous improvement. The Maintenance Admin also provides administrative support for maintenance projects, calibration activities, utilities tracking, contractors, suppliers, and other departmental initiatives.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provide administrative support to the Maintenance Manager and Maintenance Department.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance records, reports, work orders, and departmental documentation.
  • Support the administration and tracking of preventive and corrective maintenance activities, including open work orders, completion status, and outstanding maintenance items.

  • Support the control and updating of maintenance procedures, work instructions, equipment manuals, technical documentation, and departmental forms.

It's fun to work in a company where people truly believe in what they are doing. At Dutch Bros Coffee, we are more than just a coffee company. We are a fun-loving, mind-blowing company that makes a difference one cup at a time.

title: Product Manager, Cross-Border Bill Pay
description:
Product Manager, Cross-Border Bill Pay


At Western Union, we’re transforming the way people make payments across borders, creating seamless, accessible, and reliable financial experiences for customers around the world.

As our Product Manager, Cross-Border Bill Pay, you’ll play a key role in developing and enhancing our international bill payment capabilities. You’ll be responsible for driving product initiatives from discovery through delivery, identifying opportunities to simplify payment journeys, improve customer experiences, and deliver solutions that meet evolving market needs.

Working closely with engineering, technology, and cross-functional business teams, you’ll translate customer insights and business priorities into actionable product strategies, supporting Western Union’s continued innovation in global payments.


Role Responsibilities

You will be responsible for managing product capabilities across the full development lifecycle, from initial discovery and solution design through testing, launch, and ongoing optimization. You will work collaboratively with stakeholders to define product priorities, coordinate delivery, and ensure solutions align with customer needs and business objectives.

  • Define and execute the product strategy and roadmap for Cross-Border Bill Pay, aligning priorities with customer needs and business objectives.
  • Own the end-to-end product lifecycle, including discovery, solution design, development, testing, launch, and continuous improvement.
  • Develop and maintain a 12-month product roadmap, identifying opportunities for innovation, modernization, and product enhancements.
  • Translate customer insights, market research, and business requirements into actionable product initiatives and development priorities.
  • Partner with engineering and technology teams to deliver scalable, reliable, and customer-focused payment solutions.
  • Lead product backlog prioritization, requirements definition, user story reviews, and release planning within an Agile development environment.
  • Collaborate with regional teams and business stakeholders to understand market requirements, dependencies, and opportunities across international payment markets.
  • Evaluate competing priorities and make informed trade-off decisions based on customer impact, business value, technical feasibility, and resource availability.
  • Define and monitor product KPIs and OKRs, using performance data and customer feedback to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Support product testing, validate development outcomes, and ensure new capabilities meet agreed business and customer requirements.
  • Identify operational and product risks, implement appropriate mitigation strategies, and support compliance with relevant controls.
  • Work cross-functionally to resolve product incidents, address performance issues, and drive process improvements.
  • Conduct competitor benchmarking and research emerging payment technologies, market developments, and industry trends.
  • Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and partners to ensure alignment on product strategy, priorities, and delivery.

Role Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Business, Engineering, Technology, or a related field.
  • At least 5–7 years of Product Management experience within financial services, preferably payments.
  • Experience managing payment products, digital financial services, or transaction-based platforms.
  • Knowledge of cross-border payments, international bill payments, payment processing, or related financial services would be advantageous.
  • Demonstrated experience managing the end-to-end product development lifecycle, from initial discovery through launch and optimization.
  • Strong understanding of Agile development methodologies, product roadmaps, backlog management, and release planning.
  • Experience translating customer needs and business requirements into product features and actionable development priorities.
  • Demonstrated project management skills, including planning, coordination, prioritization, adaptability, and execution.
  • Experience working closely with engineering, technology, and cross-functional business teams.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret product performance data, customer insights, and market trends.
  • Experience defining and tracking KPIs, OKRs, and product success metrics.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, identify risks, and make effective decisions in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with global teams and stakeholders across multiple regions.
  • Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. Western Union will not sponsor applicants for work visas for this position.

title: Product Manager, Trakstar and Compensation
description:
At Mitratech, we are a team of technocrats focused on building world-class products that simplify operations in the Legal, Risk, Compliance, and HR functions. We are a close-knit, globally dispersed team that thrives in an ecosystem that supports individual excellence and takes pride in its diverse and inclusive work culture centered around great people practices, learning opportunities, and having fun! Our culture is the ideal blend of entrepreneurial spirit and enterprise investment, enabling the chance to move at a rapid pace with some of the most complex, leading-edge technologies available.

For over 35 years, the experts at Mitratech have been focused on solving the complex needs. Today, we serve 20,000 client companies of all sizes globally, representing 30% of the Fortune 500 and over 500,000 users in over 160 countries.

As we continue to grow, we’re always looking for resourceful, enthusiastic, and fresh perspectives. Join our global team and see what makes Mitratech a truly exceptional place to work!

Due to business and compliance requirements, this position is open only to candidates residing in MEXICO. Applications from candidates located outside this region will not be reviewed.

About the role

Product managers at Mitratech are revenue engineers. You own how your products grow revenue and keep customers successful. You choose the capabilities that matter most, either because they help sales and renewals close or because they make customers more successful. You turn those choices into requirements engineering builds from, then work with customers, support, sales and engineering until the results show up in revenue and retention.

You report into the Product Management organization and work with a distributed engineering and design team across several countries.

What you will do

  • Find the revenue opportunity. Talk to customers and admins every week, read usage and satisfaction data, join win-loss and renewal reviews, and write down the problem with the revenue case behind it.
  • Work with sales and customer success to find where a missing capability costs deals or renewals, and decide what to build in response.
  • Keep the roadmap for your area current and explain what is on it, what is not, and the revenue reason for each choice.
  • Define the problem worth solving and the job the customer is trying to get done, with the evidence behind it. Give design and engineering a clear enough picture of the problem and the outcome that they know what to build and can tell when it works.
  • Plan releases with engineering, estimate effort together, and manage scope as the release moves.
  • Represent the customer in engineering, design, support and sales conversations.
  • Demonstrate what you are building to customers and to the wider organization, collect their feedback, and secure agreement from stakeholders before a release goes to market.
  • Give sales, support and customer success what they need to sell and support each release: positioning, demos and answers to the questions customers ask.
  • Define the metrics for your area (revenue, retention, adoption and customer satisfaction), report on them, and check each release against the revenue case you made for it.

What you bring

  • 5 or more years of product management experience, including at least 3 in business-to-business enterprise SaaS.
  • A record of shipping software that real customers use, and the artifacts to show how you worked: requirements, roadmaps, discovery notes, metrics.
  • Experience working with engineering teams across time zones.
  • A record of tying product decisions to revenue, retention or expansion, with the numbers to show it.
  • Comfort with product analytics and with turning data into a decision.
  • Written and spoken English at a professional level. You will write requirements and present in English every day.
  • A bachelor's degree in business, computer science, engineering, information systems, economics or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred

  • Experience in HR technology, such as performance management, learning, applicant tracking, compensation, payroll or HCM.
  • Experience adding AI-assisted features to an enterprise product.
  • An MBA or master's degree.
  • Familiarity with tools such as Jira and Productboard.

How Mitratech will assess the role

Mitratech's product management career path defines the Product Manager level as working independently on problem definition, discovery, release planning, stakeholder alignment, metrics and influence, and as developing the skills of strategy, pricing, negotiation and customer engagement. Interviews assess against those expectations.

We are an equal-opportunity employer that values diversity at all levels. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or veteran status.

title: Activity Supervisor
description:
1. Monitor and evaluate activity areas daily to ensure safety, engagement, and inclusivity. Ensure activity

lesson plans are consistent, age-appropriate, and adaptable for campers of all abilities. Maintain ACA

accreditation compliance and enforce camp policies in all activity areas. Adjust programming as needed in

and traditions, coordinating logistics and staffing to ensure smooth execution. Coordinate with the

rotations, and closing celebrations that highlight camper accomplishments.

title: Regulatory Specialist
description:
Overview

The Regulatory Specialist supports the regulatory management of clinical research studies from study start-up through close-out and archiving. This role prepares, maintains, tracks, and files essential regulatory documents; coordinates submissions and approvals with Sponsors, CROs, and IRBs; maintains accurate electronic regulatory records; supports monitoring visits and study close-out; and helps ensure site activities remain consistent with applicable regulations, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), study protocols, Sponsor requirements, and PhaseWell Research SOPs. The Regulatory Specialist partners closely with Principal Investigators, Sub-investigators, Clinical Operations, Clinical Research Coordinators, Quality Assurance, Patient Recruitment, Business Development, Marketing, Contracts/Finance, and external study partners to support compliant, inspection-ready study conduct.


Key Responsibilities

Study Start-Up & Regulatory Submissions

  • Receive and organize regulatory packages for new studies and maintain accurate study start-up tracking.
  • Coordinate and participate in study start-up meetings to ensure stakeholder alignment on regulatory deliverables and timelines.
  • Prepare, complete, route, and maintain required regulatory documents, including Form FDA 1572s, financial disclosures, delegation logs, investigator/sub-investigator CVs and licenses, study-level informed consent forms, IRB questionnaires, and applicable authorization forms.
  • Coordinate submission of recruitment and advertising materials for IRB approval in partnership with appropriate stakeholders.
  • Track regulatory documentation submission status, approvals, expiration dates, and required follow-up actions; communicate approvals and regulatory updates to relevant site personnel.
  • Ensure final, signed, and approved documents are promptly filed in the appropriate Investigator Site File.

Regulatory Maintenance & Compliance

  • Maintain complete, accurate, current, and inspection-ready Investigator Site Files throughout the study lifecycle.
  • Ensure that study team changes are quickly and appropriately reflected in the regulatory documentation (e.g., FDA 1572 updated when there is an investigator change).
  • Monitor investigator and study-team credentials, including CVs, medical licenses, training documentation, delegation logs, and related records. Request to receive updated documentation when needed.
  • Obtain PI signatures on IND safety reports, and other applicable safety/regulatory communications, in accordance with Sponsor requirements and PhaseWell Research SOPs and ensure that these documents are promptly filed in the appropriate Investigator Site Files.
  • Process and file protocol amendments, Investigator's Brochure updates, revised recruitment materials, revised informed consent forms, and other updated study-specific regulatory documents.
  • Create and maintain regulatory memos-to-file when appropriate. Ensure that the memos ‘tell the story’ completely and clearly, and that they are appropriately dated and traceable.
  • Protect confidentiality, integrity, version control, and accessibility of regulatory records and study information.

Monitoring/Auditing/Inspection Readiness, Close-Out & Archiving

  • Prepare regulatory files and support documentation for Sponsor monitoring visits and audits, internal audits, and Regulatory Inspections. Partner with Clinical Research Coordinators and study teams to facilitate timely resolution of regulatory document requests.
  • Support study close-out activities and ensure required regulatory documentation is complete before archiving.
  • Manage the archiving of closed-study records, including source, regulatory, and eCRF records, in accordance with applicable PhaseWell Research SOPs and Sponsor requirements.
  • Coordinate sponsor notifications and return/destruction of archived records only when permitted by the sponsor-specific Clinical Trial Agreement and PhaseWell Research SOPs.

Systems, Data Integrity & Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Maintain accurate study information and regulatory documentation in the site’s Regulatory platform (if applicable).
  • Ensure regulatory documents are complete, accurate, current, appropriately filed, and readily retrievable. Conduct and document routine Quality Control checks on regulatory documentation and any associated trackers.
  • Work effectively with Principal Investigators, Sub-Investigators, Clinical Operations, Clinical Research Coordinators, Quality Assurance, Patient Recruitment, Business Development, Marketing, Finance/Contracts, and Sponsor representatives.
  • Escalate missing documentation, compliance concerns, overdue actions, or other regulatory risks promptly to the appropriate leader.
  • Support continuous improvement of regulatory processes, documentation practices, and study start-up workflows.
  • Remain current on, and comply with, all regulations, GCPs, sponsor requirements, and SOPs, as they relate to regulatory documentation.
  • Provide guidance to study team members, and other company employees, regarding compliance with regulations, GCPs, sponsor requirements, and SOPs, as they relate to regulatory documentation.
  • Assist with the development and implementation of departmental training programs, including the creation of any associated employee knowledge assessments.
  • Assist with the assessment and management of company vendors (those that are hired to provide PhaseWell with goods and services that are related to regulatory documentation) to ensure that they consistently meet regulatory requirements and PhaseWell Quality standards.
  • May assist with sponsor audits and/or regulatory authority inspections (including preparation, participation, and follow-up) in accordance with company procedures.
  • Assist in the training and/or mentoring of other Regulatory department staff.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree (or equivalent relevant experience) in Business Administration, Communications, Clinical Research, Healthcare Administration, or a related field.
  • 2–4 years of experience in clinical research, regulatory affairs, research administration, or a related healthcare/research environment; site-level clinical research experience preferred.
  • Working knowledge of FDA regulations, ICH Guidelines, HIPAA, and other Good Clinical Practices.
  • Familiarity with FDA Form 1572, investigator qualifications, delegation documentation, financial disclosures, informed consent documentation, safety reporting, protocol amendments, and IRB submissions.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and SharePoint; experience with electronic regulatory systems and clinical trial software preferred.
  • Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to maintain accurate, complete, and inspection-ready documentation.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with investigators, clinical teams, Sponsors, CROs, IRBs, and other stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple studies, deadlines, and competing priorities.
  • Ability to maintain strict confidentiality of patient, employee, Sponsor, financial, and study information.
  • Ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment about when to ask questions and when to escalate regulatory or compliance issues.
  • Professionalism/professional standards (tactful, punctual, dedicated, reliable, trustworthy, ethical, etc.)

Location

  • On-Site Monday-Friday


Cultural Values Fit

  • Patients First — Protects participant rights, safety, dignity, and confidentiality by supporting compliant, high-quality clinical research and maintaining accurate regulatory records.
  • Hustle Harder — Takes ownership of regulatory deliverables, follows through on commitments, anticipates deadlines, and moves quickly to resolve documentation gaps and study start-up needs.
  • Authenticity, Always — Communicates openly and accurately, raises concerns promptly, and builds trust through transparency, accountability, and professionalism.
  • Serve with Joy — Brings a collaborative, service-oriented approach to supporting investigators, clinical teams, Sponsors, CROs, and colleagues; welcomes feedback and contributes to a positive team environment.
  • Excellence Together — Pursues high standards in regulatory compliance, documentation, data integrity, and inspection readiness while partnering across functions to deliver consistent, compliant study execution.

Other Duties

title: Onboarding & Ramp Manager
description:
About Us

AI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation.

The bottleneck now has moved from code generation to security and safety - AI agents write code faster than any team can review it, and over 65% of the lines of code produced by them are insecure. Vulnerabilities are piling up 16x faster than companies can fix them, and adversaries are able to exploit these new vulnerabilities within hours.

AURI by Endor Labs closes that gap. It runs inside the harness where coding agents work, through hooks, skills and MCP, so the controls sit outside the model and every agent action is visible. Underneath is our patented code context graph, which maps code, open source, containers and infrastructure. It shows which vulnerabilities can actually be reached and exploited, then delivers fixes that won’t break the application. Security teams get evidence instead of noise, and developers get fixes instead of tickets.

The companies building AI trust us to secure it - our customers include OpenAI, SpaceX, DoorDash, Dropbox, Atlassian, MongoDB, Snowflake, Robinhood and Peloton to name a few.

description:
Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally?


About Analog Devices

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at and on LinkedIn and X.


At ADI, you will learn from the brightest minds who are here to help you grow and succeed. During your internship, you will make an impact through work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts. Collaborating with colleagues in an environment of respect and responsibility, you will create connections that will become a part of your professional network.


ADI’s culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning opportunities, and shared rewards. The internship program features various lunch-and-learn topics and social events with other interns and full-time employees.


At ADI, our goal is to develop our interns so they are the first to be considered for full-time roles.


Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.


Analog Design Intern – CSS Power Management

Location: Catania, Italy


Job Description

Analog Devices is seeking an Analog Design Intern – Power Management to join our engineering team in Catania.


The successful candidate will join a collaborative team developing advanced low-power analog and power-management IP for highly integrated mixed-signal ICs. Working alongside experienced analog, mixed-signal and power-management engineers, the intern will contribute to real IC development activities while gaining practical experience in circuit architecture, transistor-level design, modelling, simulation and verification.


The team develops power-management solutions with a strong focus on low-power operation, high efficiency and small solution size. Key areas include switched-mode DC/DC converters such as buck, boost and buck-boost architectures, together with the analog building blocks required for their control, monitoring and protection.


This internship provides an opportunity to apply university knowledge to real silicon designs and develop an understanding of the complete IC development process, from architecture and modelling through circuit implementation, physical design, verification and potentially silicon evaluation.


Responsibilities

  • Conduct circuit architecture research and feasibility studies for low-power power-management functions.
  • Contribute to the architecture, design, simulation and verification of DC/DC converter IP, including buck, boost and buck-boost topologies.
  • Design and analyse analog sub-circuits used within power converters, potentially including error amplifiers, comparators, voltage/current references, oscillators, gate drivers, level shifters, current-sensing circuits and protection functions.
  • Develop simulation testbenches and contribute to design verification across process, voltage, temperature and operating-load conditions.
  • Analyse important converter performance trade-offs including efficiency, quiescent current, transient response, output ripple, stability, silicon area and external component requirements.
  • Explore different converter operating modes and control techniques to optimise efficiency across load conditions.
  • Contribute to behavioural and system-level modelling to evaluate converter architectures and control-loop performance.
  • Work closely with layout engineers during physical implementation, including review of parasitic effects and layout-dependent performance.
  • Participate in technical and design reviews with experienced analog and power-management engineers.
  • Support top-level integration and verification of power-management IP within larger mixed-signal systems.
  • Where appropriate, contribute to laboratory evaluation and comparison of simulated and measured silicon performance.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a BEng, MEng, MSc or PhD in Electronic/Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics or a closely related discipline.
  • Good understanding of fundamental analog electronics and circuit theory.
  • Understanding of CMOS devices and basic transistor-level circuit operation.
  • Familiarity with feedback systems, frequency response and stability.
  • Basic understanding of power electronics and switching circuits.
  • Some experience with circuit simulation or electronic design tools through university, personal or industry projects.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Enthusiasm for learning and working collaboratively within an engineering team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Understanding of DC/DC converter architectures, particularly buck, boost or buck-boost converters.
  • Familiarity with concepts such as PWM/PFM operation, feedback control, loop stability and transient response.
  • Familiarity with transistor-level IC design and tools such as Cadence Virtuoso and Spectre.
  • Exposure to power-converter modelling or simulation using tools such as SIMPLIS, MATLAB or Simulink.
  • Understanding of common power-management building blocks such as LDOs, voltage/current references, comparators, oscillators, current sensing and gate drivers.
  • Familiarity with low-power circuit-design techniques and quiescent-current optimisation.
  • Experience using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, power supplies, electronic loads and signal generators.
  • Programming or scripting experience using Python, MATLAB or similar tools for modelling, simulation or data analysis.
  • A strong interest in analog IC design, power management and energy-efficient electronic systems.

title: Staff Scientist I, Data Science
description:
A little about us:

The Lieber Institute for Brain Development (LIBD) was established in 2010 to plot a new course in biomedical research that would change the lives of individuals affected with developmental brain disorders. We are one of the only research institutions in the world focused specifically on understanding how genes and the environment influence the way our brains develop that lead to conditions such as schizophrenia, autism, bipolar disorder and related developmental brain disorders. Through our cutting-edge research, answers are emerging and being translated into a robust pipeline of new drugs in development. And, by focusing on genes and their dynamic interplay with the environment, we are getting even closer to the “holy grail” in medical research, the discovery of strategies for primary prevention.


We are a group of dedicated, multidisciplinary and optimistic researchers, working at the cutting edge of science, utilizing state-of-the-art tools to unlock the mystery of the brain and transform the way we approach the development of new treatments, and ultimately cures. LIBD is an independent 501(c)(3) medical research institute located in the Bioscience Park on the campus of the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine and Hospital in Baltimore, MD.


Job Summary:

A Staff Scientist position in computational biology and bioinformatics is available to work within the Neural Plasticity division at the Lieber Institute for Brain Development (LIBD). Our research investigates the molecular organization, development, and function of brain circuits involved in psychiatric disorders. We combine molecular profiling of postmortem human brain tissue with experimental mouse studies and human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) and organoid models to understand how distinct neuronal populations contribute to brain function and disease, with the goal of discovering novel therapeutic targets.


The successful candidate will lead analyses of single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and other multiomic datasets generated by our team and collaborators. This position offers opportunities to develop computational approaches, shape research questions, and work closely with experimental scientists to connect molecular findings with cellular organization, circuit function, and behavior.


Specific Duties and Responsibilities:

· Analyze and interpret large-scale genomic and multiomic datasets from human brain tissue, mouse and organoid models, and public resources.

· Develop and apply computational and statistical approaches to address research questions in neuroscience and psychiatric disorders.

· Develop and maintain reproducible analysis workflows, with responsibility for data quality, documentation, and organization.

· Prepare scientific figures, write and revise manuscripts, and contribute to grant applications in collaboration with research teams.

· Present research findings at team meetings and scientific conferences.

· Other duties as assigned.


Required Minimum Qualifications:

· Master’s Degree or higher (PhD Preferred) in Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Genetics, Neuroscience, or related field is required.

· A minimum of 2 years related experience.


Special Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

· Proficiency in Linux and programming with R or Python

· Demonstrated experience analyzing large-scale transcriptomic or other genomic datasets, particularly single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics data.

· Strong understanding of statistical analysis, including experimental design, regression or mixed-effects models, multiple testing, and sources of technical and biological variation.

· Familiarity with high-performance computing, version control, and reproducible analysis practices.

· Ability to independently develop analytical strategies, troubleshoot computational problems, and critically evaluate results.

· Expertise to ask and interpret biological questions underlying the data and ability to communicate findings clearly to colleagues with varied computational and experimental backgrounds is highly desired.

· Previous experience working on genomics datasets related to neuroscience or psychiatry is preferred but not required.


Physical Requirements:

· Incumbent is required to work in an office environment.

· Must be able to move about the office and campus as well as remain stationary for extended periods of time.

· Ability to continuously operate a personal computer for extended periods of time.

· Visual acuity as well as mental acuity sufficient to collect and interpret data, evaluate, reason, define problems, establish facts, draw valid conclusions, make valid judgments and decisions are required

· Ability to speak and hear well enough to communicate clearly and understandably with sufficient volume to ensure an accurate exchange of information in normal conversational distance, over the telephone, and in a group setting

· Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate a keyboard and other office equipment, use a telephone, access file cabinets and other items stored at various levels, including overhead

· Ability to lift or move objects up to 25 lbs.


** If accommodations are needed due to pregnancy or a disability, please contact jobs@libd.org


Compensation

Candidates are hired within the starting salary range for the position which is the lower portion of the overall range. The starting salary range for this position is $82k - $87k with opportunities for employee growth over time. Placement in the starting range is based on job-related skills and experience, as evaluated throughout the interview process.


Benefits

The Lieber Institute for Brain Development offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package to help us attract and retain the best talent. Please visit for more information.


EEOC Statement: At the Lieber Institute, we are committed to a work environment of mutual respect where employment decisions are based on merit. As an equal opportunity employer, the Lieber Institute does not discriminate in employment opportunities on the basis of race, color, religion, color, sex, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital status, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, disability (physical or mental), genetic information, military service, or other non-merit based factors protected by state or federal law or local ordinance, with regard to any position or employment for which the applicant or employee is qualified.


LIEBER INSTITUTE FOR BRAIN DEVELOPMENT'S COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION

The Lieber Institute for Brain Development is a transparent and collaborative community working to produce unique and imaginative patient-oriented solutions to developmental neuropsychiatric disorders. It is committed to integrating scientists from diverse disciplines, cultures, and countries into a research team that draws upon the best of its staff. The Institute is historic—it is defining a unique model for ground-breaking science. It values translational science that revolutionizes the field and improves the quality of life for those affected by mental illness. The Institute provides an environment that fosters independent growth through mentorship and a supportive, collegial community. Diverse minds, ideas, and talent are needed to support LIBD's mission. Fresh, innovative ideas and perspectives are a competitive necessity in an increasingly diverse and global marketplace. The success of the Institute's mission depends upon leveraging a diversity of talent.


The Institute's commitment to diversity goes beyond compliance with laws and regulations that promote equal employment opportunity, prohibit discrimination and harassment, and support minority and woman owned businesses. To realize the advantages of its diversity, it is necessary to work effectively together even when differences challenge us to consider ideas and methods that seem impractical or make us feel uncomfortable.

The Lieber Institute for Brain Development demonstrates its commitment to diversity by:


·Including others: Talent is not limited to those with a narrow set of industry and academic credentials. The Institute is committed to building diverse teams, inviting others to share their perspectives, seeking out a diversity of input when making decisions, questioning traditional thinking, and promoting continuous learning and development.

·Respecting one another: The Institute is committed to listening carefully to others, seeking consensus, engaging in active and constructive debate, thoughtfully challenging one another, and providing constructive feedback.

·Building trust: The Institute is committed to sharing information and resources, depending on one another to get things done, keeping promises, and conveying high integrity in all actions.

title: Broista – Buda, TX
description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly believe in what they are doing. At Dutch Bros Coffee, we are more than just a coffee company. We are a fun-loving, mind-blowing company that makes a difference one cup at a time.

At Dutch Bros Coffee, we are a fun-loving, mind-blowing company, making a massive difference one cup at a time.

As the face of Dutch Bros, you’ll connect with customers, hustle with heart, and bring positive energy onto every single shift.

  • Adaptable and quick; you can handle a rush and keep the kindness rolling.
  • Team-oriented and ready to support your crew, no matter what’s needed.
