title: Leaves & Accommodation Specialist
description:
About Wright Service Corp:

Wright Service Corp. is a prominent leader in several environmental services industries, providing integrated vegetation management, forest management and reforestation, technology solutions, environmental and agricultural sustainability consulting, commercial environmental services, residential and commercial landscaping, tree care, interior plantscaping, and other outdoor and indoor services.

The Wright family of companies includes Wright Tree Service®, Wright Outdoor Solutions®, Eocene Environmental Group℠, Eocene Environmental Group of the West, Wright Tree Service of the West, Wright Tree Service of Puerto Rico, Wright Canada Holdings, and commonly seen brands, such as Spectrum Resource Group, ArborCare and Verdure Elements.

Wright Service Corp. has been employee-owned since 2002 and headquartered in Central Iowa since 1933, when Wright Tree Service was founded by John L. Wright.

Job Summary: The Leaves & Accommodation Specialist is responsible for the administration and coordination of employee leaves of absence, workplace accommodation, and return-to-work cases. This position serves as a subject matter expert for federal, state, and local leave requirements and provides advanced guidance regarding leaves and the interactive accommodation process, including other Company leave policies.

The Leaves and Accommodation Specialist partners closely with employees, managers, Human Resources, Benefits, Legal, Payroll, third-party leave administrators, and other internal stakeholders to ensure leaves and accommodations are administered consistently, timely, and in accordance with applicable laws and Company policies. This position manages complex and escalated cases involving overlapping leave laws, return-to-work restrictions, extended and intermittent leaves, workplace accommodations, disability benefits, and state or local leave requirements.


Leaves Administration:


  • Administer and oversee employee leave programs, including the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), state and local family and medical leaves, military leave, parental leave, short-term disability, long-term disability, and other Company leave programs.
  • Serve as the primary contact for complex or sensitive leave cases and provide guidance to employees, managers, HR Business Partners, and Benefits team members.
  • Coordinate leave administration with third-party administrators and insurance carriers, monitoring cases and resolving discrepancies, delays, and escalations.
  • Evaluate interactions among federal, state, local, and Company leave programs to ensure leaves are properly coordinated.
  • Review leave documentation and employee eligibility to ensure appropriate application of Company policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Monitor employees approaching exhaustion of FMLA, disability, or other protected leave and coordinate appropriate next steps.
  • Coordinate return-to-work activities, including review of work restrictions, fitness-for-duty documentation, transitional work considerations, and potential accommodations.
  • Partner with Payroll and Benefits to ensure appropriate benefit deductions, payroll treatment, paid time off usage, and benefit continuation during leaves.
  • Maintain accurate leave and accommodation records in Workday and applicable vendor systems.
  • Conduct routine audits of leave cases and vendor administration to promote accuracy, timeliness, and compliance.
  • Support, actively participate, and act in accordance with Wright’s culture of safety and employee ownership.
  • Comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations; maintains knowledge of and follows all company policies and procedures.
  • Maintain regular and punctual attendance at work and meetings.

ADA, Workplace Accommodation, and Return-to-Work Administration:


  • Serve as a subject matter expert on the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the ADA Amendments Act (ADAAA), reasonable accommodations, and the interactive process.
  • Independently manage complex ADA accommodation cases from initial request through determination, implementation, monitoring, and closure.
  • Lead the interactive process with employees and management, including identification of essential job functions, functional limitations, potential accommodations, and alternative accommodations.
  • Evaluate medical documentation and determine when additional information or clarification is appropriate and legally permissible.
  • Partner with managers and HR to determine whether proposed accommodations are reasonable and effective and whether they present operational or undue-hardship concerns.
  • Manage accommodation considerations involving temporary or permanent work restrictions, modified duties, modified schedules, remote work, reassignment, assistive equipment, intermittent absences, and extended leave.
  • Provide guidance concerning medical inquiries, return-to-work documentation, fitness-for-duty requirements, and confidentiality of employee medical information.
  • Maintain detailed documentation of the interactive process, accommodation decisions, and supporting rationale.

Compliance & Program Support:


  • Maintain advanced working knowledge of the ADA/ADAAA, FMLA, Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA), Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), applicable state and local leave laws, and related employment requirements.
  • Monitor legislative and regulatory developments affecting leaves and workplace accommodations and recommend updates to policies and procedures.
  • Assist with the development and maintenance of leave and accommodation policies, standard operating procedures, forms, templates, and employee and manager communications.
  • Identify opportunities to improve leave administration, employee experience, compliance controls, and vendor performance.
  • Support training for managers and internal stakeholders regarding leave administration, ADA accommodations, and return-to-work requirements.
  • Maintain the confidentiality of medical and employee information.


Other Duties:


  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills & Ability Requirements:


  • Advanced knowledge of the ADA/ADAAA and demonstrated experience independently managing the ADA interactive process and complex workplace accommodations.
  • Advanced knowledge of FMLA and its interaction with the ADA, disability programs, workers' compensation, paid time off, and state and local leave laws.
  • Advanced working knowledge of the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA), Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), and all other applicable state and local leave laws
  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate complex leave and accommodation situations involving overlapping legal and policy requirements.
  • Ability to interpret medical restrictions and translate functional limitations into discussions regarding essential job functions and potential accommodations.
  • Strong judgment and ability to recognize situations requiring escalation to HR leadership or Legal.
  • Experience working with third-party leave administrators, disability carriers, and other leave vendors.
  • Strong case-management, organizational, analytical, documentation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage a high-volume caseload while meeting regulatory and internal deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex leave and accommodation requirements to employees and managers.
  • Ability to handle confidential medical and employee information with discretion.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and enterprise HRIS or leave-management systems.

Education, Certification & Experience Requirements:


  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field preferred; an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
  • Minimum of three years of progressive experience administering employee leaves, disability programs, workplace accommodations, including experience independently handling complex cases.
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience administering FMLA and ADA accommodation cases required.

Other Preferred Requirements:

  • Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish preferred, with the ability to communicate effectively with employees regarding leave, disability, and accommodation matters.
  • Experience administering leave programs across multiple states strongly preferred.
  • Certified Leave Management Specialist (CLMS) or similar designation preferred.
  • Experience working with a third-party leave administrator or disability carrier strongly preferred.
  • Workday experience preferred.

Full-Time employees within Wright Service Corp are eligible for the following:

  • Medical (HDHP & PPO), Dental, and Vision

  • 401k and 401k match

  • ESOP (Employee Ownership Program)

  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick, Floating Holidays)

  • Paid Parental & Family Care Leave

  • Company Paid STD, LTD, and Life Insurance

  • Paid Volunteer Time

  • And More...

description:

Skills

Due to the increasing number of regulations and need for operational transparency, organizations are increasingly adopting the use of consolidated and harmonized sets of compliance controls.

Purpose

Provides high-level, complex administrative support to the Interim Chief Development Officer at the College of Fine Arts, including assisting with operations for the College of Fine Arts development team, while working closely with the Executive Director to support principal-level fundraising activities.

Responsibilities

  • Administrative Support: Provide executive-level administrative support, which includes, but is not limited to: Accurately synthesize large amounts of data into quarterly college-wide fundraising reports and other high-level reports, as requested by the Executive Director and Dean. Prepare gift proposals for individuals and foundations. Draft and process endowment and current-use funding pledge paperwork. Process Requests for Travel (RTAs) and expense reimbursements for travel, entertainment, and other miscellaneous items. title: Project Manager, New Product Development
description:
Job Title

Project Manager, New Product Development

Position Overview:

Position Summary


The Project Manager, New Product Development, leads Shaw's Home Center and TotalWorx product development projects from concept through launch. Reporting to the Director of PMO, this individual-contributor role owns each project's plan, cross-functional team, risks and stakeholder communication, and keeps every project on schedule, within scope and ready for the customer. The role also helps the business stand up a new Home Center product development process, turning the current discovery work into a process that the channel, product, technical and supply teams use every day. The Project Manager works closely with the Home Center channel, category, design, technical, quality, supply development, marketing and finance teams, and provides informal guidance to Associate Project Managers.


Portfolio Focus


  • Home Center. New and refreshed flooring programs for national home-improvement retailers. This work runs on the retailer's calendar (product line reviews, award decisions, and store load-in or reset dates), often with short notice and short production windows. The Project Manager plans backward from those dates and works ahead to protect them. The work includes protecting and refreshing the business already in stores, not only new awards.
  • TotalWorx. Shaw's trims, moldings and stair-tread accessories. The Project Manager leads TotalWorx-led projects and makes sure the accessories that go with hard surface and soft surface flooring launches are defined, sourced, costed and ready at launch. Stair treads and new trims that need overseas tooling have the longest lead times, so they must be identified early in the gate process.
  • Home Center process build. The business is moving from discovery to designing a Home Center product development process. The Project Manager will help shape and pilot it (stages and decision points, Workfront templates, roles and responsibilities, and measures) and then run projects through it.

Key Responsibilities


  • Lead multiple concurrent Home Center and TotalWorx projects from concept through launch, bringing structure, coordination and project-management discipline to complex initiatives across multiple teams and suppliers.
  • Proactively align stakeholders across channels and functions, identifying potential conflicts, dependencies and customer implications early enough to resolve them before they affect project execution.
  • Build and maintain integrated project plans, schedules, resource plans and risk registers that work backward from retailer and launch dates and identify long-lead items early.
  • Facilitate cross-functional project teams and prepare projects for tollgate reviews, making sure deliverables and decisions are ready on time.
  • Frame trade-offs among scope, timing, cost, quality and risk as clear options with a recommendation, facilitating decisions across cross-functional teams and with Director and senior-level business leaders.
  • Manage scope and change control so that projects stay aligned with business goals, the product roadmap for each account, and customer commitments.
  • Coordinate testing, compliance, claims and packaging requirements with Quality, Technical, Marketing and Legal so that products meet both Shaw and retailer standards.
  • Help design, pilot and continuously improve the new Home Center product development process, and apply and improve PMO standards, templates and reporting.
  • Keep Workfront current as the single source of truth for project data, and produce clear status reporting and dashboards for the PMO Director, stakeholders and leadership.
  • Use AI tools and workflow automation to reduce manual work in planning, status reporting and analysis, while checking outputs for accuracy and protecting confidential information.
  • Provide informal guidance and support to Associate Project Managers.

Qualifications


Required


  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Supply Chain, Project Management or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex projects through ambiguity and changing requirements, adapting plans quickly while maintaining stakeholder alignment and execution discipline.
  • 5+ years of professional project management experience leading multiple concurrent or complex cross-functional projects. Experience in new product development, manufacturing, engineering, supply chain, continuous improvement or product launch environments is strongly preferred.
  • Working command of project management methodology (PMI / PMBOK, stage-gate, and hybrid or agile practices), including integrated schedules, risk and change management, and budget and cost tracking.

description:
About the team

The Corporate Development team at Zillow is a high-impact, entrepreneurial function advancing Zillow's Housing Super App vision through acquisitions and strategic investments, as well as financial and strategic analysis across the business. We have been active on the M&A front, including acquisitions such as Virtual Staging AI, Follow Up Boss, Spruce, Aryeo, and VRX Media in recent years, and partner closely with senior leadership on the company's most consequential strategic and financial decisions.

About the role

As a Manager on the Corporate Development team, you will work closely with senior leadership as part of a lean M&A team, applying your strategic and analytical skills to identifying, evaluating, and advancing growth opportunities, both organic and inorganic, across Zillow Group's lines of business. This is an individual contributor role where you'll work alongside senior team members in partnership with business leaders, supporting the thesis and business case that inform M&A as well as transaction execution. We are looking for candidates with strong M&A and financial foundations, intellectual curiosity, and the horsepower to build a long-term career in corporate development.

This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.

In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $130,100.00 - $207,900.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.

In Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Virginia the standard base pay range for this role is $123,700.00 - $197,500.00 annually. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.

In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

  • Research, evaluate, and help develop recommendations for acquisition opportunities
  • Contribute to investment theses and business cases that inform build, buy, and partner decisions
  • Support all transaction phases, including sourcing, due diligence, structuring, negotiation, closing, and integration
  • Provide financial and strategic analysis of acquisition targets, including valuation

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience
  • 4+ years of experience, including at least 2 years in investment banking or private equity; corporate development or strategic finance experience is a plus

  • Clear, concise communicator comfortable presenting analysis and recommendations to senior stakeholders
  • Strong three-statement financial modeling skills and broad financial acumen, including corporate finance principles, financial statement analysis and valuation methodologies, applied to novel business situations
  • Experience executing M&A transactions through the full process
  • Ownership mentality, questioning assumptions and taking responsibility for conclusions
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage several priorities simultaneously
  • Strong initiative and judgment; performing in a fast-paced, dynamic, entrepreneurial environment, working efficiently with cross-functional teams in a remote environment

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.


How we work is a key part of that transformation. Through Cloud HQ, our strategic approach to distributed work, most employees have the flexibility to work from wherever they’re most productive—enabling us to move fast, stay connected and deliver on our people promise.


Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the U.S. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2026, and included on TIME’s America’s Best Companies 2026 list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.


No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. title: Postdoctoral Fellow - RNA Genomics
description:
A little about us:

The Lieber Institute for Brain Development (LIBD) was established in 2010 to plot a new course in biomedical research that would change the lives of individuals affected with developmental brain disorders. We are one of the only research institutions in the world focused specifically on understanding how genes and the environment influence the way our brains develop that lead to conditions such as schizophrenia, autism, bipolar disorder and related developmental brain disorders. Through our cutting-edge research, answers are emerging and being translated into a robust pipeline of new drugs in development. And, by focusing on genes and their dynamic interplay with the environment, we are getting even closer to the “holy grail” in medical research, the discovery of strategies for primary prevention.


We are a group of dedicated, multidisciplinary and optimistic researchers, working at the cutting edge of science, utilizing state-of-the-art tools to unlock the mystery of the brain and transform the way we approach the development of new treatments, and ultimately cures. LIBD is an independent 501(c)(3) medical research institute located in the Bioscience Park on the campus of the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine and Hospital in Baltimore, MD.


Job Summary:

We are seeking a highly motivated and self-driven postdoctoral fellow to join our research group. Our research focuses on understanding how gene regulatory mechanisms are disrupted in psychiatric and neurological disorders and how these insights can be translated into novel therapeutic strategies. The successful candidate will lead the design and execution of experimental studies and collaborate closely with computational biologists to analyze and interpret experimental results.


Visit the Hwang Lab’s profile at LIBD () or our lab website () for more information. For inquiries about projects, please contact Taeyoung Hwang at taeyoung.hwang@libd.org.



Key responsibilities:

  • Design, perform, and troubleshoot molecular biology experiments using neuronal cell culture systems.
  • Prepare next-generation sequencing (NGS) libraries for genomic assays, including RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and CUT&RUN.
  • Perform molecular cloning and viral transduction.
  • Conduct molecular and cellular assays, including qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry.
  • Collaborate with computational biologists to integrate experimental and computational findings.
  • Other duties as assigned.

The Access Supervisor manages the day-to-day operations of the Access department, the agency's centralized intake and information and referral team. The position includes supervision of staff, and ensures that each inquiry is assessed accurately, linked to the right service, and followed up in a timely way. The Supervisor also builds and maintains working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

Responsibilities

Management Responsibilities

  • Supervises and evaluates performance of Access team members, including their phone assessment and customer service skills.
  • Provides regular individual and group supervision, coaching, and training to Access team members.
  • Makes employment decision recommendations for Access team members, including but not limited to hiring and terminations.
  • Directs daily Access operations: coverage, workflow, call, email, and walk-in response, and handling of urgent or complex inquiries.
  • Provides clinical oversight of intake and assessment practice, including consultation on complex or escalated cases.
  • Maintains a current understanding of all agency programs and community resources so inquiries are linked to the right services.
  • Monitors follow-up and team performance using intake and referral data; escalates trends, barriers, and policy or system issues to agency leadership.
  • Contributes to refining Access policies, screening and documentation standards, and provides input on data, reporting, and system needs as Access evolves.
  • Supports rollout of new or revised workflows, tools, and partner processes, including training and coaching staff through change.
  • Serves as the day-to-day contact for partner agencies on referrals and handoffs and participates in cross-agency workgroups.
  • Works with program directors and supervisors to ensure all inquiries are followed up on.
  • May provide field instruction to interns.

Direct Service Responsibilities

  • Handles calls and inquiries alongside Access team members.
  • Creates a warm, welcoming experience for all callers and accurately assesses callers' needs.
  • Responds to all inquiries, providing appropriate referrals or linkages, and seeking consultation as indicated.
  • Performs documentation and record keeping.
  • Represents JCFS and its programs in a positive, professional manner to both internal and external contacts.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Traits and Competencies

  • Self-reflective; actively appraises own responses and reactions.
  • Flexible; able to pivot and adjust as unplanned requests and priorities arise
  • Able to take varied perspectives and think critically.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Managerial acumen, including the ability to supervise a multidisciplinary team.
  • Sound independent judgment and decision making in a variety of situations.
  • Collaborative; builds strong relationships with staff, partner agencies, and community organizations.
  • Comfortable with data and case management or CRM systems; applies shared standards consistently.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Excellent customer service skills.
  • Commitment to equitable, culturally responsive service.

Decision Making Authority

  • Uses independent judgment and a high level of discretion in determining how work gets done within the scope of the position. Anticipates and develops solutions to complex problems.

Requirements

  • Master’s Degree in Social Work or related
  • Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) or Licensed Clinical Professional Counselor (LCPC) licensure required.
  • Minimum two (2) years of direct clinical
  • Prior supervisory experience required; at least two (2) years of experience preferred.
  • Prior administrative experience required; at least two (2) years of experience preferred.
  • Experience with partner agencies, multi-agency collaboration, or process improvement preferred.

title: Service Desk Specialist (L2/L3)
description:
What this Job Entails

The IT Support Specialist (L2/L3) provides advanced, mostly in-office support for our client, a ~1,500-person company running a 95% Mac / 5% Windows environment. This role handles escalated and complex issues, delivers hands-on device and network support, and helps build the runbooks and automation that improve self-service over time.

Scope

  • Works on complex, non-routine issues that require independent judgment and root-cause analysis
  • Operates with minimal supervision; serves as the escalation point between frontline support and specialist or vendor teams
  • Identifies recurring issues and turns fixes into documented, automated workflows

Your Roles and Responsibilities

  • Resolve escalated and complex support issues, with ownership from intake through resolution
  • Provide in-office, hands-on support for hardware, software, peripherals, and conference spaces
  • Support and troubleshoot macOS devices (95% of the fleet) and the Windows minority, including OS, application, and performance issues
  • Manage device lifecycle through Iru (MDM): enrollment, configuration profiles, app deployment, patching, and compliance
  • Troubleshoot Meraki Wi-Fi connectivity and coverage issues; work with network teams on escalations
  • Administer and support Google Workspace and Slack: accounts, groups, permissions, and integrations
  • Build, maintain, and improve IT runbooks and automated workflows in Console (ITSM)
  • Analyze ticket trends to find recurring issues, close knowledge gaps, and reduce escalations
  • Lead new-hire device setup and onboarding; manage offboarding and hardware recovery
  • Coordinate with vendors on hardware repairs, RMAs, and escalated software issues
  • Maintain accurate IT asset inventory
  • Ensure devices meet security standards (encryption, OS currency, MDM compliance)
  • Mentor junior support staff and share knowledge across the team (L3)

Required Qualifications/Skills

  • 3 to 5+ years of IT support experience (L2), or 5+ years (L3), in a fast-paced, Mac-centric environment
  • Deep macOS troubleshooting skills; working knowledge of Windows
  • Hands-on experience with an Apple MDM (Iru/Kandji, Jamf, or similar)
  • Google Workspace and Slack administration experience
  • Experience troubleshooting enterprise Wi-Fi (Meraki preferred)
  • Experience with an ITSM platform and writing runbooks or knowledge base content
  • Strong root-cause analysis and problem-solving skills
  • Exceptional customer service and communication skills, including explaining technical issues to non-technical users
  • Self-directed, with sound judgment on when to resolve, escalate, or automate

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Console or similar ITSM and automation platforms
  • Workflow automation or scripting experience (Bash, Python, Apps Script, or no-code automation tools)
  • Okta or other identity provider administration
  • Apple certifications (ACSP, ACIT) or Meraki certification (CMNA)
  • Experience supporting conference rooms and AV/video conferencing

Physical Demand & Work Environment

  • Primarily on site in the client's office, with occasional remote work
  • Must have the ability to perform office-related tasks which may include prolonged sitting or standing
  • Must have the ability to move from place to place within an office environment
  • Must be able to lift and carry IT equipment up to 30 lbs
  • Must have the ability to communicate effectively
  • Some positions may require occasional repetitive motion or movements of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers

Salary Range

$30.12 - $50.19 USD (Hourly)
  • Please note that the salary information provided herein is base pay only (gross); it does not include other forms of compensation which may or may not apply to this specific position, namely, performance-based bonuses, benefits-related payments, or other general incentives - none of which are guaranteed, may be subject to specific eligibility requirements, and are wholly within the discretion of Astreya to remit.
  • Further, the salary information noted above is a range that consists of a minimum and maximum rate of pay for this specific position. Where an applicant or employee is placed on this range will depend and be contingent on objective, documented work-related considerations like education, experience, certifications, licenses, preferred qualifications, among other factors.

  • Dental provided through UHC

description:

The Senior Project Manager, Gas Operations, leads high-risk, large-scale, and complex gas infrastructure projects across Connecticut and Massachusetts. This role operates in a multi-stakeholder environment and requires strong leadership, regulatory acumen, and cross-functional coordination. The Senior Project Manager will be responsible for ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, within scope, and within budget, while maintaining compliance with all regulatory and company standards. This position involves direct engagement with internal leadership, external regulators, municipal officials, and community stakeholders.

  • Develop and manage comprehensive project plans, budgets, schedules, and communication strategies.
  • Coordinate regulatory approvals, permitting, and stakeholder engagement including municipalities and state agencies.
  • Collaborate with the engineering & procurement departments to manage procurement activities, including the development and evaluation of bids for engineering, design, and construction services.
  • Monitor and report on project performance, risks, and financial exposure; implement mitigation strategies.
  • Ensure compliance with internal policy and external regulatory requirements.
  • Present project updates and strategic recommendations to senior leadership and steering committees.
  • Mentor junior project managers and contribute to continuous improvement of project management practices.
  • Lead change management initiatives and organizational process development.
  • Provide expert representation at municipal meetings and regulatory proceedings.
  • Support emergency storm restoration efforts as needed.
  • Travel across MA/CT as required.
  • Participate in industry events and technical committees to expand professional network.
  • Participate in community outreach events.
  • Maintain project documentation and ensure timely close-out aligned with corporate goals.
  • Ensure safety and quality control plans are implemented and maintained throughout project lifecycle.
  • Participate in random drug testing as part of safety-sensitive designation.

Qualifications:

Technical Knowledge/Skill:

  • Deep understanding of project management principles and practices.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple complex projects concurrently.
  • Experience in regulatory interface, providing expect testimony, and public engagement.
  • Strategic thinking and decision-making capabilities.

Education:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Finance, Business, or equivalent Engineering-related discipline preferred or equivalent experience.
  • Master’s degree preferred.

Experience:

  • Eight (8) or more years of operational/managerial experience, including at least five (5) years experience in project/program management.

Licenses & Certifications:

  • PMP, PgMP, PfMP, CAPM, PMO-CP or Project Management Masters Certificate preferred.
  • Six-Sigma & Taproot certification preferred.

This position is categorized as safety-sensitive for the purpose of drug testing. As an employee in this position the individual shall be subject to random drug testing.

title: Assistant Branch Manager
description:
Grow Your Career. Impact Lives. Shape the Future of Consumer Finance.


At Regional Finance, growth is more than a strategy. It's an opportunity for our people to thrive. Over the past several years, we have expanded significantly, creating new career paths, leadership opportunities, and professional development experiences across our organization.


As a proud NYSE-listed company, we serve more than half a million active customers through a network of 360+ branches across 20 states and a rapidly growing digital platform. With approximately $2.1 billion in net finance receivables, nearly double our position in 2020, our momentum reflects both the strength of our business and the dedication of our team.


If you're passionate about helping people, driven by growth, and excited to contribute to a company transforming the future of consumer finance, we invite you to join our team and build something meaningful with us.

Introduction

At Regional, we're building a national, omnichannel lender where customers can reach us in our branches, by phone, and online, and get the same personal service every time. Customer obsession drives every decision we make, and we're investing in modern technology and AI-powered tools to make each interaction faster, simpler, and more personal. For you, that means less time on paperwork, more time helping customers reach their goals, and a front-row seat as we shape the future of personal lending.

We believe your career should grow as fast as you're willing to push it: many of our executive leaders started exactly where you would, as an Assistant Manager, and built their way up to leading their own district through our structured training and development programs. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the future of financial services.

Top performers in this role can earn up to $72,640 per year in total compensation, including bonus. Base pay starts at $19.00 to $28.00 per hour depending on skills and experience, and our bonus program lets you earn up to an additional $1,200 every month based on your individual and team performance.

In This Role, You Will

  • Exceed individual and branch-level loan sales targets, driving volume and conversion through proactive customer outreach and follow-up
  • Build and maintain relationships by engaging customers throughout the full loan lifecycle — while recommending tailored financial solutions
  • Assist in the training and coaching of new team members, providing a culture of growth for yourself and your team
  • Apply credit underwriting techniques and sales tools to drive informed lending decisions
  • Manage early-stage delinquent consumer loan accounts (1-30 days past due) through outbound calls, texts, and emails, working with borrowers to resolve past-due balances through payment arrangements, extensions, or other approved solutions.
  • Ensure compliance, accuracy, and operational excellence in all lending activities
  • Clearly educate and inform customers on loan terms and optional products, ensuring they have a thorough understanding of their options
  • Effectively multitask and adapt to the dynamic demands of the role, ensuring timely and efficient service

You will thrive if you enjoy:

  • Purpose-Driven Performance – Every sale represents a customer whose financial burden you've helped ease; success is measured by results because results mean real impact on real lives
  • We promote from within – A majority of our team members grow into leadership roles here, so your career path is built in from day one.
  • Clear Goals, Meaningful Rewards – Individual and branch-level sales targets are transparent, with uncapped bonus potential tied to performance that puts customers in a better financial position
  • Growth into Leadership – You take ownership, motivate those around you, and show up as a leader on the team

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3+ year of experience in a performance-driven sales environment
  • Ability to handle cash payments
  • High School Diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license and reliable, insured transportation

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bilingual in Spanish/English
  • Associates or Bachelors degree

Work Schedule: This is an on-site role serving customers in person and by phone. Standard hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM. Occasional Saturdays and late evenings may be required based on business needs.

Benefits That Support You

We offer competitive salaries and benefits designed to support your health, financial wellbeing, work life balance, and future.

  • G.O.A.L. Training Program - Designed to prepare Regional’s top performing Assistant Managers for Branch Manager positions. Throughout the program you will learn how to become a successful leader with the company.
  • Caring About Regional Employees (C.A.R.E.) Fund - At Regional, we care deeply about our employees, so we've established the C.A.R.E. fund to support team members facing severe emergencies. This optional, employee-funded program lets colleagues contribute directly to help each other through hardship.
  • Health Insurance - Including prescription coverage
  • Dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
  • 401(k) Plan – with up to 4% matching contributions
  • Paid Time Off – 17 PTO days plus company holidays

title: Seasonal Doughnut Maker
description:
Since its founding in 1937, Krispy Kreme’s focus has remained the same - making fresh doughnuts using our founder’s original recipe. The brand’s iconic Hot Light lets consumers know when doughnuts are being made in the shop so they can stop in and enjoy them hot, right off the line.


Our Doughnut Makers have one of the most critical roles within our shops! You are responsible for making our iconic doughnuts while ensuring a level of quality that meets Krispy Kreme standards and in turn, satisfying our customers. You will prepare the dough, the yeast brew, the glaze, and the fillings. Don’t worry, we will make sure you know how to do all of that to become a key member of our team.


During peak seasons, we rely on a flexible, seasonal staffing model to ensure our A-Glazing customers receive friendly, efficient service and a well-maintained store appearance. Join us for a fun and rewarding seasonal experience.


A TASTE OF WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING:

  • Prepare all ingredients necessary for doughnut production - brew, dough, glaze, fillings, and icings.
  • Accurately weigh ingredients, measure liquids, mixing, and frying doughnuts
  • Record keeping (times and temperatures) of all products prepared to ensure freshness and reduce waste.
  • Maintain sanitation standards within production area to ensure proper cleanliness and smooth operation of equipment.

YOUR RECIPE FOR SUCCESS:

  • Two (2) years of experience in a job involving food handling and safety.
  • Must be 18 years of age or over.
  • Effective communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Open availability and flexibility is a must – ability to work any shift
  • Ability to understand weights and measurements.
  • Has a steadfast commitment to nurture an equitable, unbiased culture where our peeps are empowered to showcase their originality.
  • Present self in a professional manner, including adhering to uniform standards.
  • Must be authorized to work in the US without sponsorship.

*The above statements are intended to describe the general nature of work performed by the employees assigned to this job and are not the official job description for the position.


BENEFITS:

•Weekly Pay

•Career opportunities- we are growing!


WHY KRISPY KREME?

At Krispy Kreme, we focus on:

Loving People:

  • Our global culture is best captured by our Leadership Mix, a dozen behaviors that define how we work with one another across the world and give back to our communities. Check out our leadership mix here.
  • Belonging happens once each Krispy Kremer knows their bold authentic self is welcomed, dignified, and loved, where their wonderfully original identities flourish and thrive.

Loving Communities:

  • At Krispy Kreme, sharing joy is at the center of everything we do, and we strive to inspire this in our communities. Our brand purpose truly shines through our Acts of Joy and community fundraising initiatives.
  • In the U.S., we have been donating unsold doughnuts to local food banks, with a goal of bringing a smile to our consumers as they enjoy a small, sweet treat. We partner with Feeding America and Convoy of Hope, who in turn partner with organizations nationwide to distribute donations to people in need through diverse types of programs and services.
  • In 2022, we helped community groups raise $40 million globally. Last year in the U.S., we supported more than 83,000 fundraising events, raising nearly $37 million.

Loving Planet:

  • We have been conducting a multi-year global GHG emissions assessment to establish an emissions baseline, using this foundation to soon set goals for greenhouse gas emission reductions.
  • We are working on reducing food waste through donation efforts, animal feed, and composting programs.


Krispy Kreme is an Equal Opportunity Employer:

At Krispy Kreme, we believe that your originality sweetens our recipe. We value the diverse ingredients of the ethnicity, national origin, race, age, sex, gender, intersex, or veteran status of every individual. We strive for an inclusive culture that allows each of our peeps to bring their bold authentic self to work regardless of their religion, gender identity & expression, sexual orientation, or disability.


About Krispy Kreme

Headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., Krispy Kreme is one of the most beloved and well-known sweet treat brands in the world. Our iconic Original Glazed® doughnut is universally recognized for its hot-off-the-line, melt-in-your-mouth experience. Krispy Kreme operates in more than 35 countries through its unique network of fresh doughnut shops, partnerships with leading retailers, and a rapidly growing Ecommerce and delivery business with more than 14,000 fresh points of access. Our purpose of touching and enhancing lives through the joy that is Krispy Kreme guides how we operate every day and is reflected in the love we have for our people, our communities and the planet. title: Lead Power Electronics Engineer
description:
Our Company

Whisper Aero is pioneering a more compelling and connected future by delivering cleaner, quieter, and more efficient propulsion solutions. Today's open rotor propulsion systems are challenged by safety, noise, and performance limitations at all scales. Whisper's breakthrough technologies allow aircraft to fly anywhere at any time without disturbing communities, at greater speeds, and with incredible improvements in efficiency and cost. Their innovations also enable a new generation of air moving products that can blend into the soundscapes of daily life. Whisper was founded by industry veterans, Mark Moore and Ian Villa, and continues to innovate a future that’s as considerate as it is compelling with its world-class team in Tennessee.

About the Role

Whisper Aero is looking for a Lead Power Electronics Engineer to own the development of the next generation of motor controllers and electronics that drive our propulsion systems. This is a unique opportunity to take technical ownership of a critical piece of our technology, lead a talented team of engineers, and help shape the future of electric aviation.

In this role, you'll lead the development of our motor controllers from initial concept through detailed design, prototyping, testing, and validation. You'll be responsible for the complete controller, spanning high voltage power electronics, embedded hardware, firmware, software, and system integration. You'll build and lead a multidisciplinary team, drive key technical decisions and work closely with our motor, propulsion, and systems engineering teams to deliver tightly integrated, high performance propulsion solutions.

We're looking for someone who combines deep technical expertise with the desire to build, lead, and deliver; someone who is as comfortable making critical architecture decisions as they are getting hands-on in the lab and solving challenging problems alongside their team. This is an opportunity to own a product from the ground up, push the boundaries of power electronics, and see your designs powering the next generation of aircraft.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the motor controller. Lead the end-to-end development of Whisper Aero's motor controllers and associated electronics from requirements of definition and system architecture through detailed design, prototyping, integration, verification, and validation.
  • Build and lead a high-performance team. Manage, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team of hardware, firmware, and software engineers. Set technical direction, establish priorities, and foster a culture of ownership, collaboration, and engineering excellence.
  • Define the technical architecture. Lead key design decisions across power electronics, embedded control hardware, firmware, and software.
  • Drive hardware and software integration. Oversee the development of embedded control systems, including microcontroller/DSP/FPGA selection, motor control firmware, communication interfaces, diagnostics, and supervisory software.
  • Turn designs into working hardware. Lead schematic and PCB design reviews, component selection, prototyping, debugging, and design iterations while remaining hands on with designs you develop.
  • Prove it works. Own the test and validation strategy for motor controllers including dynamometer and integrated propulsion testing, hardware-in-the-loop testing, environmental qualification, and EMI/EMC compliance.
  • Work across disciplines. Collaborate closely with motor design, mechanical, thermal, propulsion, and systems engineers to optimize the performance and integration of our complete electric propulsion systems.
  • Take products from prototype to production. Drive design for manufacturability, reliability, and scalability by working with suppliers and manufacturing partners to transition designs into production ready hardware.
  • Shape how we engineer. Establish technical standards, development processes, design review practices, and engineering tools that enable the team to move quickly without compromising safety, quality, or performance.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, electronics engineering, or related technical field.
  • 8+ years of experience developing motor controllers, inverters, or high-performance power electronics systems, including significant ownership of system architecture and design.
  • Demonstrated experience leading engineers and delivering complex, multidisciplinary hardware development programs.
  • Strong technical understanding of inverter and motor controller architectures, including power semiconductor selection, gate drivers, DC/DC converters, power supplies, sensing, protection, and control electronics.
  • Experience designing, integrating, and testing high voltage power electronics systems (270VDC or higher).
  • Working knowledge of embedded control systems, motor control algorithms, firmware development, and hardware/software integration.
  • PCB schematic design, layout, component selection, and hardware debugging.
  • Designed for EMI/EMC performance and supporting compliance testing.
  • Development and execution of hardware verification and validation plans including environmental and electrical testing.
  • Strong technical judgment, communication, and leadership skills with the ability to make decisions, drive execution, and develop the engineers around you.
  • A willingness to work on tasks outside your primary job functions.
  • This position requires access to information, technology, or materials subject to U.S. export control laws. To comply with these regulations, applicants must be authorized to access export-controlled information under applicable U.S. laws and regulations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree or PhD in electrical engineering, power electronics, or a related field.
  • Development of aerospace or other safety critical electronics systems.
  • Experience with RTCA DO-160 environmental qualification, DO-178C, DO-254, or ARP4754A development processes.
  • Use and troubleshooting of high-speed, high-power density electric motor drives including SiC or GaN power devices.
  • Interaction and understanding of field-oriented control, sensorless control, or other advanced motor control strategies.
  • Integrating motor drives directly into electric motor housings including thermal management, packaging, and EMI/EMC considerations.
  • Experience taking power electronics products from early prototypes through qualification and production.

Benefits:

  • Top-tier Benefits: Employee-first focused comprehensive benefits package, minimum of 90% employer-paid plans for employees and dependents with optional HSA/FSA account offerings
  • PTO & Federal Holidays: Starting at four weeks of paid time off for vacation, sick, and personal days
  • Competitive Salary: Value-based compensation, plus enjoy Tennessee’s no-income-tax life
  • End of Year Bonuses: For eligible employees
  • We always have beverages and snacks available to energize you throughout the day, with paid team meals based on office demands.
  • 401(k)
  • Relocation Assistance
  • Professional Development Stipend

Whisper Aero is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusivity in the workplace. All aspects of employment are decided on the basis of merit, qualifications, and business needs. We do not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. Whisper Aero also participates in E-Verify and will provide the Social Security Administration (SSA) and, if necessary, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), with information from each applicant's Form I-9 to confirm work authorization.

title: Captain
description:
Rate of Pay: $57,200 per year

Organize and conduct inspections and searches of inmates, detainees, and offenders and their living and work areas.

Prepare records and reports as assigned.

Maintain logs and verify inmate counts.

Foster a team effort among correctional officers providing support, motivation, training, and assistance to them as required.

Report and investigate all unusual occurrences.

Direct the work of employees to ensure effectiveness.

Supervise daily routine of the security section.

Enforce post orders and ensure that correctional officers are familiar with shift assignments.

Manage disciplinary reports and prepare reports of disturbances and shift activities.

Function as shift supervisor as needed: supervise, instruct, train, and ensure the safety of assigned employees, inmates, detainees, and offenders; schedule employees, inmates, detainees, and offenders work and off-duty time; and assist in formulating security and work procedures.

Supervise and provide custody and security of inmates, detainees, and offenders including observing actions of inmates, detainees, and offenders; squatting and bending to perform “pat” and “strip” searches of inmates, detainees, and offenders; restraining and securing sometimes assaultive inmates, detainees, and offenders; and transferring and transporting inmates, detainees, and offenders by walking or riding in various vehicles such as trailers, vans, buses, etc.

Supervise and provide security of inmates, detainees, and offenders performing technical skills such as construction, maintenance, laundry, food service, and in varied industrial and agricultural operations which involve climbing stairs, steps, and ladders, and climbing around the inside and outside of buildings; work outdoors and indoors without air conditioning; work around motorized or moving equipment and machinery; subject to all types of weather.

Respond to emergencies including climbing stairs, steps, and ladders while searching for escaped inmates, detainees, and offenders; hearing calls for and calling for help; giving first aid at the emergency site; carrying an injured or unconscious inmate, detainee, offender or employee various distances to safety up or down stairs, steps, and ladders; use force and deadly force to include the use of chemical agents and firearms to control inmates, detainees, and offenders.

Read, review, and properly apply information found in inmate, detainee, and offender records which is related to said individual’s health and safety and to the security of the facility; provide appropriate information to other personnel; comply with all policies, procedures, rules, and regulations; enforce inmate, detainee, and offender disciplinary rules; and supervise the preparation and maintenance of records, forms, and reports.

Perform a variety of marginal duties not listed, to be determined and assigned as needed.

Required Knowledge Skills/Abilities:

Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills.

Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.

Excellent time management skills with a proven ability to meet deadlines.

Ability to function well in a high-paced and at times stressful environment.

Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite or related software.

Mid-management level in a security department

Education and Experience:

At least three years of experience in a correctional institution is required.

5 years of experience in a correctional setting and 1-year experience in a supervisory position preferred.

Must be TCole certified or must be able to obtain TCole Jailers License where applicable.

Physical Requirements:

The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to satisfactorily perform these essential functions without causing undue hardship for the employer.

Extended periods of continuous standing and walking.

Frequent periods of sitting.

Repetitive climbing of stairs to reach the assigned areas and working at heights.

Occasional kneeling, squatting, and bending to perform “pat” or “strip” searches.

Frequent grasping, reaching, pushing, pulling, bending, twisting.

Occasionally responding to altercations and occasional restraining and securing assaultive offenders

Ability to respond rapidly to potential security and/or medical codes/issues.

Frequent transferring and transporting offenders by walking or riding in various offenders.

Remaining awake and alert while on duty for 12 or more hours per shift

Occasional lifting and carrying up to 50-100 lbs.

Ability to occasionally withstand direct or indirect exposure to OC spray.

Exposure for up to 12 hours or more per shift of outdoor elements and temperatures with scheduled breaks

Ability to hear and understand verbal communications.

title: Aerospace Sales Engineer-Aftermarket
description:
Summary of the Role:

​​The Aftermarket MRO Sales Engineer is responsible for driving revenue growth and customer satisfaction in the aerospace aftermarket through the sale of polymer‑based products and solutions, including seals, elastomers, engineered plastics, and consumable components used in maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) applications. This role supports aircraft owner‑operators, MRO facilities, distributors, and broker/resellers, combining strong technical knowledge of polymer materials with commercial expertise to address aftermarket performance, availability, and cost‑of‑ownership requirements. The Aftermarket MRO Sales Engineer serves as the technical and commercial interface between customers and internal engineering, quality, manufacturing, and supply chain teams to develop compliant, interchangeable, and value‑driven polymer solutions. This includes supporting material selection, application suitability, regulatory compliance, and aftermarket substitution strategies to deliver competitive and profitable outcomes across the product lifecycle. ​The Aftermarket MRO Sales Engineer is responsible for building relationships across all levels within existing customers and prospective target accounts to generate new business opportunities.

title: PRN APP (SMG)
description:
Welcome! We’re excited you’re considering an opportunity with us! To apply to this position and be considered, click the Apply button located above this message and complete the application in full. Below, you’ll find other important information about this position.

The Advanced Practice Professional (APP) provides high-quality, patient-centered care as a member of the interdisciplinary healthcare team. Working collaboratively with physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals, the APP assesses, diagnoses, treats, and manages patients within their scope of practice and area of specialty. The APP is responsible for delivering evidence-based care, promoting positive patient outcomes, maintaining professional and regulatory standards, and supporting the clinical, educational, and operational goals of the department and organization.

Additional Job Description:


Additional Job Description

The Advanced Practice Professional (APP) has coordination and clinical skills required for the comprehensive management of urgent care/emergency medicine patients, (including biological, social, and psychological assessments). The APP coordinates involvement of medical specialty teams necessary to develop a comprehensive plan for the patient and reviews the plan of care with the other members of the clinical team, participates in directing that care, performs diagnostic/therapeutic procedures and coordinates discharge planning (as applicable). The APP participates in the education of residents and medical/nursing students. Provide healthcare services consistent with state law and the requirements of the professional licensing or certification authority and/or hospital privileges, where applicable.


Required Certifications:

American Heart Association BLS, ACLS and ATLS certification required.

Fundamentals of Critical Care Support (FCCS) Certification required immediately upon hire (based on class availability).


EXPERIENCE:

1. Acute care or emergency medicine experience preferred.

2. Eligible new graduates will be considered.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

EDUCATION, CERTIFICATION, AND/OR LICENSURE:

1. Masters level education as Medical/Surgical (as applicable) Physician Assistant preferred.


CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.

1. Manages comprehensive and individualized care for urgent care/emergency medicine patients and their families in the ambulatory setting.

2. Consults and/or pre-procedure/evaluations, acute visits and wellness visits.

3. Completes integrated assessments.

4. With the collaboration of urgent care/emergency medicine faculty or by following established clinical Guidelines and Protocols, orders additional tests or consults as deemed appropriate.

5. Performs and communicates results of diagnostic tests following established clinical guidelines and scope of practice.

6. Consults and communicates with clinic and hospital staff regarding abnormal findings in the evaluations of patients.

7. Performs succinct comprehensive clinical evaluations and documents findings in medical record.

8. Facilitates patient follow-up by coordinating appropriate services and tests for follow-up appointments in the clinic (as applicable).

9. Develops a comprehensive individualized plan of care for urgent care/emergency medicine patients, which includes teaching, follow-up planning and necessary referral to other members of the health care team as necessary.

10. Demonstrates expertise in caring for patients across the age continuum of their educational experience and certification.

11. Identifies unstable or complex urgent care/emergency medicine patient care situations and facilitates appropriate intervention in the clinic and/or hospital setting.

12. Recognizes emergency situations and initiates effective emergency care.

13. Evaluates urgent care/emergency medicine patients and serves as a coordinator for follow up procedures and tests in the ambulatory setting (as applicable).

14. Assists in the collection of outcome measures (as applicable).

15. Demonstrates critical thinking and diagnostic reasoning skills in clinical decision making by the identification, evaluation and management of the individual needs of patients/families.

16. Demonstrates the ability to utilize equipment in a safe manner.

17. Bases decisions made/actions taken on the relevant scientific principles, established standards of care and/or research findings.

18. Utilizes teaching/learning theory and appropriate teaching strategies in the provision of education to nursing staff, hospital staff, students, patients, families and the community.

19. Promotes an environment that facilitates learning by responding to appropriate patient/family preferences, priorities and readiness to learn.

20. Updates own knowledge base throughout the year.

21. Completes all identified clinical competencies.

22. Serves as a resource person for staff caring for the urgent care/emergency medicine patient.

23. Provides educational programs to professional and paraprofessional personnel in area of expertise.

24. Participates in community programs, distribution of literature, as appropriate in area of expertise.

25. Documents the plan of care, interventions and evaluations in a clear and concise manner for every patient visit in the patient’s medical record following approved hospital/UHA policies and compliance standards for documentation.

26. Collaborates with other leaders and staff to effectively achieve patient outcome based improvements in care.

27. Provides leadership in the development and implantation of changes in the urgent care/emergency medicine practice that positively impact patient outcomes.

28. Works collaboratively with medical and nursing staff to facilitate creative problem solving and provide professional support.

29. Participates and initiates inter-disciplinary approaches to patient care, program development and education. Serves as a professional role model.

30. Promotes and practices innovation of the expanded role in the delivery of care to urgent care/emergency medicine patients and families throughout the inpatient hospitalization, and the ambulatory setting.

31. Participates and provides leadership for committees and task forces.

32. Documents hours and submits billing reports, as appropriate.

33. Reviews and interprets urgent care/emergency medicine data from sources such as patient registries, clinical and financial reports, length of stay, access to care, and cost per case reports and recommends/implements changes as necessary.

34. Participates in clinical trials and research studies with the Principal Investigator.

35. Assists urgent care/emergency medicine Faculty, Administrators and Directors in the collection of outcome measures.

36. Other duties/projects as assigned.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

1. Heavy/Hard Work: Work requires strength and/or stamina, lifting, moving, stooping, reaching, positioning of patients, standing, walking, and carrying of patients, materials and equipment weighting 40+ pounds.

while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to

perform the essential functions.

2. Protracted or irregular hours.

3. Working around biohazards.

4. Working around infectious diseases.

5. Working with or near the deceased.

6. Working with hands in water.

7. Electrical hazards associated with patient care equipment.

SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

1. Proficiency with computers.

2. Strong communication skills.

title: Database Administrator
description:
Our vision is a world of peaceful relationships with food, weight, and body image, where everyone with an eating disorder can experience recovery. We believe that exceptional, individualized care leads to lasting recovery from eating disorders. That’s why our teams are comprised of compassionate, dedicated professionals from a variety of backgrounds who collaborate to provide the very best evidence-based care for our clients at all levels of care.

Position Overview:

The Database Administrator is responsible for the reliability, performance and security of Accanto Health's Azure data platform, which integrates data from the electronic health record, Salesforce and financial systems to support enterprise reporting and analytics. As the organization's first dedicated database administrator, this position establishes and maintains platform standards, monitoring, backup and recovery, access controls and documentation. The role administers Azure SQL and data warehouse environments, ensures the reliability of data ingestion from source systems, tunes database and reporting performance, and safeguards protected health information in accordance with HIPAA. This position partners with the Data Architect, Data Developers, and the EHR and application teams, and reports to the Director of Health Data Analytics.

Schedule

  • 8am-5pm, Monday to Friday

Salary Range:

  • $150,414- $184,970 commensurate with experience

Location:

  • Remote- Must be US based, and able to work with no restrictions in the US in a remote home office.

  • Travel up to 10%

Visa / work permit sponsorship is not available for this position

How Database Administrators Empower Recovery:

Platform and environments

  • Azure SQL and warehouse environments across development, test and production — compute and storage sizing, performance tiers, and platform cost.
  • Environment lifecycle, including scheduled refreshes of non-production from production so that test data is current enough to surface real edge cases. This is currently unowned and refreshes have lapsed; you will own the cadence, the vendor request process, and the cost conversation that goes with it.
  • Ingestion reliability from the EHR, Salesforce and financial systems — monitoring, alerting, failure triage, and documented re-run procedures.

Performance

  • Tune ETL/ELT transformations and reporting queries (SSRS, Power BI).
  • Own indexing, statistics and partitioning strategy for large tables such as claims, transactions and encounters.
  • Establish performance baselines, so that “the report is slow” becomes a measurement rather than an argument.

Security and compliance

  • Role-based access control, least-privilege design, and periodic access review.
  • PHI safeguards under HIPAA: encryption in transit and at rest, data masking, audit logging.
  • Vendor and contractor access management, including access paths covered by business associate agreements.
  • Participation in incident response for data-related events.

Reliability

  • Backup, restore and disaster recovery — including published RPO and RTO targets and restore tests that are actually performed, not just documented.
  • Detection and resolution of source-to-warehouse synchronization gaps.
  • Root-cause analysis of data inconsistencies, including cases where the source system holds several conflicting copies of the same fact.

Documentation and continuity

  • Platform documentation, runbooks, and data lineage from source through to the reporting layer. This is a first-class responsibility, not an afterthought — undocumented dependencies are our single largest operational risk today.
  • Cross-training and written procedures, so no critical process depends on one person.

Partnership

  • Data Architect, Data Modelers, Data Developers and Analytics leadership.
  • The EHR and application teams, and our EHR vendor's technical staff. Configuration changes are made in the application land in our warehouse, so this role is one of the few that has to see both sides. These teams currently plan separately; helping to close that gap is part of the job.
  • Finance, on platform cost and forecasting.

Education Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required in information technology, Healthcare Administration, Health Information Management, Healthcare Informatics, Computer Science, Business, or related field preferred; Associate Degree and 7 years equivalent experience may be considered in lieu of degree.

Professional Qualifications:

  • Five or more years administering relational databases in production, including SQL Server or Azure SQL.
  • Demonstrated performance tuning on large transactional datasets.
  • Hands-on experience with Azure data services, including pipeline monitoring and failure triage.
  • Troubleshooting synchronization between a source system and a downstream warehouse.
  • Comfort working with source data that is poorly documented, denormalized or hierarchically structured — and the discipline to write down what you learn.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA safeguards as they apply to database and platform administration.
  • Healthcare (EHR or revenue cycle) or financial systems experience preferred.
  • Microsoft Fabric and/or Synapse preferred.
  • Experience supporting a site or entity consolidation — merging, mapping or retiring facility-level data preferred.
  • Infrastructure-as-code or scripted deployment, and source control for database objects preferred.

Competencies:

  • Administers relational database platforms in production — backup and recovery, high availability, capacity and storage planning, patching and upgrades
  • Diagnoses performance problems using execution plans, indexing, statistics and partitioning; establishes baselines rather than reacting to complaints
  • Writes and tunes SQL fluently, and reads code written by others
  • Implements database security: role-based access control, least privilege, encryption, masking, audit logging and periodic access review
  • Safeguards protected health information in accordance with HIPAA at the database and platform layer
  • Monitors data pipelines and integrations (APIs/web services, SFTP/file feeds, middleware), triages failures, and documents re-run and remediation steps
  • Works effectively with poorly documented source systems — infers structure, validates findings with subject-matter experts, and records what is learned
  • Owns platform reliability end to end, including escalation and incident response
  • Applies change control discipline: release readiness, testing coordination, backout planning and deployment standards
  • Treats documentation as a deliverable — runbooks, data lineage, interface and architecture diagrams, knowledge base articles
  • Manage competing priorities with sound judgment, follow-through and appropriate escalation
  • Explains technical constraints, configuration options, access controls and data considerations to technical and non-technical audiences
  • Builds credibility and influences without authority across business owners, super users, clinical and operational staff, InfoSec/Compliance and leadership
  • Manages vendor technical relationships, including holding a vendor to a commitment
  • Transfers knowledge so that no critical procedure depends on one person

Accanto’s Commitment to Equal Opportunity: Accanto is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

What we offer:

Employee Benefits: We understand the importance of a well-rounded benefits package. That’s why we’re dedicated to providing a range of plans to meet your needs.

For full-time employees, we offer:

  • HSA and PPO insurance with HSA or FSA options (Blue Cross Blue Shield)
  • Dental insurance (Delta Dental)
  • Vision insurance (EyeMed)
  • Short-term and long-term disability insurance
  • Company-paid life insurance
  • 401(k) plan available two months after start date
  • Company 401(k) matching for up to 50% of your contribution, up to 6% of your compensation

Paid time off is a crucial part of maintaining work and life balance. Our generous PTO plan accrues annually and begins with your first whole pay period. Eligible employees enjoy seven paid holidays and one floating holiday in addition to their regular PTO.

title: Lab Resource Coordinator-Vivarium
description:
The Opportunity:

In this role, you will report to the Territory Area Manager and will work closely with the Avantor’s Advanced Laboratory Services professionals to serve our customers by performing customized, mission-based lab work and research protocols that help return time back to science.

Location: Cambridge, MA

Shift: Monday – Friday 7:30 am – 4:00 pm

Hourly pay range: $28 - $31

Health & Wellness

  • Wellness programs
  • Eligible for medical coverage starting Day 1

Time Off
